feature.entry: Services/UploadService.php, Services/StorageRouter.php, Services/MediaVariantWriter.php, Services/PosterService.php, Services/ImageOptimizationService.php, src/blocks/media-upload, [mvs_upload] shortcode, REST MediaController upload routes

audit.feature: Upload pipeline (validation, variants, posters, optimization) — free
audit.verdict_reason: The primary upload path (POST /media -> UploadService::handle) is genuinely RIGHT-SIZED and well-built: server-side MIME detection, extension + double-extension blocking, size limits, EXIF/GPS stripping, hash dedup, privacy-aware driver routing, optimization + WebP/AVIF siblings, thumbnail generation with fallbacks, and proper delete cleanup via the orphan-path cascade. But three things drag the feature into MIXED: (1) replace_file is a half-built parallel upload that skips every one of those protections and leaks private bytes to cloud; (2) find_by_hash dedup is site-global and discloses other users' (including private) media IDs to an uploader; (3) the media-upload block + [mvs_upload] shortcode render a silent blank for logged-out / uncapable users and never refresh the page after upload, while the block accepts video but never captures a poster frame the way the FAB modal / BP activity / album uploaders do. So: the main door is solid, but a secondary door (replace) is wide open, one read path leaks, and the most basic surface (block/shortcode) is the least complete.

api.notes: Routes: POST /media (create, cap-checked upload_mvs_media/manage_options + rate limit 30/min) GOOD. POST /media/{id}/replace (update_item_permissions_check) is correctly permissioned but the HANDLER is a defective parallel pipeline (see findings). PUT/DELETE /media/{id} permissioned correctly. The four __return_true routes (GET /media, POST view/download/share, GET access/group) are intentionally public with in-query/in-handler privacy gates and rate limits — triaged and defensible, except POST /media/{id}/view still counts anonymous views by intent (self-noted as v1.3 hardening). Response shape of create_item is consistent with mvs/v1 (prepare_item_for_response) and surfaces duplicate_warning/existing_media_id. replace_file response also uses prepare_item_for_response (consistent) but the underlying data is stale because thumbs/variants were never regenerated. Pagination on GET /media uses the shared Pagination helper. No dead routes found in this feature; quota-check endpoint the block calls (mvs-pro/v1/me/quota/check) is Pro-provided and gracefully 404-skipped.

dataflow.notes: Happy path is clean: handle() -> StorageService::get_driver_for_privacy() -> MediaRepository::insert(mvs_media_index) -> meta (exif, optimization, original_filename) -> extract_and_store_metadata -> generate_thumbnails (via MediaVariantWriter/VariantSpec, single writer) -> init_stats -> fires mvs_before_media_insert / mvs_media_uploaded. Delete cleanup is correct: delete_cascade() collects file_path + every *_path meta and fires mvs_media_files_orphaned -> StorageCleanupService::delete_everywhere across local+cloud; UserDeletionService funnels through the same path. Caching follows the cardinality rule (per-media stats in mvs_media_stats table, not options). GAPS: (1) the staged poster SOURCE file (uploads/wpmediaverse/posters/<id>.<ext> written by PosterService::stage_bytes/stage_client_frame/extract_via_ffmpeg) is never recorded under any *_path meta, so get_stored_file_paths() never collects it and it is orphaned forever on delete — only the sized poster variants are reclaimed. (2) find_by_hash() is site-global with no author scope, used for dedup decisions AND returned to the client. (3) replace_file bypasses the entire service: writes the index row directly, deletes only the old original (orphaning old thumb_*/webp/avif/poster files since it doesn't run delete_cascade), and fires no mvs_media_uploaded hook so gamification/activity/Pro-quota listeners never see the new bytes.

ux.notes: Surfaces exposing upload: (a) media-upload Gutenberg block, (b) [mvs_upload] shortcode (delegates to the block), (c) BP profile/group tab uploader (bp-tab-upload.js), (d) album uploader (album-upload.js), (e) shared-ui FAB upload modal (shared-ui/view.js), (f) BP activity composer (bp-activity-media.js), (g) admin replace-file. The block/shortcode is the weakest: render.php:14-16 bare-returns for logged-out or non-upload-cap users => silent blank page, violating Coding Rule #11 (no silent render fallthrough; render_block_empty_state exists and is unused here). The shortcode inherits that blank with no sign-in CTA even though the dashboard shortcode elsewhere DOES show a logged-out CTA. After a successful upload the block shows a success line but never reloads or refreshes any on-page grid, so the user can't see their new media without a manual refresh (BP tab, album, FAB modal all reload). The block's file input accepts video/mp4+webm but view.js never captures a client poster frame (no canvas/thumbnail FormData append) — only shared-ui, bp-activity-media, and album-upload do — so block/shortcode video uploads get no poster unless server ffmpeg/cover-atom succeeds. BP tab uploader has NO privacy selector (every upload forced to default) and skips preview for non-image files. Mobile/390px: dropzone + privacy select inline styles look fine; privacy select was raised to 44px in 1.4.0 per changelog. No structural overflow risk spotted in the block CSS.

findings.title: replace_file bypasses the entire upload pipeline (no thumbs, no optimization, no EXIF strip, no extension block, no privacy routing, no variant cleanup, no hook)
findings.customer_impact: When a member edits a media item and uploads a replacement file, the site stores the raw new file but keeps showing the OLD thumbnails (they point at the now-deleted original), never generates WebP/AVIF, never strips GPS EXIF, never blocks a dangerous extension, and — worst — always uses the active cloud driver regardless of privacy, so replacing a PRIVATE item pushes private bytes to the public CDN bucket. It also only deletes the old original, leaving the old thumbnails/webp/avif/poster files orphaned, and fires no mvs_media_uploaded hook so quota/activity/gamification never see the change. A customer will report broken thumbnails after Replace, private media leaking to CDN, and stale optimization.

findings.title: Hash-based duplicate detection is site-global and discloses other users' (including private) media IDs to the uploader
findings.customer_impact: find_by_hash() searches the whole mvs_media_index with no author or privacy scope. In 'skip' mode the upload is rejected with a 409 carrying existing_media_id; in 'warn' mode the response carries existing_media_id and the block shows 'Existing media #N already contains this content.' A member who happens to upload a file byte-identical to someone else's PRIVATE upload is told it exists and handed its internal ID — an information-disclosure / enumeration leak across the privacy boundary. Dedup should be scoped to the uploading author (or at minimum never return another user's id).

findings.title: Staged poster source file is never tracked for cleanup — orphaned bytes accumulate forever
findings.customer_impact: Every video/audio poster and client-captured frame writes uploads/wpmediaverse/posters/<id>.<ext> as the thumbnail SOURCE, but that path is never persisted under a *_path meta key. On media delete, get_stored_file_paths() collects only file_path and *_path variants, so the poster source is left on disk (and the sized poster variants are cleaned, but not the source). Over time a busy video community accumulates dead poster files in uploads — storage grows with no way to reclaim it via the normal delete flow.

findings.title: media-upload block and [mvs_upload] shortcode render a silent blank for logged-out / non-upload-cap users
findings.customer_impact: A site owner who drops the Media Upload block or [mvs_upload] on a public page sees a working uploader; a logged-out visitor (or a logged-in user without upload_mvs_media) sees NOTHING — an empty hole on the page with no 'please sign in to upload' message. This violates the plugin's own Rule #11 (no silent render fallthrough; render_block_empty_state() exists and is used elsewhere). Customers report 'my upload form disappeared / shows blank' for non-members.

findings.title: Successful block/shortcode upload never refreshes the page or any media grid
findings.customer_impact: After uploading via the block/shortcode the user gets a green 'N file(s) uploaded successfully' line but the page does not reload and no on-page Media Grid / My Media list updates, so the new media is invisible until a manual refresh. Every other upload surface (BP tab, album, FAB modal) reloads. Users think the upload didn't 'stick' and re-upload, creating duplicates.

findings.title: media-upload block accepts video but never captures a client poster frame
findings.location: src/blocks/media-upload/render.php:83 (accept includes video) vs src/blocks/media-upload/view.js:260-303 (no canvas capture / no 'thumbnail' append)
findings.customer_impact: The block's file picker accepts MP4/WebM, and the create_item endpoint has a ready client-frame poster path (MediaController.php:639-657), but the block JS never captures a first-frame canvas and never sends the 'thumbnail' file — unlike the FAB modal, BP activity composer, and album uploader which all do. So videos uploaded through the block/shortcode show the generic play-icon placeholder unless the server happens to have ffmpeg or the file embeds a cover atom. Inconsistent video experience depending on which upload surface the customer used.

findings.title: BP tab uploader has no privacy selector — every tab upload is forced to the site default
findings.customer_impact: Users uploading from their BuddyPress profile/group media tab cannot choose public/members/private per upload (the block, FAB modal, and edit modal all offer it). Everything lands at mvs_default_privacy. A member who wants a private upload from their profile tab has to upload then edit each item afterward.

findings.title: EXIF GPS-strip re-saves JPEG at quality 95 and PNG with default compression, after the optimization pass would run again separately
findings.customer_impact: When a JPEG carries GPS data, extract_and_strip_exif re-encodes it via GD at a hardcoded quality 95 (not the filterable mvs_optimize_jpeg_quality), then the optimization pass re-encodes again. Double re-encode of GPS-tagged photos means slightly more quality loss and CPU than necessary. Minor, but the hardcoded 95 ignores the customer's configured quality and the lossless guard.

overcooked_items: The four __return_true public routes carry a long inline justification comment block (MediaController.php:60-77) — fine to keep, but record_view counting anonymous views 'by intent' is a self-acknowledged soft spot that has been deferred since 1.3; either gate it behind a session token or drop the anonymous-view ambition rather than leaving a permanently-deferred TODO.

StorageRouter exists largely as a thin delegate to StorageService::get_driver_for_media/get_driver_for_privacy with a comment promising 'Phase 6 will fold the inline checks into this routing' — the inline cloud-eligibility check it was meant to replace still lives in UploadService::generate_thumbnails (line ~864), so the abstraction is half-adopted and currently buys little. Either finish folding the inline checks in or inline StorageRouter back; right now it is a second name for the same decision.
missing_for_complete_solution: Route replace_file through UploadService (or a shared internal method) so a replaced file gets the SAME validation, extension blocking, EXIF strip, privacy-driver routing, optimization, WebP/AVIF, thumbnail regen, old-variant cleanup (delete_cascade), and mvs_media_uploaded firing as a fresh upload. Today Replace is a downgrade.
Scope find_by_hash duplicate detection to the uploading author (and never return another user's media id) so dedup can't disclose private media across users.
Record the staged poster source path (posters/<id>.<ext>) under a *_path meta key (e.g. poster_source_path) so it is reclaimed by the orphan-cleanup cascade on delete.

Give the media-upload block/shortcode a visible empty state for logged-out and non-upload-cap users (a sign-in / 'you cannot upload here' message via render_block_empty_state), matching the dashboard shortcode's logged-out CTA.
Refresh the page or emit a CustomEvent that on-page Media Grid / My Media blocks listen for, after a successful block/shortcode upload, so users see their new media without a manual reload.

Add client-side first-frame poster capture to the media-upload block's view.js (same canvas->blob->'thumbnail' append the FAB modal already does) so block/shortcode video uploads get a poster without depending on server ffmpeg.
Add a per-upload privacy selector to the BP tab uploader so profile/group tab uploads aren't all forced to the site default.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED real, blocker-grade. `replace_file()` (MediaController.php:833-902) is a live, user-facing endpoint: route registered at line 143-158 (POST /media/{id}/replace) and called from the member dashboard edit modal (src/blocks/dashboard-view/view.js:705, "File replaced!" toast). It bypasses the entire upload pipeline that the normal path (`create_item` -> `UploadService::handle()`) runs.

Verified each defect against the canonical pipeline:

1. PRIVACY LEAK TO CDN (the headline claim) — CONFIRMED, blocker. replace_file:864-865 stores via `$storage->get_driver()` (the active/cloud driver) unconditionally. `StorageService::get_driver_for_privacy()` (line 100-102) is, per its own docblock, "the single enforcement point... every write path resolves its driver here instead of calling get_driver() directly, so a private upload can never land on a public cloud bucket." handle() uses it (UploadService:281); replace_file does not. On a site with BunnyCDN/S3 active, replacing a private/members/friends item pushes private bytes to the public CDN bucket. The old-file delete (line 880) likewise only hits the active driver, not StorageService::delete_everywhere().

2. STALE THUMBNAILS — CONFIRMED. replace_file never calls generate_thumbnails(); thumb_* meta is untouched and keeps pointing at the now-deleted original's variant files.

3. ORPHANED VARIANTS — CONFIRMED. Only $old_path (original) is deleted (line 877-881). Old thumb_*/_webp/_avif/poster files are never reclaimed (delete_item uses async mvs_media_files_orphaned cleanup; replace_file uses none of it).

4. NO mvs_media_uploaded HOOK — CONFIRMED. handle() fires it (UploadService:499-516) for quota/gamification/activity consumers; replace_file fires nothing.

5. NO OPTIMIZATION / WebP / AVIF — CONFIRMED (handle() at UploadService:246-258, 300-329; absent in replace_file).

6. NO EXIF/GPS STRIP — CONFIRMED. handle() strips GPS via extract_and_strip_exif() (UploadService:146-149, default-on mvs_strip_exif); replace_file does not.

7. NO EXTENSION BLOCK — partially confirmed. handle() has an explicit dangerous-extension blocklist incl. double-extension image.php.jpg (UploadService:155-176); replace_file relies only on a finfo MIME sniff (line 855-861). The MIME sniff reduces the practical webshell risk (content must sniff as an allowed image/video/audio type), so this sub-claim is the weakest, but the extension-block step is genuinely absent.

Severity stays blocker: the private-media-to-public-CDN leak is the same data-exposure class the team treats as release-blocking (card 9925110293), and CLAUDE.md Coding Rule 18 (added 2026-06-04) makes REST a mandatory first-class surface because a native mobile app is planned — so this is not a dead/secondary endpoint. No gate, filter, or consumer elsewhere mitigates it.

Relevant files: includes/REST/Controller/MediaController.php:833-902 (replace_file) and :596+ (create_item, the correct pattern); includes/Services/UploadService.php:146-176, 246-281, 499-516 (the full pipeline replace_file skips); includes/Services/StorageService.php:100-116 (get_driver_for_privacy enforcement point); src/blocks/dashboard-view/view.js:695-724 (live caller).

verified.title: Hash-based duplicate detection is site-global and discloses other users' (including private) media IDs to the uploader
verified.customer_impact: find_by_hash() searches the whole mvs_media_index with no author or privacy scope. In 'skip' mode the upload is rejected with a 409 carrying existing_media_id; in 'warn' mode the response carries existing_media_id and the block shows 'Existing media #N already contains this content.' A member who happens to upload a file byte-identical to someone else's PRIVATE upload is told it exists and handed its internal ID — an information-disclosure / enumeration leak across the privacy boundary. Dedup should be scoped to the uploading author (or at minimum never return another user's id).

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED in code, end to end. find_by_hash() (UploadService.php:1192-1203) runs `SELECT media_id FROM mvs_media_index WHERE file_hash = %s LIMIT 1` with NO user_id and NO privacy filter — it is site-global. The mvs_media_index schema (Migrator.php:287-319) carries both a user_id column and a privacy column (default 'public', also storing private/restricted/group rows), so a hash match can return media owned by another user, including private media. The disclosure reaches the uploader on both code paths: (1) skip mode returns a 409 WP_Error carrying existing_media_id (UploadService.php:130-138); (2) warn mode records the ID (line 142) and MediaController.php:712-716 attaches existing_media_id + duplicate_warning to the 201 response. The front-end then renders the literal internal ID to the uploader — media-upload/view.js:315 ("Existing media #${lastDuplicateId} already contains this content.") and shared-ui/view.js:949 ("existing media #' + state.uploadModalLastDuplicateId"). No author/privacy scope exists anywhere in the path, and nothing in audit/, qa/, or CLAUDE.md documents this as intentional. So the cross-privacy enumeration leak the finding describes is real.

Severity corrected high -> medium. The leak is genuine but bounded: it is an existence-oracle plus an opaque internal media ID, not content disclosure or access bypass. The attacker must already possess the exact file bytes to trigger a match (so they learn nothing about the file's content — they have it), and the leaked integer ID does not itself grant access: the /serve and view paths re-check can_view per request (the 1.4.0/1.5.0 privacy hardening), so the disclosed ID cannot be used to fetch the private media. The materialized harm is therefore "a private upload with these exact bytes exists on this site, internal id N" — an information-disclosure / enumeration leak across the privacy boundary, but with no private-content exposure and no access-control bypass. That is a medium info-leak, not a high. The recommended fix (scope find_by_hash to the uploading author, or at minimum never return another user's id) remains correct.

verified.title: media-upload block and [mvs_upload] shortcode render a silent blank for logged-out / non-upload-cap users
verified.customer_impact: A site owner who drops the Media Upload block or [mvs_upload] on a public page sees a working uploader; a logged-out visitor (or a logged-in user without upload_mvs_media) sees NOTHING — an empty hole on the page with no 'please sign in to upload' message. This violates the plugin's own Rule #11 (no silent render fallthrough; render_block_empty_state() exists and is used elsewhere). Customers report 'my upload form disappeared / shows blank' for non-members.

verdict.reason:
PARTIALLY REAL but mis-rated and built on a false premise. Confirmed: src/blocks/media-upload/render.php:14-16 (and the identical shipped build/blocks/media-upload/render.php) does `if ( ! is_user_logged_in() || ! current_user_can( 'upload_mvs_media' ) ) { return; }` with no visible output, and [mvs_upload] (Shortcodes.php:104-133) routes through that same template. So a logged-out visitor on a page with this block/shortcode genuinely sees a blank region rather than a "please sign in to upload" prompt. That UX gap is real.

BUT the finding's justifying claims are false:
1. It asserts `render_block_empty_state()` "exists and is used elsewhere." It does NOT exist anywhere in includes/, src/, or build/ (grep returns zero hits). RENDER-STATE-RULES.md section 3 describes it as a helper "to add" — aspirational, never implemented. The CI enforcement it cites (bin/empty-state-baseline.txt, bin/empty-state-audit.sh) also does not exist. Rule #11 is an unenforced aspiration here, not a contract this block uniquely breaks.
2. The finding implies media-upload uniquely deviates from a pattern other blocks follow. False: sibling blocks do the IDENTICAL bare logged-out return — media-stats/render.php:16-17 (`if ( ! is_user_logged_in() ) { return; }`) and story-viewer/render.php:46-47. The silent logged-out return is the prevailing pattern across the block suite, not an anomaly.
3. This is documented, tracked baseline tech debt, not an undiscovered violation: RENDER-STATE-RULES.md section 4 explicitly lists media-upload's return as "Review — may be cap-gated; if so, render 'Log in to upload' gate," targeted (and never shipped) for 1.1.3.

Severity correction high->low: the impact is a missing courtesy message for logged-out viewers, not a broken feature, data loss, or security hole. By default every standard WP role (subscriber..admin) is granted upload_mvs_media (MediaCapabilities::get_role_caps()), so the "logged-in user without cap" scenario only occurs on custom-role sites; the realistic case is logged-out visitors seeing a blank instead of a sign-in nudge. Real, but a low-priority documented UX nit — not high.

audit.feature: Storage & serving (drivers, signed URLs, /serve, MediaUrl) — wpmediaverse free
audit.verdict_reason: The core serve pipeline is genuinely well-engineered and complete: HMAC-signed /serve with per-request privacy re-checks for restricted media, range/206 streaming with Content-Length correctness, AVIF/WebP negotiation, traversal containment on every disk read, driver-agnostic location-based display, public-cloud direct-CDN bypass, and a proper async cross-driver delete cleanup cycle (StorageCleanupService + delete_everywhere + get_stored_file_paths) wired to both REST delete and account deletion. That is RIGHT-SIZED-to-strong. But two axes drag it to MIXED: (1) API has a fully dead surface — the entire download path (REST /media/{id}/signed-url `download` arg, SignedUrlService download-disposition serve branch, record_download(), and the mvs_dl param) has ZERO callers in free or pro; downloads are handled entirely client-side via the inline file_url. And the /media/{id}/signed-url route itself has no frontend consumer at all. (2) read-side watermark serve wiring (watermark_url meta + size=watermark serve branch) has no writer, so it can only ever 404. Plus schema/dead-code rough edges. Nothing here LEAKS or dead-ends for a customer on the happy path, but there is meaningful overcooked dead surface and one incomplete (watermark) read path.

api.notes: Two REST routes in mvs/v1: GET /media/{id}/signed-url (logged-in + exists + can_view permission_callback, rate-limited 60/60, returns {media_id, signed_url, expires_in, download}) and GET /serve (permission __return_true — intentional, HMAC is the credential, documented + triaged). /serve permission is correct (S3-presigned-URL analogue). validate() correctly uses isset not empty (handles uid=0), checks expiry, hash_equals on HMAC-SHA256. BUT: (a) /media/{id}/signed-url has NO frontend consumer anywhere (all signed URLs are minted server-side in render.php via the container) — dead API route. (b) The `download` capability is 100% dead: no caller in free OR pro ever passes download=true to generate() or sets mvs_dl; the download-disposition branch in serve(), record_download(), the mvs_media_views download-event insert, and the `download` REST arg are all unreachable. (c) mvs_size (PARAM_SIZE) is read in serve_file() but never declared in the /serve route args schema — works because WP passes unregistered query params through and it is HMAC-bound, but it is a schema inconsistency. (d) get_signed_url returns the absint-sanitized media_id which is fine; response shape is a flat array (consistent enough with the rest of mvs/v1).

dataflow.notes: Strong. Delete cleanup is now complete: delete_cascade() reads get_stored_file_paths() (original file_path + every *_path variant meta) and fires mvs_media_files_orphaned BEFORE deleting meta; StorageCleanupService (registered + init() called at Plugin.php:203) enqueues via Action Scheduler (inline fallback) and calls delete_everywhere() which deletes from BOTH local and active cloud driver — closes the previous orphaned-bytes gap on both REST delete and account deletion. Privacy gate is applied at every read path: serve() re-checks can_view per-request for non-public media (signed-URL-as-bearer-token gap closed), public_cloud_direct_allowed() requires privacy=public AND no active access rules before emitting any direct CDN URL, get_driver_for_privacy() keeps all non-public bytes local-only. Privacy-change listener (mvs_media_privacy_changed -> sync_urls_on_privacy_change -> relocalize_media_urls) re-points cloud URL meta to local on public->restricted escalation. Caching is correct per cardinality rule: signing secret + TTL are single global options (≤50 keys), no per-entity transients, per-request reuse via container singletons. Storage secret auto-generated with autoload=false. One inherent (documented) residual: a media that WAS public-on-CDN stays publicly fetchable at the raw CDN URL after going private — relocalize rewrites meta but does not delete/re-ACL the cloud object.

ux.notes: Serve is consumed by media-player, pdf-viewer, story-viewer, media-grid render.php (all mint server-side via container->get('signed_urls')) and via MediaUrl::thumb()/file() facade and MediaRepository sign helpers — broad coverage across blocks, BP tabs, single template, lightbox. Lightbox download button is gated on the mvs_allow_downloads global + per-media allow_download flag, has an empty-state toast ('This media is not available for download.'), and posts to /media/{id}/download for stats. findings.title: Entire download path is dead code (REST download arg, serve mvs_dl branch, record_download, download view-event)
findings.customer_impact: No customer-visible breakage, but a paying customer who reads the docs/API and expects the signed-URL `download` flag to produce a real Content-Disposition: attachment download will find it does nothing — the lightbox download just reuses the inline file_url and relies on the browser `download` attribute. Downloads of public-on-CDN media never increment the signed-URL download counter (a separate /download endpoint handles stats). The dead branch is maintenance surface that looks load-bearing but isn't.
findings.detail: No caller in free or pro passes download=true to generate() or sets mvs_dl. The download-disposition serve branch, record_download(), and the mvs_media_views download-event row are unreachable. lightboxDownload() in src/blocks/shared-ui/view.js:1293 uses data.file_url (inline disposition) + a.download attr, and POSTs to media/{id}/download for the stat.

findings.title: REST GET /media/{id}/signed-url has no frontend consumer
findings.customer_impact: Customers building a headless/JS integration may assume this is the intended way to obtain a playable URL, but the product itself never calls it (all signed URLs are minted server-side in render.php). It is a correct, secured endpoint with no internal user — either document it as a public integration seam or drop it. No breakage today.
findings.detail: grep across src/ and assets/ (free + pro) finds zero fetch/apiFetch of media/{id}/signed-url. All consumers go through the container SignedUrlService directly or MediaUrl/MediaRepository helpers.

findings.title: Watermark serve path (size=watermark) has a reader but no writer
findings.customer_impact: On a Pro site using watermarks, any code path that mints a size=watermark signed URL or reads watermark_url meta will 404 (the docblock says 'fall back to lock-overlay') because nothing writes watermark_url meta. Pro customers expecting a watermarked-preview served via /serve get the lock overlay instead of the watermarked image. Functionally the lock fallback is graceful, but the watermark-preview-via-serve feature is incomplete.
findings.detail: serve_thumbnail() handles size=watermark by reading watermark_url meta; MediaRepository::get('watermark_url') signs it. But grep finds no writer of watermark_url in free or pro (only tests set it). Pro Watermarker writes wpmediaverse/previews/{id}-preview.jpg per the docblock, with no meta linkage. Cross-boundary; flagged for Pro follow-up.

findings.title: mvs_size param read by /serve but not declared in route args schema
findings.customer_impact: No customer impact and no security hole (the size is HMAC-bound in the signature and sanitize_text_field'd before use). It is a self-documentation/schema-consistency gap that makes the route harder to introspect via the REST schema and slightly inconsistent with the rest of mvs/v1's args declarations.
findings.detail: serve_file() reads SignedUrlService::PARAM_SIZE but the register_rest_route args only declare MEDIA_ID, USER, EXPIRES, SIGNATURE, DOWNLOAD. Works because WP forwards unregistered query params.

audit.feature: Explore feed (grid, search, tags/categories, load more) — free
audit.verdict_reason: There are TWO parallel Explore implementations that have drifted apart. The primary `/media/` archive path (templates/explore.php + MediaController REST + load-more.js + card-builders.js) is RIGHT-SIZED and correctly privacy-gated. But the second surface — the `mvs/explore-feed` Gutenberg block AND the `[mvs_explore_feed]` shortcode, which share src/blocks/explore-feed/render.php — bypasses MediaRepository and PrivacyService entirely and queries `WHERE status='publish'` with NO privacy filter and NO moderation filter. That is a blocker-class leak of private/friends/group and pending/rejected media to everyone, including logged-out visitors. It is the exact "fix landed on one surface, missed the others" class the cycle is chasing (the 1.6.0 profile-listing members-leak fix #9941246549 was applied to MediaRepository, which the block render never calls). Its Load More also drops video/audio and serves full-res file URLs. The feature is complete and dependable on one surface and broken/leaking on the other.

api.notes: Routes: GET mvs/v1/media (list — used by load-more.js + explore-feed block view.js + explore-search suggestions), GET mvs/v1/tags/cloud (tag cloud, used by explore-view view.js), GET mvs/v1/tags (autocomplete), GET mvs/v1/users (people search, used by explore-search.js). All four are permission_callback __return_true but legitimately public: get_items enforces privacy IN the SQL (anon -> privacy='public'; logged-in non-moderator -> public+members+own; moderator -> any) at MediaController.php:308-314, and rate-limits 120/min (line 273). tags/cloud + tags are public taxonomy terms (no PII), same surface as wp/v2/tags. The triage comments at MediaController.php:60-77 and TagController.php:34-38 document this intentionally. Pagination headers are honest: X-WP-Total + X-WP-TotalPages set from the same WHERE as the data query (MediaController.php:509-510). Search uses FULLTEXT-or-LIKE with a real index (line 356-367). Pro extends cleanly via mvs_feed_media_ids / mvs_feed_query_args filters (BoostService consumes mvs_feed_media_ids). NOTE: the explore-feed block's own loadMore (view.js) does NOT pass scope=public, so for a logged-in non-moderator it returns public+members+own (acceptable), but combined with the block's leaking initial render the net effect is still a leak on that surface (see dataflow). No dead routes; no broken wiring on the REST side.

dataflow.notes: The archive path is clean: explore.php -> MediaRepository::query()/query_count() -> build_privacy_where() (correct per-mode gating, with the 1.6.0 'profile' mode and mvs_profile_privacy_levels filter) -> TemplateHelpers::render_grid_item -> bulk_get_stats. Privacy is gated at the read path. BUT src/blocks/explore-feed/render.php:26-36 is a second, independent read path that goes straight to `$wpdb` with `SELECT * FROM mvs_media_index WHERE status='publish'` — no `privacy` predicate, no `moderation_status='approved'` predicate, no viewer scoping, no blocked-user exclusion. It does not call MediaRepository or PrivacyService at all, so none of the 1.6.0 privacy fixes reach it. This is the same leak class flagged for BP tabs/activity, but total (private/friends/group/custom + unmoderated all rendered). It also means Pro's mvs_feed_media_ids boosting and the mvs_feed_query_args filter never apply to the block's initial render (extensibility hooks silently skipped on this surface). Caching follows the cardinality rule (stats via bulk_get_stats, per-entity in tables, not options). Tag/category filters resolve slug->term_taxonomy_id and fail-closed to an empty state on unknown slugs (explore.php:224-243) — good. No write path here so delete-cleanup is N/A.

ux.notes: Surfaces exposing this feature: (1) /media/ archive + tag/category archives + profile feed via templates/explore.php; (2) mvs/explore-feed Gutenberg block; (3) [mvs_explore_feed] shortcode (shares render.php with the block); (4) explore-view tag cloud (Interactivity API). Surface 1 is end-to-end wired with rich empty states (no-media, no-search-results, tag-not-found, category-not-found — each with Browse-all CTA + popular tags), a logged-out join banner, mobile 44px tap targets per the 1.4.0 mobile pass, and correct Load More (load-more.js + per-layout card-builders.js, registry rebuild for lightbox). Surface 2/3 is a DIFFERENT, thinner implementation: its Load More (view.js:172-196) only renders items where file_type starts with 'image/' — video and audio items are appended as EMPTY divs (no else branch), and it uses item.file_url (full-resolution / possibly gated) instead of thumbnail_url, unlike card-builders.js. Its only empty state is a bare 'No media items found' line. Two surfaces with the same name produce visibly different cards, different Load More behavior, and different privacy posture — the core drift problem. The explore-view tag cloud and explore-search people-toggle are solid. Mobile structural risk: the block grid uses mvs-cols-N with no @media fallback visible in its style.css scope (the archive grid is covered by frontend.css); a 5-column block at 390px is an overflow risk.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED REAL — blocker. The explore-feed block render path leaks private and unmoderated media to all visitors on initial server render.

Evidence:
1. src/blocks/explore-feed/render.php:26-36 (and identical compiled copy build/blocks/explore-feed/render.php:28,35) run: SELECT * FROM mvs_media_index WHERE status='publish' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT %d — with NO privacy and NO moderation_status predicate, and no get_current_user_id()/can_view() gate. It executes for every visitor including logged-out ones.

2. Schema proves status != privacy != moderation. Migrator.php:293-296 defines three independent columns: status (publish/draft/scheduled/trash), privacy (public/private/members/friends/custom), moderation_status (approved/pending/rejected). Filtering only on status='publish' does not constrain the other two.

3. The leak materializes. UploadService.php:336,368-369 stores every non-draft upload with status='publish' regardless of the user's chosen privacy (kept in the separate privacy column). A Private upload is status='publish', privacy='private' and matches the leaky WHERE — so its thumbnail, title, and permalink are rendered in full.

4. Divergence proves it is a bug, not intent. The same feed's load-more consumer, REST mvs/v1/media get_items (MediaController.php:304-314), enforces moderation_status='approved' AND a privacy WHERE (privacy='public' for anon; public/members/own for logged-in non-moderators). The canonical MediaRepository::build_query_parts()/build_privacy_where() (MediaRepository.php:1320-1361, 1399+) is documented as the single source of truth for the privacy WHERE fragment 'previously copy-pasted across explore + 3 Pro feed templates.' The block render path calls none of it.

5. The [mvs_explore_feed] shortcode shares the leak: Shortcodes.php:256 render_block_template('explore-feed',...) loads build/blocks/explore-feed/render.php (Shortcodes.php:485), the same vulnerable query.

Impact: the first page (default 12 items) of Private/Friends/Group/Custom-privacy media — and any Pending/Rejected items — is disclosed in full to unauthenticated visitors anywhere a site owner places the block or shortcode. Same leak class as the 1.6.0 MediaRepository privacy-WHERE centralization, which this render path bypasses. Severity blocker/dataflow is correct.

verified.title: Two divergent Explore implementations with no shared core
verified.customer_impact: The /media/ archive and the Explore block/shortcode are entirely separate code paths with different privacy gating, different card markup, and different Load More mechanics. Bug fixes and privacy hardening applied to one (the archive, via MediaRepository) never reach the other. Customers see inconsistent behavior depending on which Explore surface they land on, and the team has to fix everything twice. The block render should delegate to MediaRepository::query() with the same privacy/viewer scoping the archive uses.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED in code, and the divergence is actually worse than the finding states.

Three independent query paths exist for the same "Explore" feature, none sharing a privacy core:

1. Archive SSR (templates/explore.php:182-289) — routes through MediaRepository::query() with status='publish', moderation_status='approved', privacy scoping by viewer (anon->'public', logged-in non-mod->'visible' = public/members/own, mod->'any'), exclude_non_cover_group, and the mvs_explore_query_args filter. Load More on this surface uses a vanilla-JS script (assets/js/frontend/load-more.js) driven by data-* attributes (data-endpoint="media", data-scope="public", data-group-covers="true").

2. Block/shortcode SSR (src/blocks/explore-feed/render.php:26-36) — hand-rolled $wpdb->get_results with ONLY "WHERE status = 'publish'". No privacy filter, no moderation_status filter, no group-cover exclusion, no filter hook. The block is also the shortcode backend (Shortcodes.php:256), so this is a real second customer-facing surface. Load More here is a completely different mechanism: the Interactivity API store mvs/explore-feed (src/blocks/explore-feed/view.js) building DOM nodes manually.

3. REST MediaController::get_items() (includes/REST/Controller/MediaController.php:271-374) — a THIRD, inline privacy/moderation implementation ($where/$params built by hand: moderation_status='approved', anon->public, logged-in non-mod->public OR members OR own, plus scope/blocked-user/group-cover handling) that both Load More paths converge on but that duplicates rather than reuses MediaRepository's build_privacy_where().

The claimed customer impact materializes concretely and includes a privacy leak the finding only implied: because render.php filters on status alone, the explore-feed block/shortcode renders private and members-only media — and unmoderated/rejected media (no moderation_status gate) — to anonymous visitors on its initial server-side render. The archive surface (MediaRepository) does NOT leak this way. The team also recently hardened profile/listing privacy in MediaRepository (build_privacy_where 'profile' mode, Basecamp #9941246549, mvs_profile_privacy_levels filter, since 1.6.0) and that hardening never reaches the block's SSR. Markup also diverges (render.php emits bare img+overlay; explore.php delegates to TemplateHelpers::render_grid_item with author/stats), so fixes land on one surface only. No docblock, CLAUDE.md rule, or audit report documents this as intentional — to the contrary, CLAUDE.md Rule 14 (sibling dedup) and the MediaRepository "single source of truth" framing argue the block SSR should delegate to MediaRepository::query() with viewer scoping, exactly as the finding recommends.

Severity high is correct, arguably under-rated given the anonymous-visibility leak of private/members-only/unmoderated content via the block; treating it as high/dataflow is appropriate.

verified.title: Explore block Load More silently drops video and audio and serves full-res images
verified.customer_impact: On the block/shortcode surface, clicking Load More only appends items whose file_type starts with 'image/'. Video and audio results are appended as empty grid cells (no else branch), so on a video/audio-heavy community Load More appears to add blank tiles or nothing. It also uses item.file_url (the original file, which can be large or access-gated) instead of thumbnail_url, unlike the archive's card-builders.js. Customers report 'Load More is broken / shows blanks' on pages using the shortcode.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED REAL. The explore-feed block's loadMore (src/blocks/explore-feed/view.js:172-196) unconditionally creates and appends a `div.mvs-grid-item` (line 173-174, 194) but only fills it when `fileUrl && fileType.startsWith('image/')` (line 178). There is no else branch, so video and audio results append as empty grid cells. Verified that the REST endpoint actually returns mixed types: MediaController returns media_type with enum [image,video,audio,document] (line 1474-1476) and the media_type filter is OPTIONAL (line 316) — the default explore feed (filter='') returns video/audio items, so they WILL hit loadMore and render blank.

Also confirmed the second claim: line 178-180 sets img.src = item.file_url (the original file). MediaController exposes file_url and thumbnail_url as DISTINCT fields (lines 1321 vs 1336; thumbnail_url = thumb_large/poster, file_url = original). Both correct surfaces use the thumbnail: server-side initial render calls render_grid_thumbnail -> media_thumbnail (render.php) and the sibling archive builder assets/js/frontend/card-builders.js (buildMediaThumbnail) prefers thumbnail_url and has full video/audio/poster/placeholder handling. This view.js loadMore is the lone surface that diverges — serving full-res originals (perf hit, and access-gated for non-public media) and dropping non-image types.

Strong corroboration: CLAUDE.md coding Rule 18 (added 2026-06-04) explicitly names "Load More" among the 2026-06 bug class "where a fix lands on one surface and misses the others." No gate, filter, or intentional-behavior docblock excuses this. The customer impact (blank tiles on video/audio communities, full-res images on Load More) materializes as described.

api.notes: Routes consumed by the single page: POST /media/{id}/view (record_view, __return_true with rate-limit + privacy gate — correct for anonymous view counting), GET /media/{id}/reactions + POST/DELETE, GET /media/{id}/comments + POST/PUT/DELETE, /media/{id}/favorite, /users/{id}/follow, /me/favorites, /me/following, /media/{id}/stats, PUT/DELETE /media/{id}, POST /media/{id}/report. Permission_callbacks on write paths are correct (create/update/delete checks). TWO read routes are public (__return_true) and DO NOT apply the privacy gate: GET /media/{id}/comments (CommentController::get_items, includes/REST/Controller/CommentController.php:175) and GET /media/{id}/reactions (ReactionController::get_items, includes/REST/Controller/ReactionController.php:121). DEAD/UNWIRED-FROM-THIS-SURFACE: POST /media/{id}/share and POST /media/{id}/download exist and increment share/download stats, but the single page never calls them — only the shared-ui lightbox (src/blocks/shared-ui/view.js:1276,1321) does. So share + download stats are recorded from the grid lightbox but never from the single page, an inconsistent-surface gap. Response shapes are consistent with mvs/v1; pagination headers (X-WP-Total/TotalPages) present on comments. record_view inserts user_id null with %d format placeholder (includes/REST/Controller/MediaController.php:983,988) — harmless in practice but technically a type mismatch for anonymous rows.

dataflow.notes: Read path: TemplateLoader::serve_single_media looks up mvs_media_index by slug/id (status=publish), applies can_view, sets $GLOBALS, registers OG/Twitter meta + document title, includes media-single.php. URLs route through MediaUrl::file()/SignedUrlService (correct choke point). Privacy gate is applied at BOTH the TemplateLoader read path AND duplicated inside the template (templates/media-single.php:42-66) — the in-template gate is now dead because TemplateLoader already 404s non-viewable media before include; harmless redundancy. Delete cascade (MediaRepository delete, includes/Repository/MediaRepository.php:2089-2101) is thorough: stats, views, meta, reactions, favorites, mentions, album_items, notifications, activity, access_rules, access_grants, comments, index — and fires mvs_media_files_orphaned for byte cleanup. GAP: mvs_reports is NOT deleted on media deletion (no DELETE against mvs_reports anywhere) — reports referencing a deleted media_id are orphaned and can surface stale rows in the moderation queue. DOUBLE-COUNT: on a video/audio single page, BOTH the media-player wrapper (data-wp-init=actions.trackView, templates/media-single.php:224,251 -> player view.js trackView POSTs /view) AND the media-social wrapper callbacks.init (src/blocks/media-social/view.js:670) POST /media/{id}/view on the same page load — so every video/audio view is counted twice, while images count once. View counts are inflated ~2x for AV media and inconsistent across media types. Caching/cardinality looks correct (per-media stats live in mvs_media_stats table, not options/transients).

ux.notes: Surfaces for this feature: the /media/{slug}/ single page template (primary), plus the media-player / pdf-viewer / story-viewer / media-stats blocks (separate Gutenberg surfaces). The single page renders ONLY image/video/audio (templates/media-single.php:68-70 + 178-260). A 'document' media item (PDF — get_media_type returns 'document', UploadService.php:598) produces a single page with NO viewer, NO download, NO inline content — just header + (optional) description + social bar. Dead end. The dedicated pdf-viewer block (src/blocks/pdf-viewer/render.php) is NEVER referenced by the single template, so PDFs the plugin accepts have no first-class single-page experience. No DOWNLOAD button anywhere on the single page even for images/AV, although the /download endpoint + global mvs_allow_downloads + per-media allow_download opt-out all exist and the lightbox exposes download — customers who enable downloads will expect a download button on the single page and won't find one. Empty states: logged-out users correctly get login-prompt favorite + 'Log in to comment'. Share button works (Web Share + clipboard) but never records a share stat from this surface. RE-INTRODUCED BUG: the template removed the leading link emoji from the Share label to stop a double-icon next to the lucide share-2 SVG (card #6, templates/media-single.php shareLabel comment), but handleShare's setTimeout resets shareLabel to a link-emoji + 'Share' (src/blocks/media-social/view.js:382 and build/blocks/media-social/view.js) — so 2s after any share the emoji reappears beside the SVG icon, recreating the double-icon. Responsive: video box locks aspect-ratio (good); story-viewer uses heavy inline styles with a hardcoded #0073aa avatar ring and inline color hex (drifts from design tokens) but story-viewer is not part of the single page. Initial per-viewer state (reported/favorited) is correctly hydrated server-side to avoid fl. Owner correctly cannot favorite/report own media.

findings.title: GET /media/{id}/comments has no privacy gate — comments on members/private media leak to anonymous callers
findings.customer_impact: Anyone (logged out) can read every comment on a members-only or private media item by hitting the public REST route directly, even though the single page itself is gated. Same class of members-level leak the team just fixed on BP tabs/activity. A customer running a private community will consider this a privacy breach.

findings.title: GET /media/{id}/reactions has no privacy gate — reaction data on non-public media is public
findings.customer_impact: Reaction counts (and, for a logged-in third party, existence) for members-only/private media are readable by any anonymous caller via the public route. StatsController gates the same kind of read but reactions does not — inconsistent and leaks engagement data on content that should be hidden.

findings.title: Video/audio views are double-counted on the single page
findings.customer_impact: Every load of a video or audio single page records TWO views (player wrapper trackView + social wrapper init both POST /view), while images record one. Customers' analytics and 'Top Media' dashboards over-report AV views ~2x and treat media types inconsistently — the numbers they show their members are wrong.

findings.title: No download button on the single page despite a working download endpoint + settings
findings.customer_impact: There is no way to download media from its own single page, even when the admin enabled the global 'Allow downloads' setting and the per-media owner opt-in. The /media/{id}/download endpoint and stats exist and the grid lightbox has a download button, so customers reasonably expect one here too. Download stats are therefore never recorded from the most-shared URL of the item.

findings.title: Document/PDF media renders a blank single page (no viewer, no download)
findings.customer_impact: If an admin re-enables application/pdf uploads (or any non-AV/non-image type), the resulting /media/{slug}/ page shows only a header and description — no PDF viewer, no file link, no download. The plugin ships a full pdf-viewer block but never wires it into the single page. A paying customer who uploads a PDF lands on a dead-end page and opens a support ticket.

findings.title: Share label re-introduces the double-icon bug fixed in card #6
findings.customer_impact: The template deliberately dropped the leading link emoji from the Share button so it wouldn't render two icons next to the lucide share-2 SVG. But after a user shares, the JS timer resets the label to 'link-emoji + Share', so the double icon comes back 2 seconds later. Looks broken/unpolished on the most visible action button.

findings.title: mvs_reports rows are not cleaned up when media is deleted
findings.customer_impact: Deleting a media item leaves its abuse reports orphaned in mvs_reports (every other related table is cleaned). Moderators can see reports pointing at content that no longer exists, and report counts stay inflated.

findings.title: Dead in-template privacy gate duplicates TemplateLoader's gate
findings.customer_impact: No customer impact today, but the privacy logic is implemented twice (TemplateLoader::can_view_media and again inline in the template). The two can drift; a future change to one and not the other could reopen a leak. Should be one source of truth.

findings.title: OG image is generated for non-public media but 403s at serve time for the scraper
findings.customer_impact: For members-only/private items, the og:image URL is minted with uid=0 + skip_privacy=true, but the /serve route re-checks can_view for non-public media and denies the anonymous scraper — so the social card shows title/description with a broken/missing image. Either intended (title-only card) or should fall back to a generic placeholder; today it's a silently broken preview image.

overcooked_items: Duplicate privacy gate inside templates/media-single.php (lines 42-66) — TemplateLoader already 404s non-viewable media before the include, so this block never fires; remove it and keep the gate in one place (TemplateLoader::can_view_media).

Three-tier tag resolution fallback in the template (JSON meta -> mvs_tag_id meta -> get_the_terms term relationships, lines ~280-330) is a lot of legacy-format branching in a template file; this belongs behind a single repository method, not inline in media-single.php.
missing_for_complete_solution: A download button on the single page, gated by mvs_allow_downloads (global) + per-media allow_download, that POSTs to /media/{id}/download so download stats are recorded consistently with the lightbox.
A viewer for 'document' media (PDF) on the single page — either embed the existing pdf-viewer iframe path or at minimum show a file card with a download/open link, so non-AV media is not a dead end.
Privacy gate (can_view) on the public GET comments and GET reactions routes, matching StatsController, to stop members/private engagement data leaking via direct API.
De-duplicate view recording on the single page so each visit counts exactly one view regardless of media type (image vs video vs audio).
Cleanup of mvs_reports in the media delete cascade so deleting media doesn't orphan its abuse reports.
Fix the Share button label reset so it never re-adds the emoji next to the lucide icon (keep plain 'Share').

feature.name: Albums & Collections (CPTs, album viewer, Pro multi-collection bridge)
feature.entry: Services/AlbumService.php, Services/CollectionService.php, REST AlbumController + CollectionController + BulkController, src/blocks/album-viewer, mvs_collection_media_ids filter, PRO Collections/ + mvs_pro_collection_items table

audit.feature: Albums & Collections (CPTs, album viewer, Pro multi-collection bridge)
audit.verdict_reason: The REST API surface for albums and collections is well-built, consistent, rate-limited, and correctly gated. But the non-REST READ surfaces for albums (single-album page template, album-viewer block, and the [mvs_album] shortcode — all three share the gateless album-viewer render path) have NO album-level privacy gate, so a members-only or private album leaks its title, description, item count, categories, author, and the full list of item titles/permalinks to anyone who hits the album, including logged-out visitors. This is exactly the members-level read-path leak class this cycle was meant to close, replicated across three album surfaces. Separately, deletion cleanup is incomplete: deleting an album or collection from WP admin (not via REST) orphans mvs_album_items / pinned-cover meta, deleting a user never removes their albums/collections, and the Pro mvs_pro_collection_items table is never purged when a collection is deleted (only on media delete). The feature is mostly right-sized in complexity, but these privacy and cleanup gaps make it not dependable for a paying customer who relies on private albums.

api.notes: Album routes (AlbumController.php:68-213): list/get/create/update/delete + reorder + items add/remove + cover. All write routes carry real permission_callbacks (owner-or-edit_others). GET /albums and GET /albums/{id} use __return_true but enforce privacy in the handler (privacy->can_view at AlbumController.php:253 and :279) — correct and triaged. Collection routes (CollectionController.php:59-132): list/get/create/update/delete + rules. get_items requires login; get_item is public for published collections by design (CollectionController.php:336). Bulk route (BulkController.php:42) gates on edit_mvs_medias and re-filters to owned IDs (filter_allowed_ids, BulkController.php:253). Pro multi-collection route (CollectionItemsController.php:54) gates on login + verifies collection ownership on write (CollectionItemsController.php:154). Response shapes consistent with mvs/v1; X-WP-Total/TotalPages headers honest (AlbumController.php:260, CollectionController.php:164). Minor: bulk 'privacy' param has no enum validation (BulkController.php:65) — an arbitrary string is written straight to media_repository->set (BulkController.php:232); a bad value yields a privacy level can_view treats as deny-all (default: return false), effectively hiding media with no error surfaced. Minor: reorder_items has no rate limiter (AlbumController.php:416) while sibling writes do.

dataflow.notes: Entry->service->table is clean for the happy path. Album items live in mvs_album_items; AlbumService::add_items writes album_id back onto each media (AlbumService.php:232) and fires mvs_album_items_added (AlbumService.php:255). Media-delete cleanup is good on the media-as-item side: MediaRepository::delete_cascade clears mvs_album_items (MediaRepository.php:2095), BulkController::bulk_delete clears it inline (BulkController.php:149), and Pro purges mvs_pro_collection_items on mvs_media_deleted (Pro Plugin.php:220). bulk_change_privacy correctly routes through MediaRepository::set so mvs_media_privacy_changed fires (MediaRepository.php:622) and BP activity privacy stays in sync. GAPS: (1) Deleting an album/collection CPT from WP admin runs no cleanup — only the REST delete_item handlers clean up (AlbumController.php:396-399 deletes items + term rels; CollectionController.php:280 nullifies mvs_favorites.collection_id). No before_delete_post listener exists on Album/Collection post types, so admin/Trash deletion orphans mvs_album_items, the _mvs_album_cover_media_id post_meta, and smart-collection rule meta. (2) UserDeletionService (UserDeletionService.php:41) cascades only media rows from mvs_media_index by post_author — it never deletes the user's mvs_album / mvs_collection CPTs or their items, so a deleted user's albums/collections + Pro membership rows orphan. (3) No mvs_collection_deleted / mvs_album_deleted action is fired anywhere, so Pro cannot purge mvs_pro_collection_items when a collection is deleted (it only listens on mvs_media_deleted) — Pro collection-membership rows accumulate forever after a collection is removed. Caching follows the cardinality rule (per-entity data in mvs_ tables, not options). Cover meta is self-healing on read (AlbumService.php:409).

ux.notes: Surfaces: (a) single-album page template album.php, (b) album-viewer block (src/blocks/album-viewer), (c) [mvs_album] shortcode (delegates to album-viewer render via render_block_template, Shortcodes.php:162), (d) [mvs_collection] shortcode (Shortcodes.php:545), (e) single-collection template collection.php, (f) Pro 'Save to' collection-picker popover (Pro collection-picker.js, hooked to Free favorite buttons). Owner editing on album.php is wired end-to-end (Interactivity API edit/delete, add-media uploader, set-cover) and has empty states ('This album is empty.'). BUT: album-level privacy is never enforced on any non-REST album read surface — album.php reads privacy only to print a badge (album.php:38,83), album-viewer render.php queries items with no can_view and no album gate (render.php:37-46), so a members/private album leaks title/description/item-count/categories/item titles+permalinks to anyone. Per-item images degrade to broken (signed /serve denies anon) but metadata leaks. The album-viewer block has no album picker — the editor must hand-type a numeric Album ID (edit.js:16-21), poor authoring UX. The [mvs_collection]/collection.php paths render any published collection to anyone by design (collections have no privacy field), but private media a user favorited into a manual collection — or matched by a smart-collection rule with no privacy clause — still has its title/permalink rendered to the public (Shortcodes.php:602 filters only on status='publish', not can_view). Mobile: grids use .mvs-cols-N / --mvs-grid-cols with no obvious per-breakpoint clamp in render.php; columns up to 5 hard-typed could overflow at 390px — flag for structural review (not browser-tested).

findings.title: Single-album page template has no privacy gate — members/private albums leak to anyone
findings.customer_impact: A creator sets an album to Members-only or Private. Anyone (including logged-out visitors) who opens the album's permalink sees the album title, description, item count, categories, author, privacy badge, and the title+link of every item in it. The item thumbnails break for unauthorized viewers (signed serve denies them) but the album's existence and full contents listing leak. This is the same members-level read leak the team just fixed on BP tabs/activity, now live on the album page.

findings.title: Album-viewer block and [mvs_album] shortcode render album contents with no privacy check
findings.customer_impact: The same album leak via a second and third surface: embedding the Album Viewer block (or [mvs_album id=...] shortcode, which shares this render) on any public page renders a private/members album's items to every visitor. render.php only checks the post is an mvs_album and items are status=publish — it never calls PrivacyService::can_view on the album. A fix on album.php alone would miss these two surfaces (the exact one-surface-fix-misses-others bug class).

findings.title: Deleting an album/collection from WP admin orphans custom-table rows and meta
findings.customer_impact: Cleanup only happens on the REST delete route. When an admin deletes an album or collection from the WordPress Posts list or empties Trash, mvs_album_items rows, the pinned-cover post meta, and smart-collection rule meta are left behind. Over time the database accumulates orphaned membership rows that can resurface as ghost items if an album ID is reused, and bloats backups. No before_delete_post listener exists on either CPT.

findings.title: User deletion never removes the user's albums, collections, or their membership rows
findings.customer_impact: When a member is deleted, the cascade cleans their media and per-user social rows but never touches mvs_album / mvs_collection CPTs (they live in wp_posts, not mvs_media_index) nor mvs_album_items / mvs_pro_collection_items keyed to those albums/collections. A deleted user's albums and collections (and Pro membership rows) orphan, which is a GDPR-erasure gap a paying site owner will be asked about.

findings.title: No mvs_collection_deleted hook — Pro multi-collection rows are never purged on collection delete
findings.customer_impact: CollectionController::delete_item nullifies mvs_favorites.collection_id but fires no action, and Pro only purges mvs_pro_collection_items on mvs_media_deleted. So every time a collection is deleted, its Pro membership rows stay forever. On Pro sites these rows accumulate indefinitely and a future collection reusing the same ID would silently inherit stale memberships. Free should fire mvs_collection_deleted (and mvs_album_deleted) and Pro should listen.

findings.title: Per-item privacy leak in collection rendering (favorited private media / smart-rule matches)
findings.customer_impact: A published collection is public by design, but its item loop filters only on status='publish' (Shortcodes.php:602), not on PrivacyService::can_view. If a user favorited someone's private media into a manual collection, or a smart collection's rules match private media (CollectionService::resolve has no privacy filter unless the owner adds a privacy rule, CollectionService.php:96-128), the title and permalink of that private item are exposed publicly. Images break for anon but titles/links leak.

findings.title: Bulk change_privacy accepts an unvalidated privacy string
findings.customer_impact: The bulk action writes whatever 'privacy' string the client sends straight to storage with no enum check. A typo or bad client value (e.g. 'friend' vs 'friends') is silently saved; PrivacyService then treats the unknown level as deny-all (default: return false), so the media vanishes from everyone's view with no error returned. The route reports success while effectively hiding the items.

findings.title: Album Viewer block requires a hand-typed numeric Album ID (no picker)
findings.customer_impact: To place the Album Viewer block an editor must know and type the album's numeric post ID into a sidebar field — there is no album search/select control. Non-technical site builders cannot discover the ID without digging into the admin, so the block feels broken/half-finished compared to the rest of the block library.

findings.title: reorder_items write route has no rate limiter
findings.customer_impact: Every other album write (create/update/delete/add_items) is rate-limited via RateLimiter::check, but reorder is not. A drag-reorder UI that fires one PUT per drop, or an abusive client, can hammer the endpoint with unbounded per-row UPDATEs. Low impact but inconsistent with the rest of the controller.

overcooked_items: Smart-collection rule engine (CollectionService::resolve) supports 7 rule keys (media_type, tag, category, author, date_after, date_before, privacy) assembled into dynamic JOINs/WHEREs, but the only UI that writes rules is the REST /rules route and editor JSON — there is no customer-facing rule builder UI, so most of this flexibility is unreachable by the people paying for it. Either ship a rule-builder UX or trim the engine to the rules a customer can actually set.
Two near-identical rule-enrichment code paths exist: CollectionController::enrich_rule (CollectionController.php:438) and an inline duplicate in collection.php:41-58. Consolidate into one helper.
missing_for_complete_solution: Album-level privacy enforcement on ALL non-REST read surfaces (album.php template, album-viewer block render.php, and therefore the [mvs_album] shortcode) — call PrivacyService::can_view(album_id, current_user) and show a proper 'private album' empty state instead of leaking metadata.
Per-item privacy filtering when rendering collections so favorited/smart-matched private media titles and links are not exposed on public collection pages.
before_delete_post cleanup on mvs_album and mvs_collection CPTs (delete album items, pinned-cover meta, rule meta) so WP-admin deletion matches REST deletion.

Album and collection cleanup in UserDeletionService, plus a mvs_collection_deleted / mvs_album_deleted action so Pro can purge mvs_pro_collection_items — needed for GDPR erasure and to stop orphan accumulation on Pro sites.
An album picker control in the Album Viewer block editor (search-and-select) so non-technical editors don't have to type a numeric ID.
Enum validation on the bulk change_privacy parameter so an invalid value returns an actionable 400 instead of silently hiding media.
A customer-facing smart-collection rule builder UI (or removal of the unused rule keys) so the rule engine the product ships is actually usable.

feature.name: Dashboard + profile editing (My Media, avatar, DM/online settings)
feature.entry: templates/partials/dashboard-content.php, templates/profile-edit.php, Services/ProfileService.php, REST ProfileController + UserController, src/blocks/dashboard-view
feature.note: DM/online selects just added to dashboard surface (adac3e1) — check remaining profile surfaces are complete.

audit.feature: Dashboard + profile editing (My Media, avatar, DM/online settings) — free
audit.verdict_reason: The feature is broad and the recently-added DM/online selects DID land on all three profile-edit surfaces (standalone template, [wpmediaverse_profile_edit] shortcode, dashboard inline form) — that surface-parity check passes. But there are real, customer-visible gaps: (1) the dashboard header (avatar/name/bio) does not refresh after an inline profile save because the dashboard and profile-edit Interactivity stores hold separate contexts and the save path never syncs them back; (2) the custom-avatar attachment file is orphaned on user deletion (UserDeletionService cleans every mvs_* table but never deletes the _mvs_custom_avatar attachment or its file); (3) the online_status options the member sees (Yes/No only) do not model the followers level the admin option + enforcement layer support, so a site defaulting to followers shows a wrong/misleading value and silently downgrades to everyone on save. API and privacy gating are solid and well-triaged. Net: dependable core, a few half-cooked edges a paying customer will hit.

api.notes: mvs/v1 profile routes are clean and consistent. ProfileController: GET/PUT /me/profile and POST/DELETE /me/avatar all use check_logged_in() (returns 401 WP_Error, not bare false) — correct, these are self-only edits. PUT args declare types, enum, and sanitize_callback for every field including the new dm_access/online_status (sanitize_key + enum from ProfileService::META_VALUES). Avatar upload validates MIME + 2MB size in the service with filters (mvs_avatar_allowed_types, mvs_avatar_max_size). Error responses are actionable (mvs_no_file, mvs_invalid_avatar_type, mvs_avatar_too_large). UserController's three __return_true routes are intentional and correctly documented: privacy is enforced at the SQL level (users/{id}/media uses privacy IN clauses keyed to viewer auth) and username/registered are gated to self+admin (WMV-01). No dead routes — every route has a frontend consumer (profile-edit.js, user search, public profile). No broken wiring — every JS fetch (me/profile, me/avatar) maps to a registered route. Minor: GET /users/{id}/media sets X-WP-Total but not X-WP-TotalPages (slightly dishonest pagination for clients that page by total-pages). The ProfileController PUT/POST/DELETE responses are NOT formally schema'd (no get_item_schema on ProfileController) which technically violates the plugin's own Coding Rule 6, but shape is consistent in practice.

dataflow.notes: Entry->service->WP user fields/usermeta->avatar attachment is clean and single-sourced: ProfileService owns AVATAR_META_KEY + META_FIELDS, and the DM/online user-meta keys (_mvs_dm_access, _mvs_show_online) are consumed correctly by MessagingService (DM gate) and the mvs_show_online_status filter in Plugin.php (online visibility) — so those settings genuinely take effect. Privacy reads on the public user endpoints fail-safe (SQL privacy clauses by viewer auth). Extensibility hooks fire on every transition (mvs_profile_updated, mvs_avatar_uploaded, mvs_avatar_deleted, mvs_user_data_purged). Caching follows the cardinality rule (per-user data in usermeta, not options/transients). TWO real defects: (a) user-deletion cascade does not delete the custom avatar attachment — UserDeletionService phase-1/2 cover every mvs_* table but the _mvs_custom_avatar attachment post + its file on disk are orphaned (delete_avatar() in ProfileService is the only path that frees them, and deletion never calls it); (b) online_status value domain is inconsistent across layers — ProfileService::META_VALUES['online_status']=[everyone,nobody], but the admin option mvs_show_online_status whitelist=[everyone,followers,nobody], so the 'followers' level the site default can hold is not representable in the member surface.

ux.notes: Surfaces exposing profile editing: (1) standalone template /media/edit-profile/ (templates/profile-edit.php), (2) [wpmediaverse_profile_edit] shortcode (Shortcodes.php ~670-797), (3) dashboard inline edit form (dashboard-content.php 139-258). All three now carry the DM 'Who can message you' + 'Show your online status' selects — the recently-added selects did reach every profile-edit surface (the #1 bug class for this cycle is NOT present here). My Media dashboard surfaces (dashboard tab template + dashboard-view block + shortcode dashboard) all share dashboard-content.php, so tabs/empty states/load-more are uniform; every tab has a real empty state. BIGGEST UX defect: after an inline profile save on the dashboard, the header avatar/name/bio do not update — mvs/profile-edit store updates its own context and closes the form via mvs/dashboard::toggleProfileEdit, but never writes the new displayName/avatarUrl/bio back into the mvs/dashboard context that renders the header, so it shows stale data until reload. The standalone editor and shortcode editor are NOT reachable from the BP profile tab (read-only Media/Albums only) and there is no in-dashboard link to the standalone /media/edit-profile/ page — discoverability of DM/online settings depends entirely on the user opening the dashboard inline form. online_status select misrepresents state when site default = followers (no matching option). Mobile/390px: the dashboard inline edit uses .mvs-profile-field-row two-column rows (name pair, dm/online pair) — structural risk of cramped selects at 390px unless the row collapses to single column; flag for verification.

findings.title: Dashboard header shows stale avatar/name/bio after inline profile save
findings.customer_impact: A member edits their name/bio/avatar in the dashboard's inline editor, sees 'Profile updated successfully', the form closes — but the profile header at the top of the dashboard still shows the OLD name, bio and avatar until they reload the page. Looks like the save didn't work; will generate 'my changes don't stick' support tickets.
findings.detail: The dashboard renders the header from the mvs/dashboard context (displayName/avatarUrl/bio, set server-side in dashboard-content.php:39-44). The inline form runs in a separate mvs/profile-edit context. On save, profile-edit.js updates its OWN context and calls dashboard.actions.toggleProfileEdit() to close the form, but nothing copies the new values into the mvs/dashboard context. The two stores never sync, so the header is stale post-save.

findings.title: Custom avatar attachment + file orphaned on user deletion
findings.customer_impact: When an admin deletes a member (or removes them from a site), the member's uploaded avatar image stays on disk forever as an orphaned Media Library attachment. Over time this accumulates as untracked storage the customer pays for and a privacy concern (deleted user's photo still served).
findings.detail: handle_user_deletion() cascades media via MediaRepository and purges every per-user mvs_* table, but never removes the _mvs_custom_avatar attachment. ProfileService::delete_avatar() (which wp_delete_attachment + delete_user_meta) is only called from the explicit REST DELETE path, never from the deletion cascade. The cascade should look up ProfileService::get_custom_avatar_id() / call delete_avatar() (or wp_delete_attachment on the stored ID) for the deleted user.

findings.title: online_status value domain inconsistent: member UI cannot represent the 'followers' level the admin default supports
findings.customer_impact: If the site owner sets the default Online Status Visibility to 'Followers only', a member opening their profile editor sees the 'Show your online status' select fall back to the first option ('Yes'/everyone) — it misrepresents the real setting, and if they touch Save it silently downgrades them to 'everyone'. The member surface and the admin/enforcement layer disagree about what values exist.
findings.detail: ProfileService allows only [everyone,nobody] for online_status and the three editor surfaces only render Yes/No, but the admin option whitelist is [everyone,followers,nobody] and the get_profile() fallback can return the option value 'followers'. The data-wp-bind--value=followers matches no <option>. Either add a 'Followers only' option to the three member selects (and to META_VALUES) or normalize 'followers'->'everyone' when surfacing per-user.

findings.title: GET /users/{id}/media omits X-WP-TotalPages header
findings.customer_impact: Clients/integrations that paginate a member's media gallery by total-page count get an incomplete pagination contract and may stop early or over-fetch.
findings.detail: $total is computed and emitted as X-WP-Total, but X-WP-TotalPages (ceil(total/per_page)) is not set, unlike WP core list controllers. Add the second header for an honest pagination contract.
