verified.title: Dashboard header shows stale avatar/name/bio after inline profile save
verified.customer_impact: A member edits their name/bio/avatar in the dashboard's inline editor, sees 'Profile updated successfully', the form closes — but the profile header at the top of the dashboard still shows the OLD name, bio and avatar until they reload the page. Looks like the save didn't work; will generate 'my changes don't stick' support tickets.
verified.detail: The dashboard renders the header from the mvs/dashboard context (displayName/avatarUrl/bio, set server-side in dashboard-content.php:39-44). The inline form runs in a separate mvs/profile-edit context. On save, profile-edit.js updates its OWN context and calls dashboard.actions.toggleProfileEdit() to close the form, but nothing copies the new values into the mvs/dashboard context. The two stores never sync, so the header is stale post-save.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed in code. The dashboard profile header and the inline editor live in two SEPARATE Interactivity API stores/contexts:

1. The header (templates/partials/dashboard-content.php:116-136) sits inside the OUTER `data-wp-interactive="mvs/dashboard"` element (line 111) and binds to that context's values: `context.avatarUrl` (line 118), `context.displayName` (line 121), `context.bio` (lines 122-123). These are seeded server-side at dashboard-content.php:39-44 from `wp_get_current_user()`.

2. The inline edit form (lines 139-258) has its own NESTED `data-wp-interactive="mvs/profile-edit"` element (line 141) with an independent context block (lines 144-164: firstName/displayName/bio/avatarUrl/etc.).

On save, profile-edit.js `saveProfile` (lines 100-104) writes the new values ONLY to the profile-edit context (`ctx.displayName`, `ctx.bio`, `ctx.avatarUrl`), shows "Profile updated successfully." (lines 106-108), then calls `store('mvs/dashboard').actions.toggleProfileEdit()` (lines 111-114) merely to close the form. The dashboard store's `toggleProfileEdit` (view.js:779-784) only flips `editingProfile` and clears `profileMessage`/`profileError` — it does NOT copy displayName/avatarUrl/bio. Grepping the entire dashboard view.js shows it references `displayName`/`avatarUrl`/`bio` NOWHERE; only `profileMessage`/`profileError` at lines 782-783. The dashboard `init` callback (view.js:1444-1485) runs once on mount and never re-reads or re-fetches profile values, and there is no watcher.

Writing to the `mvs/profile-edit` context does not mutate the separate `mvs/dashboard` context, and the header div is a sibling of (outside) the profile-edit element, so it keeps rendering the dashboard context's original server-seeded values. Net effect: header name/bio/avatar stay stale until a full page reload. Same staleness applies to avatar upload/delete (profile-edit.js:162-163, 203-204), which update only the profile-edit context. No guard, filter, watcher, or consumer rescues this; no docblock or CLAUDE.md note marks it intentional. The claimed customer impact (success toast immediately followed by a visibly unchanged header on the primary member dashboard, every save -> "my changes don't stick" tickets) materializes exactly as described.

Severity: the data IS persisted server-side and a reload heals it (no data loss), so it is a pure stale-display defect rather than a functional failure. But it fires on every profile save on a core member surface and directly contradicts the on-screen success message, which is precisely the kind of "looks broken" UX that generates support tickets. high/ux is defensible; it could equally be argued as a strong medium. I leave the rating as-is.

feature.name: Social interactions (reactions, comments, favorites, mentions, shares, follows)
feature.entry: Social/ (ReactionService, CommentService, FavoriteService, MentionService, ShareService, FollowService), REST ReactionController + CommentController + FavoriteController + FollowController

audit.feature: Social interactions (reactions, comments, favorites, mentions, shares, follows) — free
audit.verdict_reason: Follows and the comment write/edit/delete paths are right-sized and solid. But three things break the "complete, dependable" promise: (1) a privacy hole — comments, reaction counts, and the activity feed are readable/writable on private/restricted media straight through the public REST routes, with controller comments that falsely claim a privacy join exists; (2) a double-fire of mvs_reaction_added that sends customers duplicate notifications, duplicate activity rows, and duplicate webhooks on every reaction add; (3) two half-built features shipped — @mentions are parsed nowhere (notification path is wired but the producer is never called) and ShareService is dead code while the Share button on the single-media surface never records a share. These are exactly the "half-cooked" and "missing surface" classes the owner wants avoided.

api.notes: Routes are clean in shape, namespaced mvs/v1, pagination headers honest (X-WP-Total/X-WP-TotalPages), enum validation on reaction_type, rate limiting on every write. Permission_callbacks are the problem. GET /media/{id}/comments and GET /media/{id}/reactions are __return_true with an inline comment asserting the underlying repo 'joins on mvs_media_index.privacy' — it does NOT (CommentService::get_for_media uses plain get_comments by comment_post_ID; ReactionService::get_counts is a raw COUNT on mvs_reactions). So private/restricted media's comments and reaction counts are world-readable by media-id. The write paths (POST comment/reaction/favorite) only check is_user_logged_in(), never PrivacyService::can_view — contrast MediaController::record_share which DOES call can_view. So any logged-in user can comment/react/favorite media they cannot view. Dead/duplicate API: ShareService::record_share exists but the only share route lives in MediaController::record_share which re-implements the INSERT and fires a DIFFERENT hook (mvs_share_recorded vs ShareService's mvs_media_shared) — ShareService is never called. MentionService has no route and no caller. Broken wiring: the Share button in the media-social block (single-media page) only does navigator.share/clipboard and never POSTs /media/{id}/share, so shares are uncounted there; only the lightbox (shared-ui) posts the share stat.

dataflow.notes: Delete cascades are genuinely thorough: MediaRepository::delete_cascade clears reactions/favorites/mentions/comments and UserDeletionService (deleted_user + remove_user_from_blog) purges all user-scoped social tables plus reverse-side follows/blocks/reports — this part is well-built. Counts are denormalized correctly (ReactionService::sync_stats updates both mvs_media_stats and mvs_media_index.reaction_count). Caching follows the cardinality rule (per-entity in mvs_* tables, CacheService drops on stat-change hooks). The breaks: (1) mvs_reaction_added double-fires — ReactionService::toggle line 100 AND ReactionController line 184 both do_action it on add; NotificationService::create and ActivityService::record have NO dedup, so every reaction-add writes 2 notifications + 2 activity rows + 2 webhook calls. On reaction UPDATE only the controller fires, so behavior is inconsistent add-vs-update. (2) Privacy gate missing at the read path for activity: ActivityService::get_feed selects mvs_activity with no JOIN on media privacy, and format_activity attaches private media's title+thumbnail+permalink — public feed (__return_true) leaks that private media exists and who interacted with it. (3) MentionService::parse_and_store is never invoked (CommentService::add never parses @mentions), so mvs_mentions stays empty and mvs_mentions_created never fires despite NotificationService listening for it. (4) Minor: deleting a collection does not null favorites.collection_id, orphaning rows; UserDeletionService doesn't delete the deleted user's mvs_comment comments left on others' media.

ux.notes: Surfaces exposing social: media-social block + media-single.php (reactions/favorite/comments/share/follow/report), shared-ui lightbox (favorite/share/reaction/report), dashboard-view (favorites tab, notifications dropdown, following), explore feed, BP profile/group tabs, member-photos/media-grid cards. Reactions/comments/favorites/follow are wired end-to-end with optimistic UI, toasts, and error rollback — good. Gaps: (a) Share is inconsistent across surfaces — lightbox records the share stat, single-media media-social block does not (the #1 'fix landed on one surface, missed the other' class). (b) @mention is a dead end for customers: a user types @name in a comment expecting the person to be notified; nothing happens (mentioned person never sees 'X mentioned you' even though that notification string and type ship). (c) media-social fetchFavorite pulls me/favorites?per_page=100 and scans client-side instead of the cheap GET /media/{id}/favorite status route used by lightbox/dashboard — a user with >100 favorites sees a wrong heart state on the 101st item. Empty states and 390px tap targets were hardened in prior releases and look fine structurally. Logged-out users correctly see prompts to log in to react/favorite/comment.

findings.title: Comments and reaction counts on private/restricted media are world-readable via REST (controller comment falsely claims a privacy join)
findings.customer_impact: Anyone (even logged out) can hit /wp-json/mvs/v1/media/{id}/comments or .../reactions for a private or members-only media item and read every comment and the reaction tally. The media-single page is gated, but the REST routes bypass that gate. The inline code comment claims the query 'returns empty (the repo joins on mvs_media_index.privacy)' — that join does not exist, so reviewers think it is safe when it is not. This is the same members-level leak class the team just fixed on BP tabs.

findings.title: Any logged-in user can comment/react/favorite media they cannot view (no can_view on write paths)
findings.customer_impact: Write permission only checks is_user_logged_in(), never PrivacyService::can_view. A member can post comments on, react to, and favorite a private/restricted item by media-id without access to it — polluting the owner's private media with interactions and notifications. MediaController::record_share already does the can_view check, so the pattern exists; these three controllers just skip it.

findings.title: mvs_reaction_added double-fires on every reaction add → duplicate notifications, activity rows, and webhooks
findings.customer_impact: Add a reaction once and the media owner gets TWO 'X reacted to your media' notifications, the activity feed shows the reaction twice, and any configured webhook fires twice. On reaction UPDATE only one fires, so the duplication is inconsistent and confusing. NotificationService::create and ActivityService::record have no dedup to absorb it. Customers will report 'double notifications' and 'duplicate activity'.

findings.title: Public activity feed leaks private/restricted media (title, thumbnail, permalink) with no privacy gate
findings.location: includes/Social/ActivityService.php (get_feed SELECT a.* FROM mvs_activity with no privacy JOIN; format_activity attaches media summary unconditionally); includes/REST/Controller/ActivityController.php:63,92 (__return_true)
findings.customer_impact: The public activity stream shows 'User X reacted to / favorited / uploaded <private media title>' with thumbnail and link to anonymous visitors. Even though the thumbnail bytes are separately gated, the title, existence, and who-interacted-with-it of private/restricted media are exposed to everyone.

findings.title: @mentions are parsed nowhere — entire mention feature is dead despite a fully wired notification path
findings.location: includes/Social/MentionService.php (parse_and_store has no callers); includes/Social/CommentService.php:38-82 (add never calls it); includes/Social/NotificationService.php:54,477-479 (listens for mvs_mentions_created, has media_mention type + 'X mentioned you' string)
findings.customer_impact: A user types @username in a comment expecting that person to be notified. Nothing happens — no mention record, no notification, ever. The notification machinery for it ships and is visible, so the feature looks supported but is non-functional. Classic half-cooked: built one half, never connected the producer.

findings.title: ShareService is dead code; the only share stat path lives in MediaController and fires a different hook
findings.location: includes/Social/ShareService.php (record_share/get_share_links never called); includes/Core/Plugin.php:366 (registered as 'shares'); includes/REST/Controller/MediaController.php:1085-1130 (record_share re-implements + fires mvs_share_recorded, not ShareService's mvs_media_shared)
findings.customer_impact: Duplicate share logic in two places that fire two different hooks, so any integration listening for mvs_media_shared never fires. ShareService::get_share_links (Facebook/Twitter/LinkedIn/email buttons) is built but exposed nowhere. Maintenance trap and a missing share-buttons surface a customer may expect from the code that ships.

findings.title: Share button on single-media surface never records the share stat (lightbox does)
findings.location: src/blocks/media-social/view.js:355-385 (navigator.share/clipboard only, no POST /share); src/blocks/shared-ui/view.js:1271-1283 (lightbox DOES POST /share)
findings.customer_impact: Share counts only increment when a user shares from the lightbox, not from the single-media page's Share button. Share statistics are silently undercounted depending on which surface the visitor used — the inconsistent-across-surfaces bug class.

findings.title: media-social favorite-status check caps at 100 and ignores the dedicated status route
findings.location: src/blocks/media-social/view.js:114-126 (fetch me/favorites?per_page=100 + client scan); GET /media/{id}/favorite status route exists at includes/REST/Controller/FavoriteController.php:57-68 and is used by lightbox/dashboard
findings.customer_impact: A user with more than 100 favorites sees a wrong (empty) heart on items beyond the first 100 after page load, because the block scans only the first 100 favorites instead of asking the server about this one item. The correct, cheap GET status route already exists and is used elsewhere — just not here.

findings.title: Deleting a collection orphans favorites.collection_id; deleted user's comments on others' media survive
findings.location: includes/Services/CollectionService.php / PostTypes/Collection.php (no before_delete_post null-out of favorites.collection_id); includes/Services/UserDeletionService.php:41-112 (no mvs_comment delete for the user)
findings.customer_impact: After deleting a collection, favorite rows keep a dangling collection_id pointing at nothing. After deleting a user, their mvs_comment comments left on other people's media remain attached with the dead user_id (author name persists). Cosmetic/orphan-data only, not a leak.

overcooked_items: ShareService entire class — dead code duplicating MediaController::record_share with a divergent hook; either route the controller through it or delete it
ShareService::get_share_links (4 social platforms) built but never surfaced — dead until a UI consumes it

CommentService::format_comment (the include_replies=true branch) is only used as a per-reply formatter now that format_comment_with_replies exists; the recursive replies query inside it is dead in the main read path
Two separate share hooks (mvs_share_recorded in the controller, mvs_media_shared in ShareService) for one action — pick one
missing_for_complete_solution: Privacy gate (PrivacyService::can_view) on the comments GET, reactions GET, and on the comment/reaction/favorite write paths — today they are open by media-id
Privacy JOIN/filter on the activity feed so private/restricted media never appears in the public stream
Wire MentionService::parse_and_store into CommentService::add (and description edits) so @mentions actually notify people — the feature is advertised by the notification code but does nothing
Single dedup or single emit point for mvs_reaction_added so reactions don't double-notify / double-log
Make the single-media Share button record the share stat like the lightbox does, OR expose ShareService::get_share_links as real share buttons
Switch media-social favorite-status to the GET /media/{id}/favorite route so it is correct beyond 100 favorites
Null out favorites.collection_id on collection delete; remove the deleted user's mvs_comment comments in UserDeletionService

feature.name: Notifications (in-plugin + BP bridge)
feature.entry: Social/NotificationService.php, REST NotificationController, Integrations/BuddyPress/NotificationIntegration.php

audit.feature: Notifications (in-plugin notification center + BuddyPress notification bridge) — free plugin
audit.verdict_reason: The REST API and core service are clean and right-sized. But two structural gaps make this NOT a complete, dependable customer solution: (1) a duplicate-notification bug — `new_message` is created by BOTH NotificationService::on_message and Messaging\NotificationListener::on_message_sent, so every DM on a REST send produces two identical rows and bypasses the mute/coalesce guard; (2) a coverage hole — on BuddyPress sites the native bell is hidden by design, yet the BP bridge only mirrors 3 of 6 notification types, so follows, favorites, and new-message notifications are written to the table but NEVER surfaced anywhere. A paying customer on a BP site silently loses half their notifications.

api.notes: 3 routes under mvs/v1: GET /me/notifications, POST /me/notifications/read, GET /me/notifications/count. All gated by is_user_logged_in() which is correct (a user only ever reads/writes their OWN notifications — get_current_user_id() is used server-side, never a path param, so no IDOR). Write path is rate-limited (RateLimiter::check notification_write 60/60) and mark_read scopes every UPDATE to user_id so a user cannot mark another user's rows read. Input is sanitized (ids via absint, filter via sanitize_text_field). All 3 routes are consumed by the dashboard-view Interactivity block — no dead routes, no broken frontend wiring. Gaps: (a) controller defines no get_item_schema()/get_collection_params(), violating the plugin's own Coding Rule #6 (every controller must define a schema); the per_page/page/filter args are declared inline instead. (b) 'filter' arg has no enum — any string is accepted and silently coerced to 'all' in the service, so a typo like filter=unraed returns all rows with a 200 instead of a 400. (c) Pagination header is half-honest: X-WP-Total is set but X-WP-TotalPages is not, so a generic REST client cannot page deterministically (the bundled JS doesn't page, so customer impact is low).

dataflow.notes: Entry hooks (mvs_user_followed/reaction_added/comment_created/mentions_created/favorite_added/message_sent) -> NotificationService::create() -> $wpdb->insert into mvs_notifications -> wp_cache_delete of the per-user count -> do_action('mvs_notification_created') -> BP bridge mirrors. Caching follows the cardinality rule correctly: the unread count is a per-user object-cache key (mvs_notif_count_{id}, group mvs, 300s TTL), invalidated on every create and mark_read — NOT an option/transient. create() guards against self-notify and double-hook-registration (static flag in init()). DELETION: media delete_cascade() purges mvs_notifications by media_id (good); UserDeletionService purges by user_id (recipient side) — but does NOT purge rows where the deleted user is the actor_id, leaving orphaned rows; these degrade gracefully to 'Someone' via get_userdata() fallback in format_notification(), so low severity. BP-side rows created by the bridge are NEVER cleaned when the underlying media or user is deleted (no mvs_media_deleted / deleted_user listener in NotificationIntegration, unlike ActivitySyncIntegration which has one) — clicking a stale BP notification falls back to bp_get_notifications_permalink() via the exists() guard, graceful but stale. DUPLICATE LOGIC: new_message is handled by two independent listeners on the same hook — a real duplicate. Privacy: notification messages that embed a media title (reaction/comment/favorite) only ever go to the media OWNER, so no private-title leak; mentions go to arbitrary users but the mention message carries no title, so no leak there either — the BP/native link can still 403 for a mentioned user without view access (soft).

ux.notes: Surfaces enumerated: (1) native MVS notification bell in the dashboard-view block (templates/partials/dashboard-content.php) — full end-to-end wiring: bell -> toggleNotifications -> GET /me/notifications, mark-all + per-item read -> POST /me/notifications/read, badge count -> GET /me/notifications/count on init; empty state present ('No notifications yet.'). (2) BuddyPress nav bell via NotificationIntegration (component registration + Nouveau filters + format_notifications). NO block, NO shortcode, NO admin page, NO standalone notifications page. THE CORE UX GAP: the native bell renders ONLY when buddypress() is absent (dashboard-content.php:299). On a BP site the bell is suppressed in favor of BP's nav bell — but the BP bridge's TYPE_TO_BP_ACTION map only mirrors media_reaction, media_comment, media_mention. The other three types (new_follower, media_favorite, new_message) are written to mvs_notifications but have NO surface on a BP site: the native bell is hidden and the bridge skips them. So on BP sites (the plugin's primary deployment), a follow, a favorite, or a DM produces a DB row a user can never see. (3) Logged-out: routes correctly 401; bell only renders for logged-in dashboard. (4) Mobile/390px: the dropdown is position:absolute chrome anchored to the bell in the dashboard header — on a 390px viewport a right-anchored fixed-width dropdown risks horizontal overflow off the left edge; flag for structural review (not browser-verified here).

findings.title: Duplicate new_message notification on every DM (two listeners on mvs_message_sent)
findings.customer_impact: Every direct message a user receives creates TWO identical 'X sent you a message' notifications and a doubled unread badge. NotificationService::on_message also bypasses the mute/coalesce/BuddyNext guards that Messaging\NotificationListener implements, so muted conversations still generate one of the two notifications. Customers will report DM notification spam and inflated unread counts.
findings.detail: mvs_message_sent fires once (MessagingService.php:1151). NotificationService::init() (run when the container resolves 'notifications' during rest_api_init) hooks on_message, which loops recipients and calls create('new_message') with no coalescing or mute check. Messaging\NotificationListener::on_message_sent (registered eagerly in Plugin::init_messaging) ALSO calls create('new_message') with the full mute/coalesce/BuddyNext logic. Both run on a REST message send. create() has no dedup. One of these listeners is redundant — the messaging listener is the correct owner; NotificationService::on_message should be removed (or never hooked) for new_message.

findings.title: On BuddyPress sites, new_follower / media_favorite / new_message notifications are invisible
findings.customer_impact: On a BP site (the plugin's main use case) the native dashboard bell is intentionally hidden, but BP's bell only ever shows reactions, comments, and mentions. A new follower, a favorite on your media, or a new DM still writes an mvs_notifications row, yet no surface displays it. The customer experiences 'I never get notified when someone follows me or favorites my media' even though the data exists.
findings.detail: $mvs_show_dashboard_bell = ! function_exists('buddypress') hides the native bell whenever BP is active. TYPE_TO_BP_ACTION maps only media_reaction/comment/mention into BP. The remaining three types are commented as 'in-app only' but there is no in-app surface on a BP site. Either mirror the missing types into BP (follower/favorite/message), or keep the native bell visible on BP sites for the BP-unmapped types.

findings.title: BP bridge never cleans its notifications on media/user deletion
findings.customer_impact: After a media item or user is deleted, the BuddyPress notification rows the bridge created (item_id = media_id, secondary_item_id = actor_id) linger. The user keeps seeing notifications that link to content that no longer exists; clicking lands on a generic notifications page (graceful) but the count stays inflated until manually cleared.
findings.detail: NotificationIntegration::init() registers no mvs_media_deleted / deleted_user / mvs_user_data_purged listener to call bp_notifications_delete_notifications_by_item_id (compare ActivitySyncIntegration.php:56 which DOES clean BP activities on mvs_media_deleted). The native mvs_notifications rows are cleaned by delete_cascade (MediaRepository.php:2096) and UserDeletionService, but the mirrored BP rows are orphaned.

findings.title: UserDeletionService purges notifications by recipient only, not by actor
findings.customer_impact: When a user is deleted, notifications other users received that were triggered BY that user remain in the table referencing a non-existent actor. They render as 'Someone …' via the get_userdata() fallback — graceful, but the rows are dead data that accumulate over time.
findings.detail: The user_scoped_tables map deletes mvs_notifications WHERE user_id = deleted_id (recipient) but there is no reverse-side delete for actor_id, unlike the reverse-side cleanup added for mvs_follows.following_id and mvs_blocks.blocked_id just below it.

findings.title: NotificationController defines no item schema (violates plugin Coding Rule #6)
findings.customer_impact: No direct customer impact, but the response shape is undocumented to API consumers and the plugin's own CI rule ('every controller must define get_item_schema()') is unmet, so integrators building against mvs/v1 get no /schema introspection for notifications while other controllers provide it — an inconsistency in the public API surface.
findings.detail: WP_REST_Controller subclass with no get_item_schema() / get_collection_params(); args are declared inline on register_rest_route instead. Also: the 'filter' arg has no enum, so an invalid filter silently returns 'all' (200) instead of a 400 validation error.

findings.title: Pagination header incomplete (X-WP-Total without X-WP-TotalPages)
findings.customer_impact: A third-party client paging /me/notifications cannot compute the last page from headers alone. The bundled dashboard JS does not page so end-user impact is nil, but it is an honesty gap versus other list endpoints in the suite.
findings.detail: Only X-WP-Total is emitted. get_notifications() returns total, so X-WP-TotalPages = ceil(total/per_page) is trivially derivable and should be added for header parity with the rest of mvs/v1 list controllers.

overcooked_items: The mvs_should_send_notification, mvs_notification_data, mvs_notification_types, and mvs_notification_message filters are a full extension surface (4 filters) on a feature whose only in-repo consumer is Pro challenge/tournament types. Reasonable for an extension point, but verify Pro actually uses more than mvs_notification_types/message before keeping all four — the data and should_send filters appear to have no consumer and add an unbenefited customization seam.
missing_for_complete_solution: A single notification surface that works the same on BP and non-BP sites — today the native bell is hidden on BP and the BP bridge covers only 3 of 6 types, so follows/favorites/DMs vanish on BP installs. Pick one canonical surface that shows ALL types regardless of BP.
Dedup of the new_message path so a DM produces exactly one notification with mute/coalesce honored.
BP-side cleanup when the underlying media or user is deleted (mirror ActivitySyncIntegration's mvs_media_deleted listener).
Email/digest notifications — there is no off-site notification at all; customers running a media community will ask 'how do users get notified when they're offline?'. Currently 100% in-session.

A per-user notification preferences UI (which types to receive) — the mvs_should_send_notification filter exists for developers but there is no customer-facing setting, so a site owner cannot let members mute, say, favorite notifications.

verified.title: Duplicate new_message notification on every DM (two listeners on mvs_message_sent)
verified.customer_impact: Every direct message a user receives creates TWO identical 'X sent you a message' notifications and a doubled unread badge. NotificationService::on_message also bypasses the mute/coalesce/BuddyNext guards that Messaging\NotificationListener implements, so muted conversations still generate one of the two notifications. Customers will report DM notification spam and inflated unread counts.
verified.detail: mvs_message_sent fires once (MessagingService.php:1151). NotificationService::init() (run when the container resolves 'notifications' during rest_api_init) hooks on_message, which loops recipients and calls create('new_message') with no coalescing or mute check. Messaging\NotificationListener::on_message_sent (registered eagerly in Plugin::init_messaging) ALSO calls create('new_message') with the full mute/coalesce/BuddyNext logic. Both run on a REST message send. create() has no dedup. One of these listeners is redundant — the messaging listener is the correct owner; NotificationService::on_message should be removed (or never hooked) for new_message.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED REAL. Two independent listeners are both hooked on the single `mvs_message_sent` action and both call NotificationService::create('new_message') with no dedup, producing two identical rows (and a doubled unread badge) per DM.

Wiring proof:
- includes/Core/Plugin.php:258 calls init_messaging() unconditionally on every request. init_messaging() (line 1438-1439) does `new NotificationListener($messaging_service); $listener->init();`, registering on_message_sent on mvs_message_sent (NotificationListener.php:33).
- includes/Core/Plugin.php:691 resolves the 'notifications' container key during register_rest_routes (rest_api_init). The factory (lines 597-600) calls NotificationService::init(), which registers on_message on the SAME action (NotificationService.php:56). The static $registered guard only blocks double-registration of the same NotificationService instance; it does nothing about the separate NotificationListener.
- mvs_message_sent fires once per real message send (MessagingService.php:1151). Both callbacks therefore run.

Duplicate insert proof:
- NotificationService::on_message (NotificationService.php:376-380) loops recipients and calls create(recipient, 'new_message', sender) with NO mute/coalesce/BuddyNext check.
- NotificationListener::on_message_sent (NotificationListener.php:48-92) applies mute skip, 30s coalesce transient, and BuddyNext deferral, THEN calls create(recipient,'new_message',sender,0,0) (line 89).
- create() (NotificationService.php:74-165) has zero dedup for new_message — recipient != sender and type is allowed, so it always $wpdb->insert()s a row. Two rows result. get_unread_count (line 250-268) counts all unread rows, so the badge doubles.

Not intentional / not a missed guard: git blame shows the duplicate was introduced by commit aa79594 ("fix: wire DM notifications") on the false premise that 'new_message was defined but never wired.' The pre-existing NotificationListener (from commit e606365, DM-engine move) ALREADY wired new_message WITH the guards — verified via `git show aa79594^:includes/Messaging/NotificationListener.php` showing create('new_message') at line 89 before that commit. So the messaging listener is the correct owner and NotificationService::on_message is the redundant, guard-less duplicate. No remove_action, no suppressing filter, no create()-level dedup exists anywhere.

Mute-bypass sub-claim also confirmed: NotificationService::on_message has no is_muted check and no mvs_buddynext_active check, so muted conversations and BuddyNext-active sites still generate one of the two notifications.

Severity 'high' is correct: deterministic, user-visible defect on a core feature (every received DM doubles + inflated unread count + defeats mute), affecting all messaging-enabled sites, but not a crash/data-loss blocker. The fix is to remove (or never hook) NotificationService::on_message and let Messaging\NotificationListener own new_message.

verified.title: On BuddyPress sites, new_follower / media_favorite / new_message notifications are invisible
verified.customer_impact: On a BP site (the plugin's main use case) the native dashboard bell is intentionally hidden, but BP's bell only ever shows reactions, comments, and mentions. A new follower, a favorite on your media, or a new DM still writes an mvs_notifications row, yet no surface displays it. The customer experiences 'I never get notified when someone follows me or favorites my media' even though the data exists.
verified.detail: $mvs_show_dashboard_bell = ! function_exists('buddypress') hides the native bell whenever BP is active. TYPE_TO_BP_ACTION maps only media_reaction/comment/mention into BP. The remaining three types are commented as 'in-app only' but there is no in-app surface on a BP site. Either mirror the missing types into BP (follower/favorite/message), or keep the native bell visible on BP sites for the BP-unmapped types.

verdict.reason:
Partially confirmed in code, but narrower than claimed. CONFIRMED: dashboard-content.php:299 sets $mvs_show_dashboard_bell = ! function_exists('buddypress'), so on any BP site the in-plugin notification bell (the only surface that fetches/lists mvs_notifications via me/notifications, wired solely to actions.toggleNotifications in dashboard-view/view.js) is not rendered. NotificationIntegration.php:28 TYPE_TO_BP_ACTION mirrors only media_reaction/media_comment/media_mention into BP; on_notification_created returns early for the rest. NotificationService creates all six types (new_follower, media_reaction, media_comment, media_mention, media_favorite, new_message). So new_follower and media_favorite write a row but, on a BP site, have NO surface at all — neither the (hidden) bell nor BP's bell nor any BP activity (ActivitySyncIntegration emits nothing for follow/favorite). That part of the finding is REAL.

REFUTED for new_message: the finding's claim that new DMs are invisible on BP sites is wrong. The floating chat panel is rendered globally on wp_footer (Plugin::render_chat_panel, default mvs_chat_panel_visibility='everywhere', with an explicit 'bp_pages' option) and its trigger shows an unread badge driven by me/messages/unread-count + a background unreadTimer (messaging.js). That surface is fully independent of the notification bell, so new_message reaches the recipient on a BP site.

Net: a genuine UX gap, but it affects 2 of the 3 cited types (follower + favorite), not 3. Downgrading high→medium: it is a real silent-notification-loss on the plugin's main platform, but it is not data loss/security, is limited to two lower-frequency social signals, and the most user-noticed type (DMs) is actually surfaced. Fix is as the finding suggests — either add follower/favorite to a BP mapping (note BP add_notification needs item_id/media_id, which new_follower lacks, so it'd need a different shape) or keep the native bell visible on BP sites for BP-unmapped types.

feature.name: Moderation & reports (queue, AI moderation, user blocks)
feature.entry: Services/ModerationService.php, Social/ReportService.php, Admin/ModerationQueue.php, REST ModerationController + ReportController, mvs_blocks table

audit.feature: Moderation & reports (queue, AI moderation, user blocks) — free
audit.verdict_reason: The backend (ModerationService, ReportService, cascade cleanup, block enforcement in DMs/activity) is solid and correctly built. But the feature is incomplete for a paying customer on the free tier: (1) the entire mvs/v1/moderation REST controller (6 routes) is dead — no frontend or admin consumer uses it; (2) user reports submitted from the frontend have NO admin surface in free (the report-viewing/resolving UI lives only in Pro's ReportManager), so a free customer collects abuse reports they can never read or action; (3) block/unblock and report-user REST routes exist but no free UI exposes them, so members cannot actually block anyone from the UI; (4) the AI moderation queue only populates if a paid external AI provider key is configured, otherwise the whole Moderation page is permanently empty. So the parts that ship are right-sized, but key surfaces are missing — a customer hits dead ends.

api.notes: Permission callbacks are correct: ModerationController gates every route on moderate_mvs_media; ReportController gates on is_user_logged_in() with per-action RateLimiter and self-report/self-block guards in the service. Input is validated (reason enum, absint IDs, sanitize callbacks). Response shapes are consistent with mvs/v1 and pagination headers (X-WP-Total/X-WP-TotalPages) are honest. The problem is wiring, not security: the entire ModerationController (GET /moderation, /moderation/counts, POST /{id}/approve, /{id}/reject, /{id}/analyze, GET /ai/usage) has ZERO consumers — the admin Moderation page runs its own form-POST flow via ModerationQueue::handle_actions() and direct service calls, never touching REST. That is 6 dead routes. On the Report side, /media/{id}/report is consumed by media-social view.js, but /users/{id}/report, POST+DELETE /users/{id}/block, and GET /me/blocked have no frontend consumer anywhere in free (verified by grep across src/, assets/, templates/) — routes exist, no UI calls them.

dataflow.notes: Entry->service->table->output is clean for what exists. ModerationService writes moderation_status + moderation_log via MediaRepository; get_queue/get_counts read mvs_media_index directly with prepared queries. ReportService writes mvs_reports/mvs_blocks with prepared inserts, dedupe via has_reported(), and an auto-hide-at-threshold path (mvs_report_auto_hide_threshold, default 3). Block enforcement is applied at read paths that matter: MessagingService + MessagingController gate on is_blocked_either_way(), and ActivityService excludes get_blocked_ids() from the feed. Hooks fired for extensibility: mvs_moderation_changed, mvs_report_submitted, mvs_user_blocked, mvs_media_flagged. CLEANUP GAP: MediaRepository::delete_cascade() deletes 12 mvs_* tables but NOT mvs_reports rows targeting the deleted media (target_type='media', target_id=$media_id) — those reports orphan forever. User-deletion cleanup (UserDeletionService) is thorough and DOES purge reports/blocks on both sides, so the gap is media-deletion-only. Caching: get_counts result is cached in a 60s transient (mvs_moderation_counts) used only for the menu badge, never invalidated on approve/reject, so the badge can be stale up to 60s (acceptable, fixed-key, within Rule 16). Privacy gates: block enforcement is NOT applied to the explore feed / media grid / single-media reads — a blocked user's public media still shows everywhere except the activity feed and DMs. That may be intended (blocks scoped to feed+DM) but it is asymmetric and undocumented.

ux.notes: Surfaces enumerated: (a) Admin Moderation page (ModerationQueue) — AI Flagged / Pending / Resolved tabs, bulk approve/reject, per-row approve/reject via HTML5 form= association (the nested-form bug was already fixed in 1.4.0). Empty state present ('Queue is Clear'). BUT: menu registered with 'manage_options' while render_page() and the REST cap accept 'moderate_mvs_media' — an Editor (granted moderate_mvs_media) can moderate via REST and can render the page if they reach the URL, but the menu item is hidden from them. Access inconsistency. (b) Frontend Report button — wired only in media-social (media-single template + media-social block / album). NOT present on explore grid, media-grid, lightbox, or member-photos, so reporting is inconsistent across surfaces (the #1 bug class this cycle). The report dialog hardcodes details:'Reported via media page' — the user's free-text detail is never captured even though the API and DB support it. The 7 reason labels in view.js are hardcoded English, not run through __(), unlike the rest of the file. (c) NO free admin surface to VIEW or RESOLVE the reports that the frontend collects — mvs_reports rows are write-only in free; the report queue/resolve UI is Pro-only (ReportManager + mvs_moderation_tabs 'User Reports' tab). (d) User-block UI does not exist on any free surface — members cannot block anyone from the UI even though the engine and routes are complete. Logged-out: report button correctly hidden/replaced; fine. Mobile/390px: report flow injects a <select> into the confirm dialog at runtime via querySelector('.mvs-confirm') + requestAnimationFrame — fragile and the injected select has no explicit 44px tap-target styling, structural mobile risk.

findings.title: Frontend abuse reports are write-only in free — no admin surface to read or resolve them
findings.location: includes/Social/ReportService.php:49 (report write); includes/Admin/ModerationQueue.php:176 (tabs only show flagged/pending/rejected media, never mvs_reports rows)
findings.customer_impact: A free customer enables the Report button, members file reports, those rows land in mvs_reports — and the site owner has nowhere in the free plugin to see them. The report queue and resolve/dismiss UI live only in Pro (ReportManager). On free, reports accumulate invisibly and abuse is never actioned. Either ship a minimal report list in free or stop exposing the report button until there is somewhere for reports to go.
findings.detail: ReportService::report/update_status/count_by_status all exist; ModerationQueue only renders media-status tabs and exposes mvs_moderation_tabs for Pro to inject the User Reports tab. No free admin code reads mvs_reports (grep of includes/Admin/ is empty).

findings.title: Entire mvs/v1/moderation REST controller (6 routes) is dead in free
findings.location: includes/REST/Controller/ModerationController.php:67-163; admin flow at includes/Admin/ModerationQueue.php:69 (form POST, not REST)
findings.customer_impact: Six registered, permission-checked, schema-defined REST routes (GET /moderation, /moderation/counts, POST /{id}/approve, /{id}/reject, /{id}/analyze, GET /ai/usage) are never called by any free UI — the admin Moderation page uses its own admin-post form handler instead. This is maintenance surface and attack surface that buys the customer nothing; it should either back the admin UI or be removed.
findings.detail: Verified no consumer in src/, assets/, or templates/ for v1/moderation*. The admin page calls ModerationService directly.

findings.title: User-block and report-user routes exist but no free UI exposes them
findings.customer_impact: The block-user engine is fully built and enforced in DMs and the activity feed, but a free member has no button anywhere to block a user or report a user, and no 'Blocked users' management screen. The customer is sold 'user blocks' as a safety feature they literally cannot use from the UI. Either add the block button + blocked-list surface or move these routes to Pro.
findings.detail: grep for blockUser/unblock/users/*/report/me/blocked in src+assets returns no callers. is_blocked_either_way is consumed only server-side by Messaging and ActivityService.

findings.title: mvs_reports rows orphan when their target media is deleted
findings.location: includes/Repository/MediaRepository.php:2063 delete_cascade() — deletes 12 mvs_* tables, omits mvs_reports
findings.customer_impact: Deleting a reported media item leaves its report rows behind forever. Over time mvs_reports fills with rows pointing at media that no longer exists; the Pro report queue (and any count_by_status badge) shows phantom pending reports the owner can never clear by acting on the media. User-deletion already cleans reports correctly — media-deletion is the gap.
findings.detail: UserDeletionService::handle_user_deletion (lines 84-104) deletes reports both as reporter and as user-target, but neither delete_cascade nor any mvs_media_deleted listener removes target_type='media' reports.

findings.title: Report dialog never captures the user's detail text; reason labels not internationalized
findings.location: src/blocks/media-social/view.js:586-650 (details hardcoded line 623; reason labels lines 593-602)
findings.customer_impact: The report flow shows only a reason dropdown and always sends details:'Reported via media page' — the moderator never sees why the reporter flagged it, even though the API and DB store a details field. findings.detail: No textarea is wired into the report confirm dialog (the textarea at line 370 belongs to a different action). REASONS labels bypass wp.i18n.

findings.title: Moderation menu hidden from Editors who can otherwise moderate

findings.detail: render_page() and the REST permission both accept moderate_mvs_media; only the menu registration uses the stricter manage_options.

findings.title: AI moderation queue stays empty unless a paid external AI provider is configured
findings.location: includes/Core/Plugin.php:845 maybe_queue_ai (returns if no active provider); includes/Services/AIService.php:178 (moderate_content needs provider + signed URL)
findings.customer_impact: The free Moderation page headlines 'AI Flagged' but AI moderation only runs when an OpenAI/Google Vision key + budget is set up. A free customer with no AI provider sees a permanently empty 'AI Flagged' tab and no indication that AI moderation requires external setup — looks broken. There is no manual 'send to AI' action in the free admin UI either (the /analyze route is dead).
findings.detail: handle_flagged auto-action (flag/hide/reject) only fires off mvs_media_flagged, which only fires from AIService::process when a provider returns unsafe.

findings.title: Report button surface coverage is inconsistent
findings.location: src/blocks/media-social/view.js:586 + templates/media-single.php:441 (only places reportMedia is wired)
findings.customer_impact: Members can report media only from the single-media page / media-social bar, not from the explore grid, media-grid, lightbox, or member-photos. Reporting feels arbitrary depending on where the member encountered the media.
findings.detail: reportMedia action exists only in media-social; other display surfaces render media without any report affordance.

findings.title: Moderation count badge transient never invalidated on approve/reject
findings.location: includes/Admin/ModerationQueue.php:44-47 (60s transient, no delete on action)
findings.customer_impact: After approving or rejecting items, the menu 'awaiting moderation' badge can show a stale count for up to 60 seconds. Cosmetic.
findings.detail: set_transient('mvs_moderation_counts', ...,60) is never cleared in handle_actions().

overcooked_items: The 6-route mvs/v1/moderation REST controller — fully built (queue, counts, approve, reject, analyze, ai/usage) with permissions and schema, but consumed by nothing in free. It duplicates the admin form-POST flow. Either back the admin UI with it or delete it.
The /users/{id}/report, /users/{id}/block (POST+DELETE), and /me/blocked routes ship in free with no UI — abstraction the free customer can't reach. Move to Pro or expose UI.

is_blocked / is_blocked_either_way / has_reported / count_by_status form a fairly large service API where free only exercises a few methods — fine to keep for Pro, but it inflates the free attack/maintenance surface for capabilities the free customer can't use.
missing_for_complete_solution: A free admin surface to view and resolve user/media reports (mvs_reports). Today they are collected but unreadable without Pro — guaranteed support ticket: 'where do reported items show up?'
A frontend block-user button + a 'Blocked users' management list. The block engine is built and enforced but unreachable from the free UI.
Cleanup of mvs_reports when target media is deleted (add to delete_cascade or an mvs_media_deleted listener).

A free path for the AI Flagged tab to make sense without a paid AI provider — either hide/explain the tab when no provider is configured, or add a manual 'Analyze with AI' / manual-flag action (the /analyze route already exists but is dead).
Capturing the reporter's free-text details in the report dialog, and i18n of the reason labels.
Aligning the Moderation menu capability (manage_options) with the actual moderation capability (moderate_mvs_media) so delegated moderators can find the page.
Report affordance on the other media surfaces (explore grid, lightbox, member-photos) for consistency.

feature.name: Messaging / DM (conversations, transport, group conversations)
feature.entry: Messaging/ (MessagingService, MessagingController, RestPollingTransport), mvs_conversations/mvs_messages tables
feature.note: ANOTHER TEAM is actively reworking group conversations on this branch — report findings but tag them as possibly in-flight; do not treat unfinished group-conversation work as a bug.

audit.feature: Messaging / DM (conversations, transport, group conversations) — free
audit.verdict_reason: The 1:1 DM engine is largely complete and well-wired: 21 REST routes, all consumed by the Interactivity-API JS, with solid privacy gates on read paths (poll endpoint mirrors get_conversation()'s participant check, block-checks on create+send, request/accept/decline flow, unsend window, reactions, GDPR export/erase, user-deletion cascade). But it ships two customer-visible gaps that read as half-cooked: (1) a DUPLICATE new_message notification on every DM because both NotificationService::on_message and NotificationListener::on_message_sent hook mvs_message_sent at priority 10 and both insert a row — the listener's mute-check + 30s coalescing is bypassed by the unguarded NotificationService path; (2) the conversation LIST has server-side pagination but the JS only ever fetches page 1 (per_page=20) with no Load More / infinite scroll and no X-WP-Total header — a user with >20 active conversations silently cannot reach the older ones. This is the exact "Load More missed a surface" class the cycle is hunting. Group-conversation service methods exist with zero Free consumers (in-flight, not counted as a bug). Per-user transient keys also slip past the Rule #16 cardinality gate.

api.notes: 21 routes registered in MessagingController, all under mvs/v1, all permission_callback => check_auth (require logged-in) which is correct for private DM. Input args declared with types/enums/min-max on list/create/send/poll. Block-checks on POST /conversations and POST /messages. Error responses are actionable and status-mapped (404/403/429/410/500). GOOD. Gaps: (1) list_conversations (GET /me/conversations) and list_messages emit NO X-WP-Total / X-WP-TotalPages headers despite server-side pagination — dishonest pagination; clients can't know if more pages exist. (2) The whole group-conversation surface (create_group_conversation, get_or_create_channel, add/remove_participant, set_participant_role, rename_conversation) lives in MessagingService with NO REST route and NO Free consumer — dead API for Free (tagged in-flight, another team reworking groups). (3) update_conversation PATCH and several POST routes (read, typing, accept, decline, delete) declare no 'args' schema — acceptable since they take no body, but PATCH reads raw get_json_params() with only per-field whitelisting in the service. (4) upload_attachment validates real MIME via finfo + 10MB cap + temporary upload_files grant — solid, but returns 500 for a wp_handle_upload error that is often user-caused (disk full / bad file) rather than server fault.

dataflow.notes: Entry->controller->MessagingService->custom mvs_* tables is clean; 4 dedicated tables (conversations, participants, messages, message_reactions) all $wpdb->prepare'd. Privacy: every read path (get_conversation, list_messages, poll) joins participants and gates by user_id; poll explicitly returns identical shape on non-participant to avoid existence leak (WMV-02 fix). User-deletion cascade (UserDeletionService) purges mvs_conversation_participants + mvs_messages for the deleted user. GDPR export/erase implemented. GAPS: (1) DUPLICATE notification logic — NotificationService::on_message AND NotificationListener::on_message_sent both consume mvs_message_sent and both call create('new_message'); create() has no dedup, so two rows per DM. NotificationService eagerly inits at rest_api_init (register_rest_routes resolves 'notifications'), so on_message is registered before any send and DOES fire. (2) mvs_message_reactions is NOT in the user-deletion cascade table list — a deleted user's reactions on others' surviving messages are orphaned. (3) Direct mvs_conversations rows are intentionally retained on user deletion (documented in GDPRService) but no orphan-conversation cleanup when ALL participants are gone. (4) Per-entity transients: mvs_dm_unread_{uid}, mvs_dm_msg_rate_{uid}, mvs_dm_convo_rate_{uid}, mvs_dm_dup_{uid}, mvs_dm_notif_{conv}_{uid} use string-concat keys that evade the Rule #16 grep gate (which only matches inline $user_id), so they pass CI but still write per-user rows to wp_options on sites with no persistent object cache. (5) update_online_status writes user_meta on EVERY poll (3s) and every unread-count call — write amplification. (6) get_media_share_data returns title+permalink for ANY existing media_id with no can_view check (only the thumbnail is privacy-gated).

ux.notes: Surfaces: (a) slide-out chat panel in wp_footer (chat-panel.php) gated by mvs_chat_panel_visibility setting (everywhere/mvs_pages/bp_pages/disabled) + mvs_should_render_chat_panel filter — settings take effect, correctly suppressed on /messages/ full page and when BuddyNext owns DM; (b) dedicated /messages/ full-page template via rewrite, two-column, auth_redirect for logged-out; (c) unread badge polling on all logged-in pages. Empty states present (chat-list 'No conversations yet', messages.php 'Select a conversation'). Mobile: messaging.css has 767px breakpoint with data-active-conv toggle collapsing sidebar<->main, 44px tap targets on composer/voice/send. JS wiring is end-to-end (every apiFetch path maps to a registered route; accept/decline/mute/pin/archive/delete/unsend/reactions/typing all wired). GAPS: (1) Conversation list shows only the first 20 — loadConversations() always fetches /me/conversations?tab=X (page 1) with no Load More, no scroll-pagination; users with >20 active threads lose access to older ones with no UI hint. (2) Group-conversation UI does not exist in Free (in-flight). (3) Online-status + typing degrade silently to off when no persistent object cache (typing stored in wp_cache only) — acceptable but undocumented for the customer. (4) Duplicate notifications surface as two bell entries / two emails per DM (customer-visible).

findings.title: Every DM creates TWO new_message notifications (duplicate handler on mvs_message_sent)
findings.customer_impact: Members get two notifications (and potentially two emails) for a single direct message. The dedicated NotificationListener path applies a mute check and 30-second coalescing; the NotificationService::on_message path applies neither, so muting a conversation does NOT stop the duplicate, and rapid-fire messages are not coalesced. Looks broken/spammy to end users.

findings.title: Conversation list capped at first 20 — no Load More on any surface
findings.customer_impact: A user with more than 20 active conversations can never reach the 21st-and-older threads in either the slide-out panel or the /messages/ full page. There is no Load More button, no infinite scroll, and no on-screen indication that conversations are hidden. Heavy DM users will open support tickets saying 'my old chats disappeared'.

findings.title: List endpoints emit no X-WP-Total / X-WP-TotalPages headers
findings.customer_impact: Clients (and any third-party integrating with mvs/v1) cannot tell how many conversations/messages exist or whether more pages are available, so they cannot build correct pagination. This is also what blocks a clean Load More fix for the conversation list.

findings.title: Message reactions are not cleaned up on user deletion
findings.customer_impact: When an account is deleted, its rows in mvs_message_reactions (reactions the user left on other people's messages) are left behind, orphaned to a non-existent user_id. Over time this bloats the table and can show ghost reaction counts. mvs_conversation_participants and mvs_messages are cleaned, but mvs_message_reactions was missed.

findings.title: Per-user DM transients evade the Rule #16 cardinality gate
findings.customer_impact: On the many customer sites without a persistent object cache, every active messaging user writes per-user rows (mvs_dm_unread_*, mvs_dm_msg_rate_*, mvs_dm_convo_rate_*, mvs_dm_dup_*, mvs_dm_notif_*) into wp_options. The CI rule that should catch this only matches inline $user_id, so concatenated keys ($prefix . $user_id) pass the gate. Short TTLs limit accumulation but the rate/dup keys churn on every send; on busy sites this is real wp_options pressure the rule was written to prevent.

findings.title: Shared media preview leaks title + permalink without a privacy check
findings.customer_impact: When a message references a media_id, the recipient always receives the media title, permalink, and type for any existing media — only the thumbnail image is privacy-gated. If a shared item is private/restricted, its title and URL still surface in the message payload to anyone who can read the conversation.

findings.title: update_online_status writes user_meta on every poll/unread tick
findings.customer_impact: Presence is updated by an UPDATE to usermeta on every 3s poll and every unread-count call for every online user. On a site with many concurrent users this is constant write load on wp_usermeta with no throttle (e.g. only writing when >60s stale). Performance-only; no functional break.

findings.title: upload_attachment returns HTTP 500 for user-caused upload errors
findings.customer_impact: A failed wp_handle_upload (often a user/file/disk issue) returns 500 Server Error, which the client surfaces as a generic failure rather than an actionable 'file could not be uploaded' message. Minor; the message text is passed through but the status code mislabels the cause.

findings.title: Group-conversation engine has no Free REST/UI consumer (in-flight)
findings.customer_impact: Six public group methods (create_group_conversation, get_or_create_channel, add/remove_participant, set_participant_role, rename_conversation) plus Migrator v17 schema ship in Free with no route or UI that calls them. Tagged as in-flight per audit context (another team is reworking group conversations) — not a defect today, but it is dead surface in the Free build until the consumer lands. Flagging so it is not forgotten before release.

missing_for_complete_solution: Load More / infinite scroll on the conversation list so users with >20 threads can reach older conversations (paired with X-WP-Total headers on /me/conversations)
De-duplication of the new_message notification: one handler should own DM notifications, or create() needs a short-window dedup so mute + coalescing are always honored
mvs_message_reactions added to the user-deletion cascade in UserDeletionService
Orphan-conversation cleanup when every participant of a conversation has been deleted (mvs_conversations rows currently retained forever)
Privacy gate (can_view) on get_media_share_data so private shared-media title/permalink isn't exposed to conversation readers
Customer-facing note that typing indicators + online presence require a persistent object cache, since they silently no-op without one
Honest X-WP-Total pagination headers across the messaging list endpoints
overcooked_items: Two parallel notification consumers for mvs_message_sent (NotificationService::on_message and NotificationListener::on_message_sent) — collapse to a single owner; the duplicate is both complexity and a bug

Full group-conversation CRUD (admin/member roles, container channels, participant cap, v17 migration) shipped in Free ahead of any consumer — fine if the group rework lands this cycle, but it is currently weight the Free customer gains nothing from; keep it gated/clearly in-flight rather than half-exposed

feature.name: BuddyPress integration (activity sync/content, profile+group tabs, privacy filter)
feature.entry: Integrations/BuddyPress/ (ActivitySyncIntegration, ActivityContentIntegration, ActivityPrivacyFilter, ProfileTabIntegration, GroupTabIntegration, ActivityFormIntegration, MediaDisplayHelper)
feature.note: show_hidden skip bug just fixed in ActivityPrivacyFilter — check for remaining BP query paths that bypass it (heartbeat, REST, embeds).

audit.feature: BuddyPress integration (activity sync/content, profile+group tabs, privacy filter) — wpmediaverse (free)
audit.verdict_reason: The activity-stream privacy filter is genuinely solid post-fix: hooking bp_activity_get_where_conditions + bp_activity_get_join_sql + the count SQL covers EVERY BP query path that flows through BP_Activity_Activity::get() — sitewide, profile, group, the buddypress/v1 REST controller, RSS feeds, BP Nouveau heartbeat/load-more, and oEmbed. The audit's stated worry (heartbeat/REST/embed bypass) does not hold; there is no raw activity-query bypass and no remaining show_hidden skip. But the SAME privacy class of bug the team just fixed on the ProfileTab grid was NOT carried to the GroupTab grid: GroupTabIntegration::fetch_media_ids() runs raw SQL with zero privacy gate, and the shared render_media_grid()/render_grid_item() path has no per-item can_view check, so members/friends/private/group media leak as ghost cards (title, permalink, stats) to non-members and logged-out visitors of any public group. Compounding it, Load More on a group Media tab is mis-wired — it calls mvs/v1/media with no group filter and loads sitewide media instead of the group's. Activity-stream gating is also over-restrictive for group/custom levels (group members can't see group-privacy activities). So: API mostly fine, activity data-flow right-sized, but the tab surfaces are half-cooked in exactly the leak/wiring dimension this cycle is supposed to close.

api.notes: No dedicated BP REST routes are registered by this feature — correct, since BP activity is read through BuddyPress core's own buddypress/v1 controller, which the ActivityPrivacyFilter transparently gates via bp_activity_get_where_conditions/join_sql. The BP tabs reuse existing mvs/v1 routes (mvs/v1/media for Load More, mvs/v1/albums for create/edit/delete) rather than inventing parallel endpoints — good reuse, not over-built. Two API problems, both wiring rather than missing routes: (1) mvs/v1/media has NO 'group' filter param (MediaController.php:271-390 has no get_param('group') in the list query), so the GroupTab Load More button (BaseBPTabIntegration::render_load_more, data-endpoint=media with empty data-scope/data-author) loads sitewide media, not group media — a frontend call with no matching server filter. (2) mvs/v1/media list privacy (MediaController.php:308-314) still uses the pre-1.6.0 'public OR members OR own' logic, which diverges from the new viewer-aware 'profile' mode in MediaRepository::query_by_author (friends gating) — so a friend's friends-level items show on the profile tab's server-rendered page 1 but vanish from Load More pages. mvs/v1/albums delete/edit are wired end-to-end (bp-actions.js -> apiDelete -> route). No __return_true abuse in this feature's surface.

dataflow.notes: Activity write path is thorough and right-sized: record_upload_activity / attach_media_to_activity / emit_album_gallery_activity all (a) skip the insert entirely for private (zero public footprint, Basecamp #9936622656), (b) set hide_sitewide for private as defense-in-depth, and (c) persist _mvs_activity_privacy + _mvs_activity_privacy_level meta that ActivityPrivacyFilter reads. Delete cleanup is genuinely complete — clean_activities_for_media() removes the standalone upload activity, item_id/secondary_item_id matches, and surgically edits _mvs_media_ids for multi-media activities (dropping the activity only when it was the sole attachment). ActivityMediaLinkage drops linkage rows on bp_before_activity_delete. privacy-changed sync (sync_activity_privacy) fans out to per-media + album-gallery activities. THE GAPS: (1) GroupTabIntegration::fetch_media_ids (lines 105-145) is a raw COUNT/SELECT on mvs_media_index JOIN mvs_media_meta WHERE group_id with status='publish' and NO privacy WHERE and NO viewer gate — the read path that ProfileTab fixed via count_visible_by_author()/query_by_author() was never applied to the group scope. (2) render_media_grid/render_grid_item (BaseBPTabIntegration:383, TemplateHelpers:785) gate only on status='publish', never on can_view — so the only thing protecting non-public group media is sign-time URL signing on the thumbnail , which still leaves the card shell + title + permalink + stats exposed. Compare render_albums_grid (BaseBPTabIntegration:462) which DOES call privacy->can_view per album — the media grid is the inconsistent sibling. (3) ActivityPrivacyFilter::build_where_clause (lines 206-237) has branches for public/members/friends/own but none for level 60 (group) or 90 (custom) for non-author viewers — group members cannot see group-privacy upload activities in the stream, an over-restriction. (4) Friend-list cache is 5-min TTL with no invalidation on friendship change (minor staleness).

ux.notes: Surfaces exposing this feature: (a) BP member profile Media tab + Albums subnav + single-album view; (b) BP group Media tab + inline Media/Albums sub-tabs + single-album; (c) BP activity stream (sitewide/profile/group) rendering of MVS media; (d) BP activity post-form 'Attach media' button + privacy dropdown; (e) BP notifications (bell). Empty states are present everywhere (render_empty_media/albums/single_album with owner vs visitor copy) — no silent blanks. Settings that control it take effect: mvs_allow_user_privacy gates the activity-form privacy dropdown, mvs_default_privacy preselects it, mvs_items_per_page drives pagination. The fix-landed-on-one-surface-not-others bug class (the #1 this cycle) recurs hard: the members-level profile leak fix (count_visible_by_author / query_by_author 'profile' mode) was applied to ProfileTab but NOT GroupTab — group Media tab still lists+shows non-public media to non-members/logged-out. The Load More fix (enqueuing mvs-load-more on BP screens, Basecamp #9941413137) was applied, but for the group scope the button has no group param so it loads the wrong media set entirely. Logged-out vs logged-in: activity stream and profile tab correctly gate; group tab does not. Mobile/390px structural risk: render_media_grid hardcodes mvs-cols-3 with no column reduction at the grid level (relies on bp-integration.css media queries); the inline-styled audio/video cards in MediaDisplayHelper use fixed max-height:400px and width:100% which is fine, but the group inline sub-tabs (<nav class=mvs-bp-sub-tabs>) and the upload dropzone need a 390px check for tap-target/overflow — flag, not block.

findings.title: Group Media tab leaks members/friends/private/group media to non-members and logged-out visitors
findings.customer_impact: On any PUBLIC BuddyPress group, anyone (including logged-out visitors) who opens the Media tab sees cards for every media uploaded with that group_id regardless of privacy — including members-only, friends-only, private, and group-only items. The thumbnail image itself is protected by URL signing (shows a placeholder), but the card shell leaks the media title, its permalink link, and view/reaction/comment counts. This is the exact members-level leak class the team just fixed for the profile tab (Basecamp #9941246549) — it was never applied to the group scope. A paying customer running private-ish content in public groups will report 'my members-only photos show up to logged-out users in the group.'

findings.title: render_media_grid / render_grid_item have no per-item privacy gate (only status check)
findings.customer_impact: The shared grid renderer used by BOTH tabs checks only status='publish' before emitting a card. ProfileTab is saved only because query_by_author() pre-filters the IDs by viewer; GroupTab passes raw IDs straight in. The sibling render_albums_grid() DOES call privacy->can_view() per album (line 462) — the media grid is the inconsistent one. Add a can_view() gate inside render_media_grid (or have GroupTab::fetch_media_ids route through the repository's viewer-aware query like ProfileTab) so no surface can ever list a media the viewer cannot see.

findings.title: Group Media tab 'Load More' loads sitewide media, not the group's media
findings.customer_impact: On a group Media tab, the first (server-rendered) page shows group media, but clicking 'Load More' calls mvs/v1/media with no group filter (GroupTab::load_more_data_attrs returns empty; the endpoint has no 'group' param at all) so it appends unrelated sitewide media. Customers see the group gallery suddenly fill with photos from other groups/users. Either add a group_id filter to mvs/v1/media (gated by membership for non-public group privacy) or disable Load More on the group tab and paginate server-side like the albums grid does.

findings.title: Group-privacy and custom-privacy upload activities are invisible to fellow group members in the activity stream
findings.customer_impact: build_where_clause() grants visibility for public(0), members(20), friends(40), and own(>=40), plus admins — but has NO branch for level 60 (group) or 90 (custom) for a non-author viewer. Since attach_media_to_group_activity() sets group media to privacy='group' (level 60), a group member browsing the group's activity stream cannot see other members' group-media upload activities; only the uploader and admins can. The group activity feed looks empty/broken to members even though uploads succeeded. Add a 'group' branch (visible to group members via a membership check or a group_id IN (...) subquery) and decide custom-level visibility, so group activity actually shows to the group.

findings.title: mvs/v1/media list privacy diverges from the new viewer-aware 'profile' mode used on page 1
findings.customer_impact: The profile tab's server-rendered first page uses MediaRepository 'profile' mode (friends-level items shown to friends, members to logged-in). The Load More button hits mvs/v1/media which uses the older 'public OR members OR own' logic — so a friend sees the author's friends-only items on page 1 but they disappear from Load More pages, and the friends gate is silently dropped. Inconsistent counts/contents between the initial render and pagination. Route Load More through the same viewer-aware profile privicy levels (or expose a 'profile'/author+viewer mode on the endpoint) so page 1 and page N agree.

findings.title: Friend-list cache (5 min) is not invalidated on friendship change
findings.customer_impact: get_friend_ids() caches the viewer's friend IDs for 5 minutes with no invalidation hook on friends_friendship_accepted/deleted. For up to 5 minutes after accepting a friend request, a viewer won't see newly-friended users' friends-only activities (or will still see a just-removed friend's). Low impact, self-heals, but a hook to clear the mvs_activity_privacy cache group on friendship transitions would make it correct.

findings.title: Group Media tab does not enforce group privacy/membership before listing
findings.customer_impact: add_group_tab() registers the Media subnav whenever bp_is_group() with no check on the group's status or the viewer's membership. BP core blocks non-members from hidden groups, but for PUBLIC groups every visitor reaches the Media tab and (combined with the missing per-item gate above) sees all group media. Even independent of the leak, customers running 'public group, members-only media' expect the media list itself to respect membership. Pair a membership/group-privacy check with the per-item privacy gate.

overcooked_items: Nothing materially over-built in this feature. The rtMedia/MediaPress/BuddyBoss legacy-HTML transform paths in ActivityContentIntegration (transform_rtmedia_content + the 5 fallback branches in enhance_activity_media_content) are heavy regex machinery, but they exist for real migration parity and the team already moved new writes to the structured ActivityMediaLinkage table — acceptable as a compatibility tail rather than over-engineering. The rtMedia-parity numeric privacy levels (0/20/40/60/80/90) are justified by the documented import-intent-preservation goal.
missing_for_complete_solution: A per-item privacy gate on the shared BP tab media grid (render_media_grid/render_grid_item) OR routing GroupTab::fetch_media_ids through a viewer-aware repository query the way ProfileTab does — so the group tab cannot list non-public media to unauthorized viewers.
A group filter on mvs/v1/media (membership-gated) so the group tab's Load More returns the group's media, not sitewide media — or server-side pagination on the group tab.
A 'group' (and a decision on 'custom') visibility branch in ActivityPrivacyFilter::build_where_clause so group members can actually see group-media activities in the stream.
Alignment of mvs/v1/media list privacy with the 1.6.0 'profile' viewer-aware levels so profile-tab page 1 and Load More pages return the same set (friends gating included).
A friendship-change cache-bust for the mvs_activity_privacy friend-list cache.

A documented note/setting for what 'group' privacy means on the profile tab (currently group/custom items are owner-only in profile listings, which may surprise customers who expect group members to see them).

feature.name: Stats & views (per-media stats, admin stats page, aggregates)
feature.entry: Services/StatsService.php, Services/AdminAggregatesService.php, REST StatsController, Admin/StatsPage.php, mvs_media_views + mvs_media_stats tables, view-retention cron

audit.feature: Stats & views (per-media stats, admin stats page, aggregates) — free
audit.verdict_reason: The core loop works end-to-end for the common case: views/downloads are recorded via REST, aggregated into mvs_media_stats, surfaced on the admin Stats page, the media-stats block, the single-media/lightbox view counters, and exported to CSV — with a privacy gate on the public per-media endpoint and a bounded-growth retention cron. But it is simultaneously HALF-COOKED in two customer-visible ways (aggregate counts drift permanently inflated after a user is deleted; the media-stats block renders a silent blank for logged-out visitors, breaking the plugin's own Rule #11) and OVERCOOKED internally (the same insert-view-row + increment-stat logic is copy-pasted across four classes, one of which — StatsService::record_download — is dead code never called). No extensibility hook fires on a view/download despite the manifest's emphasis on transition hooks, and the public stats endpoints ship without the get_item_schema() that Coding Rule #6 mandates.

api.notes: Routes: GET mvs/v1/media/{id}/stats (public, __return_true) — intentional public counter, BUT it DOES apply a real privacy gate via PrivacyService::can_view and 404s on missing media, so __return_true is acceptable here and the inline comment documents the 2026-05-01 triage. GET mvs/v1/me/stats (is_user_logged_in) — correct. POST media/{id}/view and media/{id}/download (both __return_true) — intentional anonymous tracking, rate-limited (60/min views, 30/min downloads) and privacy-gated via can_view; download additionally honors the global mvs_allow_downloads toggle. Consumers verified: media-social/view.js and shared-ui/view.js both GET /stats; media-social/view.js POSTs /view. So no dead routes and no broken wiring on the read side. PROBLEMS: (1) StatsController defines NO get_item_schema()/get_public_item_schema() — violates Coding Rule #6 ('Every endpoint must define get_item_schema()'). (2) Response shape inconsistency: GET /media/{id}/stats returns {media_id,views,downloads,reactions,comments,shares,updated_at} but GET /me/stats returns a different shape {total_media,total_views,total_downloads,...} with no 'me' wrapper — two stat endpoints in the same namespace with divergent key names (views vs total_views). A client can't reuse one parser. (3) No pagination on any stats route (none needed — both are single-object reads), so pagination headers are a non-issue. (4) record_view returns {recorded:true} with no echo of the new count, so the JS counter can't optimistically update without a second round-trip to /stats.

dataflow.notes: Write path: MediaController::record_view inserts into mvs_media_views + upserts mvs_media_stats (ON DUPLICATE KEY) — correct and atomic-ish. Download path is forked: MediaController::record_download (REST), SignedUrlService::record_download (private, the /serve route), AND a third StatsService::record_download that is DEAD (grep confirms zero callers). Plus MediaRepository exposes init_stats/increment_stat/set_stat/record_event as a fourth parallel implementation. That is 4 copies of 'insert view row + bump stat column' — a Rule #14 (siblings with duplicate bodies share a base) and Rule-3/16 spirit violation; the canonical owner should be MediaRepository, with the controllers and SignedUrlService delegating. Cleanup on DELETE: media delete via MediaRepository::delete_cascade DELETEs both mvs_media_stats and mvs_media_views rows for that media (lines 2089-2090) — GOOD. User delete via UserDeletionService cascades owned media then DELETEs mvs_media_views WHERE user_id — but it NEVER recomputes mvs_media_stats, so every view/download a deleted user contributed to OTHER owners' media stays counted forever. The raw evidence rows vanish (so a recount is impossible) while the aggregate stays inflated — permanent drift, exactly the 'writes have matching cleanup on delete' miss the brief warns about. Privacy gates: read paths (/media/{id}/stats, record_view) both call PrivacyService::can_view — GOOD. The admin Stats page and media-stats block are owner/admin-scoped (block requires login + filters to post_author = current user; admin page requires manage_options/upload_mvs_media) — GOOD, no members-level leak. Caching: AdminAggregatesService::total_views is remember_persistent (object cache + daily transient fallback) and is ONLY busted on mvs_media_uploaded/mvs_media_deleted (CacheService lines 413-414), NOT on a view/download. On a site WITHOUT persistent object cache, the admin 'Total Views' card can lag real views by up to 24h. Hooks: NO do_action fires on a view or download (only mvs_stats_tabs admin filter + mvs_moderation_changed exist) — a Pro/3rd-party can't react to 'media viewed' for streaks, trending, gamification. Retention: ViewRetentionService cron (daily, mvs_purge_old_views) batches DELETE in 50k chunks on the created_at index — well-built and bounded; duplicated by StatsService::prune_views used only by WP-CLI (two retention implementations, but both reachable).

ux.notes: Surfaces enumerated: (1) Admin Stats page (Media > Stats) — date-range tabs Today/Week/Month/All, stat cards, Top Media table with permalink, AI Usage widget, CSV export (nonce + cap checked). Empty state present ('No Stats Yet'). Solid.
