One inconsistency: the date-range cards filter media by created_at, NOT by when the VIEW happened — so 'Today / This Week' shows views on media CREATED in that window, which is NOT what a customer reading 'Views this week' expects. That is a meaning bug, not just polish: a viral old photo viewed heavily this week shows 0 under 'This Week'. (2) media-stats Gutenberg block — owner dashboard widget; BUT render.php line 17 does a BARE `return;` when !is_user_logged_in(), producing a silent blank div for logged-out visitors. Violates the plugin's own Rule #11 (every render return must pair with a visible empty state via render_block_empty_state). If an owner drops this block on a public page, anonymous visitors see nothing/blank. (3) Per-media view counter — rendered in media-social block + lightbox (shared-ui) from GET /stats; works logged-in and logged-out (endpoint is public). (4) No shortcode equivalent of the media-stats block (block-only), so classic-editor / shortcode-page sites cannot surface the owner stats widget — the exact 'fix landed on one surface, missed shortcode' class the brief flags. (5) media-stats block ships heavy INLINE styles (raw hex #f8f9fa/#666, fixed px) instead of design-system tokens/classes — DS drift; the auto-fit minmax(140px,1fr) grid is responsive at 390px so no hard overflow risk, but it is unmaintainable and ignores dark mode. Settings: mvs_view_retention_days is wired (registrar + sanitize + cron) and its description correctly tells the customer aggregates are unaffected — good. No setting controls WHICH events count or lets an owner reset/recount a media's stats — a support-ticket gap once drift appears.

findings.title: User deletion permanently inflates view/download aggregates (no recount)
findings.customer_impact: When an admin deletes a member, that member's raw view/download rows are removed from mvs_media_views but the per-media Total Views/Downloads in mvs_media_stats are never decremented. Every other creator's view counts stay permanently too high, and because the evidence rows are gone the numbers can never be reconciled. Owners will email support asking why their view count went up after a user was removed, or doesn't match reality.

findings.title: media-stats block renders a silent blank for logged-out visitors
findings.customer_impact: If a site owner places the Media Stats block on a page that logged-out visitors can reach, those visitors see an empty blank space with no message. Violates the plugin's own no-silent-render rule. The owner thinks the block is broken and opens a ticket.

findings.title: Dead code: StatsService::record_download() is never called
findings.customer_impact: A full download-recording method (insert + increment) sits in the canonical StatsService but every real download path uses MediaController::record_download or SignedUrlService::record_download instead. Maintenance hazard: a future dev fixing download tracking may 'fix' the dead copy and see no effect, or the two live copies will drift apart. No direct customer symptom yet, but it is the seed of an inconsistency bug.

findings.title: Four parallel implementations of 'record view/download + bump stat'
findings.customer_impact: The same SQL (insert into mvs_media_views, increment mvs_media_stats) is copy-pasted across four classes. Rate-limiting, the ON DUPLICATE KEY upsert guard, and the event_type values are NOT consistent across them (MediaController uses upsert; SignedUrlService assumes the stats row already exists and does a plain UPDATE that silently no-ops if init_stats was never run). A download via /serve on media whose stats row doesn't exist increments nothing, so cloud-served private-media downloads can under-count.

findings.title: Admin 'Total Views' card never busts cache on a new view
findings.customer_impact: AdminAggregatesService caches Total Views and only invalidates it on media upload/delete, not when a view is recorded. On the many customer sites without a persistent object cache (the daily-transient fallback path), the admin Stats 'Total Views' figure can be up to 24 hours stale and will appear 'stuck' to the owner.

findings.title: No do_action hook fires when media is viewed or downloaded
findings.customer_impact: Pro and third-party add-ons (trending feeds, view streaks, gamification, webhooks) have no way to react to a view or download because no mvs_media_viewed / mvs_media_downloaded action is emitted. The manifest advertises transition hooks as a core extensibility promise; stats is a blind spot. Customers wanting 'notify me / award points on view' must patch core.

findings.title: StatsController defines no item schema
findings.customer_impact: Both stats routes ship without get_item_schema(), violating Coding Rule #6. The /wp-json/mvs/v1 index advertises no field documentation for stats, and headless/integrator customers building against the API get no machine-readable contract — more support questions and brittle integrations.

findings.title: Stats response shapes diverge between /media/{id}/stats and /me/stats
findings.customer_impact: Per-media stats return keys like views/reactions while user stats return total_views/total_reactions. An integrator can't share one parser across the two endpoints in the same namespace. Cosmetic for end users but a real friction point for the developers we sell the API to.

findings.title: Admin Stats date-range filters by media creation date, not view date
findings.customer_impact: The Today/This Week/This Month buttons filter on when media was CREATED, not when views occurred. An owner reading 'Total Views — This Week' actually sees lifetime views of media uploaded this week, and a heavily-viewed older item shows zero. The label promises time-windowed view analytics the data doesn't deliver.

findings.title: media-stats block uses raw inline hex/px styling, ignores design tokens and dark mode
findings.customer_impact: Stat cards are styled with hard-coded #f8f9fa/#666 inline styles instead of the shared design system, so they ignore the site's dark mode and theme accent and look off-brand on many sites. Responsive at 390px (auto-fit grid) so no overflow, but visually inconsistent with every other plugin surface.

findings.title: Owner stats widget is block-only — no shortcode parity
findings.customer_impact: Sites using the classic editor or page builders that rely on shortcodes have no way to place the 'my media stats' dashboard widget, unlike several other features that ship both a block and a shortcode. Customers on classic-editor stacks can't surface their own stats on the front end.

overcooked_items: StatsService::record_download() — dead method, never called; delete it and route all download recording through one owner (MediaRepository).

Four parallel view/download recording implementations (MediaController, SignedUrlService, StatsService, MediaRepository) — collapse to a single MediaRepository::record_event + increment_stat that everyone delegates to; the controllers should not hand-write the INSERT/UPDATE SQL.
Two retention implementations — ViewRetentionService::purge (cron) and StatsService::prune_views (CLI) duplicate the bounded-delete logic; have the CLI command call the service used by cron.

StatsService as a class is nearly vestigial: get_for_media duplicates MediaRepository::get_stats (same SELECT), get_for_user duplicates the media-stats block's user-aggregate query. Consider folding StatsService's reads into MediaRepository/AdminAggregatesService and keeping the controller thin.
missing_for_complete_solution: Recompute or zero per-media aggregates when a contributing user is deleted (or stop deleting the raw rows so a recount stays possible) — otherwise view/download counts are permanently wrong after any member removal.
A visible empty/login state for the media-stats block when logged out (Rule #11), and an empty state when the owner has zero media.
mvs_media_viewed / mvs_media_downloaded do_action hooks so Pro and integrations can react to engagement (trending, streaks, webhooks).
get_item_schema() on StatsController and a consistent response shape across /media/{id}/stats and /me/stats.

Cache invalidation of admin_total_views (and total_downloads if added) on view/download so the admin Total Views card is fresh on non-object-cache sites — or a documented note that it refreshes daily.
An admin 'recount stats for this media' / 'rebuild all stats from mvs_media_views' action (WP-CLI or row action) so owners can self-heal drifted counts instead of opening a ticket.
Make the admin Stats date-range actually window by view date (join mvs_media_views.created_at) or relabel the cards to make clear they filter by upload date.
A shortcode equivalent of the media-stats block for classic-editor / page-builder sites.
A downloads column on the admin Stats page and in AdminAggregates(currently downloads are tracked but never surfaced in the admin overview cards).

feature.name: AI features (auto-describe/tag, providers, budget caps)
feature.entry: Services/AIService.php, Services/OpenAIProvider.php, PRO Integrations/GoogleVision + Rekognition, AiSettingsRegistrar, Action Scheduler handle_ai_process

audit.feature: AI features (auto-describe/tag, providers, budget caps) — Free + Pro
audit.verdict_reason: The AI engine is well-built (clean provider abstraction, budget cap that also gates moderation, per-feature toggles, circuit breaker in Pro), but it is HALF-COOKED at the surface: the flagship "auto-describe / alt text" output (mvs_ai_description) is written to the DB and then never displayed, never used as image alt text, and never editable on any surface. The /analyze and /ai/usage REST routes have zero frontend consumers. There is no per-media surface to view, edit, accept, or re-run AI results, and no way to re-process media after enabling AI. Budget tracking is a flat per-call estimate that does not reflect real provider/model/token cost and is non-atomic. So the data flow and provider plumbing are RIGHT-SIZED, but the UX integration is HALF-COOKED — a paying customer turns on AI, pays OpenAI, and sees almost nothing for it.

api.notes: Two AI REST routes, both in ModerationController: POST mvs/v1/moderation/(id)/analyze (analyze_item) and GET mvs/v1/ai/usage (get_ai_usage). Both correctly gated by moderate_permissions_check() requiring the moderate_mvs_media capability (ModerationController.php:170-179) — no __return_true, privacy-correct. analyze_item validates the id exists (404 on missing) and returns a consistent {media_id, ai} shape. BUT: both routes are DEAD API — grep across assets/js, src, and all templates finds zero consumers. No 'Analyze' / 're-run AI' button exists in the moderation queue admin (ModerationQueue.php render_row only emits Approve/Reject forms, lines 462-474) and the StatsPage reads usage server-side via $this->ai->get_usage_stats() (StatsPage.php:329), not via the /ai/usage route. So a customer (or extension) has the endpoints but the product never calls them. The analyze route is also misplaced under /moderation rather than a media or ai namespace, and runs the full process() pipeline synchronously inside a REST request (can be a 30s+ blocking call against OpenAI with no async handoff).

dataflow.notes: Entry: mvs_media_uploaded -> Plugin::maybe_queue_ai (Plugin.php:839) gated on mvs_ai_auto_analyze + an available provider -> Action Scheduler as_enqueue_async_action('mvs_ai_process_media') (or synchronous fallback) -> handle_ai_process -> AIService::process(). process() respects per-feature toggles (auto_describe/auto_tag/auto_moderate), fires mvs_should_ai_analyze, mvs_ai_result, mvs_ai_moderation_result filters and mvs_media_flagged action — good extensibility. Results land in mvs_media_meta (ai_description, ai_tags, ai_confidence, ai_moderation, ai_status) which IS per-media meta and is cleaned up with the media row on delete (correct cardinality — not in options). Budget cap (check_budget) correctly gates analyze, auto_tag AND moderate (the 1.4.0 fix). Provider back-compat google->google_vision normalization on read is sound (AIService.php:49). CONCERNS: (1) mvs_ai_usage option accumulates one sub-array per calendar month forever with no pruning (AIService.php:333) — slow unbounded autoloaded-option growth. (2) check_budget reads the option then compares — non-atomic, so concurrent Action Scheduler workers can each pass the check and overshoot the monthly cap. (3) track_usage only adds cost on success, but a failed OpenAI call can still incur real spend the budget never sees. (4) No privacy gate before sending the image to an external provider — private/restricted media is shipped to OpenAI/Google/AWS over its signed URL with no owner opt-out per privacy level (only the global master switch). Pro circuit breaker correctly uses transients (global, not per-entity — correct cardinality).

ux.notes: Settings surface is complete and well-built: AiSettingsRegistrar exposes provider, OpenAI key+model, master auto-analyze switch, per-feature describe/tag/apply-tags/moderate toggles, monthly budget (conservative $10 default — good), and est. cost-per-call; Pro adds Google Vision key + AWS Rekognition keys/region. Free shows a tasteful Pro-upsell select for the extra providers. StatsPage surfaces calls/success/failed/cost/budget with a % bar. BUT the OUTPUT side is missing on every surface: (1) ai_description is written with a prompt that literally says 'for use as an alt text' (OpenAIProvider.php:50) yet media_thumbnail() falls back to the media TITLE for alt, never ai_description (TemplateHelpers.php:322-323) — the headline feature produces dead data. (2) No surface anywhere shows, lets you edit, or lets you accept/reject the AI description or tags on a media item — not the frontend edit modal, not the dashboard, not any admin media page (grep for ai_description/ai_tags in src/templates/assets = nothing). (3) No 'Run AI now' / 're-analyze' button anywhere, so a customer who enables AI after uploading media can never backfill existing media (no CLI command either). (4) auto_apply_tags writes to the mvs_tag taxonomy silently with no review step. (5) No OpenAI/Vision 'Test connection' button — the customer can't tell if their key works until uploads silently fail. (6) Moderation flags ARE surfaced (ModerationQueue AI Flags column) — that one path is wired. No 390px-specific risk since there's no AI-specific frontend UI to break.

findings.title: AI-generated description is written but never used or shown anywhere
findings.customer_impact: The flagship 'auto-describe / AI alt text' feature the customer pays OpenAI for produces a description that is saved to the database and then never rendered: image alt text falls back to the media title, and no admin or frontend surface displays or lets you edit the AI description. The customer enables AI, incurs API cost, and sees no description anywhere — a dead end that will generate 'where did my AI descriptions go?' support tickets.

findings.title: No surface to view, edit, accept, or re-run AI results on a media item
findings.customer_impact: There is no per-media UI anywhere (edit modal, dashboard, admin media list) to see the AI description/tags, correct them, or trigger analysis. The only AI output a customer ever sees is the moderation Flags column. People expect to review and tweak AI suggestions; here it is all-or-nothing and invisible.

findings.title: /analyze and /ai/usage REST routes have no frontend consumer (dead API)
findings.customer_impact: Two working, permission-correct endpoints ship but nothing in the product calls them — there is no 'Analyze' button and the stats page reads usage server-side instead. Customers get no manual re-analyze action; the routes are latent surface area with no payoff.

findings.title: No way to backfill AI on media uploaded before AI was enabled
findings.customer_impact: AI only runs on the mvs_media_uploaded hook for new uploads. A customer who turns on AI on an existing library can never process their back-catalog — no bulk action, no WP-CLI command, and the /analyze route has no UI. This is the single most common thing a buyer will ask support for after enabling the feature.

findings.title: Private/restricted media is sent to external AI providers with no per-privacy opt-out
findings.customer_impact: Every uploaded image, including private and restricted ones, is shipped over its signed URL to OpenAI/Google/AWS when auto-analyze is on. There is only a global master switch — no 'skip private media' control and no privacy notice. Community owners handling sensitive/private galleries have no granular control and a potential compliance surprise.

findings.title: Budget cost tracking is a flat per-call estimate, not real spend
findings.customer_impact: The monthly budget cap counts a flat mvs_ai_cost_per_call (default $0.01) per successful action regardless of provider, model (gpt-4o vs mini), token count, or image size — and a full pipeline run bills 3 separate calls. The dollar figure shown to the customer and the cap that stops spending can be far from the real OpenAI bill, so the 'hard cap' is only as honest as a guessed constant.

findings.title: Budget check is non-atomic — concurrent workers can overshoot the cap
findings.customer_impact: check_budget reads the usage option and compares without a lock, so several Action Scheduler jobs processing a burst of uploads can each pass the check before any writes back, pushing real spend past the monthly cap the owner set.

findings.title: mvs_ai_usage option grows one entry per month forever with no pruning
findings.customer_impact: Usage history accumulates indefinitely in a single autoloaded option. Harmless for years, but it is unbounded per-time-bucket data living in wp_options with no retention — minor bloat that nothing ever trims.

findings.title: No 'Test connection' for OpenAI / Vision / Rekognition keys
findings.customer_impact: The customer pastes an API key and has no way to verify it works; a bad key just causes silent failures on upload (analyze returns null, ai_status='failed') with no visible signal. They discover the problem only by noticing nothing happened.

findings.title: Pro Google Vision generate_tags has no failure de-dup / empty filtering parity with OpenAI
findings.customer_impact: GoogleVision returns raw lowercased label strings without the array_filter/array_unique/sanitize that OpenAIProvider applies, so empty or duplicate tags can reach wp_set_object_terms when auto-apply is on. Minor tag-quality inconsistency between providers.

overcooked_items: The /analyze and /ai/usage REST endpoints exist with full permission checks but no consumer — either wire a UI to them or drop them; right now they are abstraction with no customer payoff.

Three separate billable provider round-trips (analyze, generate_tags, moderate) per upload when GoogleVision/Rekognition could return labels+description+safe-search in fewer calls — the per-provider call count is higher than the job needs and inflates both latency and the (already inaccurate) budget counter.

mvs_ai_cost_per_call as a customer-facing setting is pseudo-precision: it presents a tunable dollar knob that cannot actually track real spend, adding a config field that buys the customer a false sense of accuracy.
missing_for_complete_solution: Use ai_description as the image alt text (and/or pre-fill the media description field) so the generated data actually does the job the prompt promises.
A per-media surface to view, edit, and accept/reject AI description and tags before they go live (especially before auto_apply_tags writes to the taxonomy).
A 'Run AI now' action and a bulk/CLI backfill so customers can process media uploaded before AI was enabled — the #1 expected workflow.
A privacy-aware gate or setting so owners can exclude private/restricted media from being sent to third-party AI, plus a clear notice that images are transmitted to OpenAI/Google/AWS.
'Test connection' buttons for the OpenAI key and the Pro Vision/Rekognition credentials so a bad key surfaces immediately instead of as silent upload failures.
Real or model-aware cost accounting (token/model/image-size based) so the monthly budget cap and the cost figure shown to customers reflect the actual provider bill.
Atomic budget reservation (or a small over-cap tolerance documented) so concurrent processing cannot blow past the spend limit.

feature.name: Admin settings & capabilities (settings groups, permissions matrix, setup wizard)
feature.entry: Admin/Settings/ (SettingsPage, SettingsRegistrar, FieldRenderer, PermissionsManager, Sanitizers), Capabilities/MediaCapabilities.php, Admin/SetupWizard.php
feature.note: Permissions matrix just reworked (fbf1c98) — audit the OTHER settings groups for save/effect wiring (a settings field that saves but nothing reads it = half-cooked).

audit.feature: Admin settings & capabilities (settings groups, permissions matrix, setup wizard) — free
audit.verdict_reason: The settings groups themselves are RIGHT-SIZED and dependable: every registered option I traced (General, Display, Social/DM, Storage, AI, Moderation, Webhooks, Pages) has a real consumer — there are no save-but-nobody-reads dead settings, and the file-types/webhook-secret/checkbox-default edge cases that historically wiped values are all handled with documented guards. The HALF-COOKED part is the capability surface: the Permissions matrix advertises and persists grantable caps (manage_mvs_settings, moderate_mvs_media) that the admin MENU registration ignores — every page menu is hard-gated on manage_options while the page render handlers accept the mvs_* caps. So an admin can grant a role Settings/Moderation access in the matrix, the cap is correctly stored, but that role sees no menu item and hits a feature that only works by guessing the direct URL. That is exactly the cross-surface miss this cycle keeps hitting. The Setup Wizard also writes display options through raw absint()/sanitize_text_field() instead of the canonical whitelist sanitizers, so it can persist out-of-range values the settings page would reject.

api.notes: This feature is admin-side (WP Settings API + admin-post), not REST. The two write paths are sound. PermissionsManager save: nonce verified (wp_verify_nonce 'mvs_save_role_caps') AND capability checked via current_user_can_save() (manage_mvs_settings OR manage_options hard fallback to avoid self-lockout, Basecamp #9937811664) at both the inline render-save and the admin_post_mvs_save_role_caps handler; mvs_form_roles sentinel correctly distinguishes 'role not rendered' from 'revoke all', and per-cell values are sanitize_key/sanitize_text_field'd. SetupWizard save: check_admin_referer + manage_options||manage_mvs_settings guard. No __return_true, no missing nonces. The options.php settings groups carry per-option sanitize_callback whitelists (Sanitizers::WHITELISTS) for every fixed-choice field, which SettingsContractTest introspects — stronger than typical.

dataflow.notes: Permissions matrix write is dual-pathed correctly: process_role_caps_save() applies grants/revokes to live wp_user_roles AND persists the full matrix to MediaCapabilities::OVERRIDES_OPTION, which add_caps()->apply_admin_overrides() re-applies LAST on every version-gated re-grant — so plugin updates no longer reset admin choices (the headline 1.6.0 fix, verified end-to-end in code). Plural CPT caps kept in sync via PLURAL_CAP_MAP on both save and re-apply. Every settings option I traced has at least one live get_option() consumer (UploadService, ModerationService, MessagingService, AIService, SignedUrlService, TemplateHelpers, WebhookService, ViewRetentionService, etc.) — no orphan settings. Privacy enforcement is honest at the upload write path: UploadService forces mvs_default_privacy when mvs_allow_user_privacy is off (server-side, not just UI hiding). The only UI-less registered options (mvs_cloud_direct_public_urls, mvs_comment_edit_window) are intentional and documented, and both are read. Cleanup-on-uninstall handled by remove_caps(); OVERRIDES_OPTION is not deleted on remove_caps but is harmless (re-applied only if present).

ux.notes: Surfaces exposing this feature: (1) Settings admin page with sidebar nav (general/display/social/storage/ai/permissions/webhooks) — wired end-to-end, card-based, Pro upsell + Pro-locked disabled fields for storage drivers/AI providers. (2) Permissions matrix tab — full role x cap grid covering ALL site roles (correct, since add_caps grants base caps to every role). (3) Setup Wizard (welcome/pages/display/done). The cross-surface MISS: the matrix grants manage_mvs_settings/moderate_mvs_media but the admin menu items (Settings, Moderation, All Media, Stats, Logs) are all registered with manage_options only, while their render handlers accept the mvs_* caps — granting the cap produces an invisible menu / direct-URL-only feature. Wizard display step uses raw sanitizers (bypasses whitelist) and offers only 2/3/4 columns vs settings' 2/3/4/5, and preselects items_per_page default 24 vs registered default 12. Mobile/390px: the permissions matrix is a wide multi-column <table> (10 cap columns x N roles) with no responsive wrapper visible in the markup — structural horizontal-overflow risk on phones; the file-types grid and settings cards look fluid by comparison.

findings.title: Permissions matrix grants caps the admin menu never honors (manage_mvs_settings / moderate_mvs_media)
findings.customer_impact: A site owner uses the Permissions tab to give an Editor (or shop-manager) the 'Manage Settings' or 'Moderate' capability. The cap is saved and survives updates, and the page even works if visited directly. But because every WPMediaVerse admin menu item is registered with manage_options, that role sees NO Settings/Moderation/All-Media/Stats menu link at all. The feature the matrix sold them is invisible. This is the same one-surface-fixed-others-missed class the team keeps hitting: the render guards were updated to accept mvs_* caps, the menu registration was not. Either gate the menus on the mvs_* caps too, or make the matrix honest about which caps only affect direct-URL access.

findings.title: Setup Wizard writes display options bypassing the canonical whitelist sanitizers
findings.customer_impact: The wizard saves mvs_grid_columns via raw absint() and mvs_thumbnail_style via raw sanitize_text_field(), instead of Sanitizers::sanitize_grid_columns (whitelist {2,3,4,5}) / sanitize_thumbnail_style (whitelist {square,original}). A tampered or scripted POST through the wizard can persist values the settings page would reject (e.g. 99 columns, an arbitrary thumbnail-style string), which then flow into the grid CSS and TemplateHelpers. Low real-world frequency (admin-only, nonce-gated) but it is a second, weaker write path to the same options — route it through the same sanitizers so there is one source of truth.

findings.title: Permissions matrix table has no responsive treatment — 390px horizontal overflow risk
findings.customer_impact: The matrix renders a plain <table class='mvs-recent-table mvs-caps-table'> with one Role column plus 10 capability columns, one row per site role. On a phone (the project's 390px done-criterion) that is far wider than the viewport with no scroll wrapper or stacked layout in the markup. Admins managing permissions on a tablet/phone get a clipped or overflowing grid. Needs a horizontal-scroll container or a responsive stacked variant to meet the project's mobile-is-part-of-done rule.

findings.title: Wizard column choices and items-per-page default drift from the settings page
findings.customer_impact: The wizard's Grid Columns dropdown offers only 2/3/4 while the Display settings offer 2/3/4/5, and the wizard preselects Items Per Page using get_option default 24 whereas the registered default is 12. A customer who picks '4' in the wizard then finds a '5' option later (mild surprise), and the wizard can show 24 selected on a fresh install that is actually defaulted to 12. Cosmetic, but it makes the two surfaces look like they disagree about the same setting.

findings.title: OVERRIDES_OPTION not cleared on remove_caps()/uninstall
findings.customer_impact: remove_caps() strips caps from roles but leaves mvs_role_caps_overrides in wp_options. On a deactivate-cap-strip then reactivate cycle, apply_admin_overrides() re-applies the stale matrix, which is the intended persistence behavior — but on a true uninstall this is orphaned option data. Harmless and arguably desirable for re-install continuity; flagging only for completeness so the uninstall story is a deliberate choice, not an oversight.

overcooked_items: Nothing materially overcooked. The settings architecture (5 focused classes + AiSettingsRegistrar, a WHITELISTS registry introspected by SettingsContractTest, a pre_update_option guard for the file-types add_option no-op, a hidden sentinel field to disambiguate empty-vs-absent) reads as heavy but each piece pays for a real, documented historical bug — it is defensive, not gratuitous abstraction.

The mvs_ai_cost_per_call setting plus the separate mvs_ai_monthly_budget is borderline: two numeric AI-cost knobs where most customers will only understand the budget cap. Could be simplified to a single budget with an internal cost estimate, but it is low-harm.
missing_for_complete_solution: Menu-level capability gating that matches the Permissions matrix: if you can grant manage_mvs_settings or moderate_mvs_media, those roles must get the corresponding menu items, otherwise the matrix is selling access that doesn't appear in the UI. This is the single biggest support-ticket risk in this feature.
A responsive/mobile layout for the permissions matrix (scroll wrapper or stacked rows) so admins can manage roles from a phone/tablet per the project's 390px rule.
Wizard write path should reuse Sanitizers (one source of truth) and align its column choices (add 5) and items-per-page default (12) with the settings page so the two surfaces never disagree.

No in-product explanation that some matrix caps only take effect on direct URLs / programmatic checks rather than menu visibility — a customer granting 'Manage Settings' to a non-admin role will reasonably expect a Settings menu to appear for them.

feature.name: Cleanup & GDPR (orphaned-file reclaim, account deletion, exports)
feature.entry: Services/StorageCleanupService.php, Services/GDPRService.php, mvs_media_files_orphaned + mvs_cleanup_media_files hooks, StorageService::delete_everywhere

audit.feature: Cleanup & GDPR (orphaned-file reclaim, account deletion, exports) — free
audit.verdict_reason: The 1.6.0 file-reclaim core (delete_cascade -> mvs_media_files_orphaned -> StorageCleanupService -> delete_everywhere) is genuinely right-sized and closes the real bytes-stranded bugs it was built for. But the GDPR/account-deletion data-erasure side is HALF-COOKED: two tables with user_id (mvs_message_reactions, plus reverse-side mvs_blocks.blocked_id in the GDPR path) survive a GDPR erase, mvs_transactions survives both paths while the privacy-policy text promises full removal, there is no actual orphaned-file *reclaim* sweep despite the feature name (only an event-driven hook with no recovery path for a permanently-failed Action Scheduler job or pre-1.6.0 stranded bytes), and Pro hooks none of it so Pro-owned per-user data is never purged.

api.notes: This feature is deliberately not a REST feature — it runs through WP core's privacy framework (wp_privacy_personal_data_exporters/erasers filters), WP lifecycle hooks (deleted_user, remove_user_from_blog), and Action Scheduler (mvs_cleanup_media_files). That is the correct surface choice; building custom REST routes for GDPR/cleanup would be overcooked. The one REST touchpoint, MediaController::delete_item (MediaController.php:910), correctly funnels through delete_all()->delete_cascade() so the orphan hook fires (MediaController.php:929) and has a real permission_callback (delete_item_permissions_check, line 1245) plus rate limiting. No dead API and no broken wiring found in this feature. mvs_user_data_purged (UserDeletionService.php:111) is fired for extensibility but currently has zero consumers — minor, it is a forward-looking hook.

dataflow.notes: File reclaim is solid: delete_cascade (MediaRepository.php:2063) reads every *_path meta via get_stored_file_paths (line 2117) BEFORE deleting rows, fires mvs_media_files_orphaned, and StorageCleanupService::process -> StorageService::delete_everywhere (StorageService.php:73) deletes from BOTH local and active cloud driver so migrated bytes are not stranded. Both delete entry points (REST delete + UserDeletionService phase 1) funnel through delete_cascade — no duplicate teardown logic. However the row-erasure side has coverage gaps (see findings): GDPR erase_social and UserDeletionService both omit mvs_message_reactions; GDPR erase_social omits the reverse-side mvs_blocks.blocked_id that UserDeletionService does clean (the two cleanup paths have drifted out of sync — exactly the 'fix landed on one path, missed the sibling' class); neither path touches mvs_transactions. Caching follows the cardinality rule (row_cache invalidation on trash/restore). The GDPR erase_media docblock says 'anonymize rather than delete' but the body hard-deletes via delete_cascade (GDPRService.php:336-375) — comment lies about behavior.

ux.notes: Surfaces: (1) WP Tools -> Export/Erase Personal Data — wired via GDPRService exporters/erasers, works. (2) WP Tools -> Privacy Policy suggested text (add_privacy_policy, GDPRService.php:388) — present but its promise ('all media files, social interactions, and associated metadata will be permanently removed') is FALSE given the table gaps and transactions retention, which is a compliance-risk statement for a paying site owner. (3) Account/user deletion in wp-admin Users — handled silently by deleted_user hook, no admin feedback. (4) The feature is NAMED 'orphaned-file reclaim' but there is NO admin page, dashboard tab, or CLI command that scans for and reclaims true orphans (files on disk/cloud whose media row is gone). wp mvs cleanup-local (Commands.php:1232) is a cloud-migration local-copy pruner, not an orphan reclaimer. So if an Action Scheduler delete job dies permanently, or a site upgraded from pre-1.6.0 (when account deletion deleted zero files, per StorageCleanupService.php:14-16), those stranded bytes have no recovery surface — the customer pays for storage forever with no tool to find them. No mobile/390px risk (no frontend UI).

findings.title: GDPR erase + account deletion both leave mvs_message_reactions rows orphaned
findings.customer_impact: When a member requests a GDPR data wipe OR their account is deleted, their DM message reactions (mvs_message_reactions.user_id) are never removed. The table is not in either cleanup map. The site owner believes the user is fully erased (the privacy policy says so) but personal interaction data persists — a real GDPR completeness gap and a support/compliance ticket waiting to happen.

findings.title: GDPR erase_social omits reverse-side mvs_blocks.blocked_id that account-deletion cleans — the two paths drifted
findings.customer_impact: UserDeletionService deletes rows where the user is the blocked target (mvs_blocks.blocked_id), but the GDPR eraser only deletes where they are the blocker. After a GDPR erase the user still appears as a 'blocked_id' in other members' block lists — residual personal data and inconsistent behavior between two flows that should erase identically. This is the exact 'fix landed on one surface, missed the sibling' class flagged for this cycle.

findings.title: No true orphaned-file reclaim surface despite the feature name
findings.customer_impact: Reclaim is purely event-driven off mvs_media_files_orphaned. There is no admin page or CLI command to scan disk/cloud for files whose media row no longer exists. Sites upgraded from pre-1.6.0 (when account deletion deleted no files at all) or any site where an Action Scheduler delete failed permanently keep paying for stranded bytes with zero tooling to find or reclaim them. A customer who notices ballooning storage has no self-serve answer.

findings.title: mvs_transactions retained on both GDPR erase and account deletion while privacy policy promises full removal
findings.customer_impact: Credit/monetization transaction rows tied to the user are never erased or exported. Financial-record retention may be intentional, but the suggested privacy-policy text states 'all media files, social interactions, and associated metadata will be permanently removed' — which is now untrue. Either erase/anonymize transactions or fix the policy text and document the retention basis, or the site owner ships a misleading privacy statement.

findings.title: Pro registers no GDPR exporters/erasers and does not hook deleted_user or mvs_user_data_purged
findings.customer_impact: On a Pro site, Pro-owned per-user data (quota counters, Pro tables, chapter/monetization rows) is not cleaned when a user is deleted or runs a GDPR erase, and is not included in the data export. The free side fires mvs_user_data_purged specifically so Pro could extend cleanup, but Pro never listens. Paying Pro customers get an incomplete erase/export.

findings.title: erase_media docblock claims 'anonymize rather than delete' but hard-deletes
findings.customer_impact: The method comment says media is anonymized; the body calls delete_cascade which permanently removes the media and fires file reclaim. Misleading to the next maintainer and to anyone auditing GDPR behavior from the docblock — risk of a wrong decision built on a false comment.

findings.title: Cloud delete failure relies on Action Scheduler retry but no retry/backoff is configured
findings.customer_impact: delete_everywhere lets a cloud delete exception propagate 'so Action Scheduler retries', but enqueue uses as_enqueue_async_action with no retry policy, and the inline fallback (no Action Scheduler) swallows nothing/has no retry at all. A transient CDN error during cleanup can permanently strand cloud bytes with no second attempt and no log of the failure — feeding the missing-orphan-reclaim gap above.

overcooked_items: mvs_user_data_purged action hook is fired with zero consumers anywhere in Free or Pro — either wire Pro to it (preferred, it solves the Pro-cleanup gap) or drop it until something needs it; right now it is speculative extensibility.
missing_for_complete_solution: mvs_message_reactions cleanup added to BOTH GDPRService::erase_social and UserDeletionService (single shared table-map would prevent future drift)
Reverse-side mvs_blocks.blocked_id cleanup added to GDPRService::erase_social to match UserDeletionService
A real orphaned-file reclaim tool: wp mvs reclaim-orphans (dry-run + commit) that scans disk/cloud for files with no matching media row, covering pre-1.6.0 sites and permanently-failed AS jobs
Decision + documentation on mvs_transactions retention, and corresponding correction of the privacy-policy suggested text so it does not over-promise
Pro GDPR exporters/erasers and a deleted_user / mvs_user_data_purged consumer so Pro per-user data is exported and erased
Shared single source of truth for the user-scoped table map consumed by both GDPRService and UserDeletionService, so a table added in one path can never be missed in the other
Admin-visible confirmation/logging when account-deletion file reclaim runs (and when a cloud delete fails), so owners can trust storage was actually reclaimed

feature.name: Gamification (challenges, battles, tournaments, boosts, streaks, leaderboard, compete hub)
feature.entry: Challenges/ Battles/ Tournaments/ Boosts/ Streaks/, REST CompeteSummaryController, blocks pro-battle/pro-challenge/pro-tournament/pro-leaderboard/pro-compete-hub, GamificationTemplateLoader, /compete/ rewrite
feature.note: Compete nav injection just removed (a9da475) — check feature discoverability still coherent for customers.

audit.feature: Gamification (challenges, battles, tournaments, boosts, streaks, leaderboard, compete hub) — wpmediaverse-pro
audit.verdict_reason: The gamification suite is broad and mostly wired end-to-end (REST routes, Interactivity-API stores, blocks, shortcodes, page templates, dashboard tabs, Explore banner all present and the JS-called routes all have matching server routes). But it ships three customer-visible correctness gaps that make it feel half-cooked in places: (1) the leaderboard aggregates a user's PRIVATE and members-only media into a PUBLIC score — the exact privacy-leak class this cycle is supposed to be closing; (2) the entire "spend points" economy (Boosts, streak freeze) silently bypasses the balance check and gives free boosts when wb-gamification isn't installed, with zero admin warning; (3) the /media/* gamification pages default-on (loader default '1') while every controller/service defaults off ('0'), so a fresh install serves broken challenge/battle/tournament pages whose JS hits unregistered 404 routes. No feature is over-engineered for the job; complexity is proportional. So: RIGHT-SIZED in scope, HALF-COOKED on a few load-bearing edges.

api.notes: Routes are consistent with mvs/v1 conventions: namespace mvs-pro/v1, X-WP-Total pagination headers, absint/sanitize_text_field on args, WP_Error with actionable status codes (404/400/409). Write routes correctly carry is_user_logged_in or admin (manage_options) permission_callbacks; public GET routes on challenges/battles/tournaments/active-summary use __return_true intentionally (public-by-design, triaged 2026-05-01) and that is defensible — no PII in those payloads. THREE issues: (1) CompeteSummaryController::get_public_item_schema() declares my_activity properties as activeBattles/challengeEntries/tournamentRegistrations (integers), but get_my_activity() actually returns battles/challenges/tournaments (arrays of objects) — schema lies to any API consumer and to wp-json discovery. (2) StreakController buy-freeze route registers UNCONDITIONALLY (Plugin.php:441) ignoring mvs_streaks_enabled, so a 'disabled' streaks feature still has a live spend-points endpoint. (3) On a fresh install the challenges/battles/tournaments GET routes are NOT registered (controllers gate on toggle default '0') yet the page templates render (loader default '1'), so the page's store fetch 404s — broken wiring at the default-state boundary. No dead routes otherwise; leaderboard is server-rendered (no REST needed).

dataflow.notes: Entry->service->mvs_competitions/_entries/_matches/mvs_boosts tables->media_repository for thumbs->Interactivity store output is coherent and Pro correctly queries only its own tables (the prior cross-plugin JOIN to Free's mvs_media_index was removed; thumbs now resolve via MediaRepository::get which returns '' for missing rows, so dangling media_id is rendered-safe). Hooks fired for extensibility on transitions (mvs_challenge_entry_submitted, mvs_activity_types registration, mvs_pro_leaderboard_xp_rows filter). BUT: (1) NO cleanup on media deletion for competition entries — the only mvs_media_deleted listener is for collections (Plugin.php:219). Deleting a media that is a challenge/battle/tournament entry leaves a dangling mvs_competition_entries.media_id row with its vote_count intact; a deleted-media battle can still 'win'. (2) NO user-deletion cleanup for any gamification table. (3) PRIVACY LEAK: LeaderboardRenderer::fetch_leaders() reactions/media_count queries filter only status='publish' AND moderation_status='approved' with NO privacy='public' gate — Free's MediaRepository explicitly gates privacy='public' on every visibility path (MediaRepository.php:1402), so the leaderboard inflates a user's PUBLIC score with their private/members-only uploads' reaction counts. (4) Economy integrity: BoostService::create() and StreakController::buy_freeze wrap the balance-check + deduction in if(function_exists('wbgam_*')) — if wb-gamification is absent the points are never checked or deducted but the boost row is still inserted and the media is promoted: free boosts. Boost feed promotion itself is privacy-safe (array_intersect against already-visible feed IDs).

ux.notes: Surfaces enumerated: 8 blocks (pro-battle, pro-battles-active, pro-challenge, pro-challenges-list, pro-tournament, pro-tournaments-list, pro-leaderboard, pro-compete-hub), matching shortcodes ([mvs_pro_leaderboard] etc. via Shortcodes.php + CompeteHubRenderer), 4 page templates via rewrites (/media/battles|challenges|tournaments + /compete/), deep-link item pages (/media/challenges/{id}/), dashboard Compete tabs + panels (My Media), Explore pinned banner, streak badge on usernames, admin GamificationSettings + ChallengeManager/TournamentManager/BattleMonitor. Discoverability after the a9da475 nav-injection removal is COHERENT: dashboard tabs (gated per-toggle, logged-in only) and Explore banner replace the menu link, and the loss is intentional/documented. Empty states are good for the compete-hub block (admin-only notice, blank for visitors) and leaderboard. GAPS: (1) leaderboard 'Gamification XP' source is offered in the block editor with no hint it needs wb-gamification — pick it without the plugin and you get a silently-empty list showing the WRONG copy ('get some reactions on your uploads!'). (2) Explore banner + active-summary endpoint query the competitions table with NO feature-toggle gate, so a disabled-but-still-active competition surfaces a banner linking to /media/challenges/ which the loader then 404s — a dead end. (3) Admin settings never warn that the whole points economy is inert without wb-gamification. (4) Fresh-install default mismatch ('1' loader vs '0' everywhere) yields a broken page before any settings are saved. Mobile/390px: gamification.css + per-block style.css are separate stylesheets; the compete-banner is a flex row with label/title/meta/actions/dismiss — flag as a wrap/overflow risk at 390px (not browser-verified).

findings.title: Leaderboard leaks private/members-only media into public ranking
findings.customer_impact: A creator's private and members-only uploads' reaction counts (and upload counts) are summed into their PUBLIC leaderboard score, visible to anyone — logged out included — via the pro-leaderboard block/shortcode. This is the same members-level privacy leak the team just fixed on BP tabs and activity. Add AND privacy='public' to both the reactions and media_count queries (Free's MediaRepository already gates this way).

findings.title: Boosts and streak-freeze give free spend when wb-gamification is absent
findings.customer_impact: The entire points economy is wrapped in if(function_exists('wbgam_*')). With Boosts enabled but wb-gamification not installed, create() skips the balance check AND the deduction but still inserts the boost and promotes the media to the top of Explore — boosts are free and unlimited. Same shape for streak freeze. Either hard-require wb-gamification (block boost creation with an actionable error) or make the dependency explicit; today it silently degrades to a broken economy.

findings.title: Gamification page templates default ON while controllers/services default OFF — broken pages on fresh install
findings.customer_impact: The per-page gate defaults the toggle to '1' (get_option($key,'1')) while every controller, service, dashboard tab and banner defaults to '0'. On a fresh install before any settings are saved, /media/challenges/, /media/battles/ and /media/tournaments/ render their templates, but the matching REST controllers were never registered (they require the toggle === '1', default '0'), so the page's Interactivity store fetch returns 404 and the page is dead. Change the loader default to '0' so the page state matches the service state.

findings.title: Competition entries are never cleaned up when their media is deleted
findings.customer_impact: The only mvs_media_deleted listener purges collections; there is no listener for any gamification table. Delete a photo that is a live challenge/battle/tournament entry and the entry row, its vote_count, and (for battles) its match outcome all persist with a dangling media_id. A deleted photo can still win a battle or rank in a challenge; thumbnails just render blank. Add an mvs_media_deleted handler that voids/removes affected mvs_competition_entries (and recomputes match outcomes).

findings.title: No user-deletion cleanup for any gamification data
findings.customer_impact: When a WordPress user is deleted, their challenge entries, battle participations, tournament registrations, boosts, streak meta and freeze tokens are orphaned. Battle/tournament queries that JOIN entries by user_id will show 'Unknown' opponents (CompeteSummaryController already falls back to 'Unknown'), but vote tallies and brackets referencing the ghost user stay live. Register a deleted_user handler to purge or anonymize gamification rows.

findings.title: active-summary response shape does not match its declared schema
findings.customer_impact: get_public_item_schema() declares my_activity as {activeBattles, challengeEntries, tournamentRegistrations} integers, but get_my_activity() returns {battles, challenges, tournaments} arrays of objects. Any consumer relying on the published schema (or wp-json self-discovery) gets wrong field names and types. Correct the schema to match the actual payload.

findings.title: Explore banner and active-summary are not feature-toggle gated — dead-end links
findings.customer_impact: render_explore_compete_banner() and CompeteSummaryController query mvs_competitions directly with no mvs_*_enabled check. If an admin turns a feature OFF but an 'active' row remains, the banner still renders and links to /media/challenges/ (or /tournaments/), which GamificationTemplateLoader then 404s because it IS toggle-gated. Customer clicks a promoted competition and lands on a 404. Gate these surfaces on the same toggles the loader uses.

findings.title: Leaderboard 'Gamification XP' source is a silent dead-end without wb-gamification
findings.customer_impact: The block editor offers 'Gamification XP' as a leaderboard source with no note that it requires wb-gamification. Selected without that plugin, fetch_leaders returns [] and the front end shows the reactions-flavored empty copy 'No leaders to display yet — get some reactions on your uploads!' — wrong message, blank widget, no explanation. Disable/annotate the XP option when wb-gamification is inactive, and give the XP source its own empty-state copy.

findings.title: Admin gamification settings never surface the wb-gamification dependency
findings.customer_impact: Boosts, streak freezes and the XP leaderboard all depend on wb-gamification, but the settings screen has no detection or notice. An admin enables Boosts, sets a points price, and ships a feature that either does nothing or hands out free boosts (see other finding) with no warning. Add an admin notice in the Competitions section when wb-gamification is not active.

findings.title: buy-freeze REST route registers even when streaks are disabled
findings.customer_impact: StreakService correctly gates tracking on mvs_streaks_enabled, but the StreakController buy-freeze endpoint is registered unconditionally. With streaks turned off a user can still POST /streaks/buy-freeze and spend points for a freeze token that nothing consumes. Wrap the controller registration in the mvs_streaks_enabled check.

findings.title: Compete banner is a flat flex row — 390px wrap/overflow risk
findings.customer_impact: The pinned Explore banner renders label/title/meta + divider + a second item + actions + dismiss in one container. With both a challenge and a tournament active plus two CTA buttons, this is a lot of horizontal content; if gamification.css doesn't explicitly stack it at <=640px the banner will overflow or truncate on phones. Verify the 390px breakpoint stacks items vertically.

overcooked_items: Nothing is meaningfully over-engineered for the job. The one borderline item: GamificationTemplateLoader carries PAGES/ITEM_PAGES/TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES/PAGE_TITLES/BODY_CLASSES as five parallel const maps keyed by slug — for only 4 slugs this is more indirection than a small per-slug config array would need, but it is harmless and not worth churn.

The leaderboard 'source' abstraction (reactions / media_count / gamification_xp) is fine, but shipping the gamification_xp branch in the editor while the backing plugin is optional adds a configuration that buys most customers nothing — consider hiding it unless wb-gamification is active rather than keeping it as a dead selectable option.
missing_for_complete_solution: Privacy gate on the leaderboard so private/members media never inflates a public score (support will get 'why is X #1, those photos are private?').

A hard, visible wb-gamification dependency story: admin notice + boost/streak endpoints that refuse to run (or clearly state points are off) when the plugin is absent — otherwise tickets about 'boosts are free' or 'XP leaderboard is empty'.

mvs_media_deleted and deleted_user cleanup for mvs_competitions / mvs_competition_entries / mvs_competition_matches / mvs_boosts / streak meta — customers will report ghost entries, deleted-photo winners, and 'Unknown' opponents.
Consistent feature-toggle default ('0') in GamificationTemplateLoader so a fresh/never-saved install does not serve broken /media/* competition pages.
Toggle-gate the Explore banner + active-summary so disabling a feature actually removes its promo links instead of leaving 404 dead ends.
Correct the active-summary JSON schema so the documented API matches the response (developers integrating the compete-hub data will file this).
An XP-source-specific empty state and editor gating so the leaderboard never shows reactions copy for an empty XP board.

feature.name: Connectors & feed layouts (Flickr connector, Instagram/Flickr/Pinterest/Dribbble layouts, feed shortcodes/blocks)
feature.entry: Connectors/ (ConnectorManager, ConnectorRESTController, OAuthHelper), Integrations/Flickr/, Frontend/Layouts/ + LayoutManager, Blocks/Shortcodes.php feed shortcodes
feature.note: Load More on shortcode pages just fixed (d8a0447) — check the remaining interactivity (lightbox, filters) on those surfaces too.

audit.feature: Connectors & feed layouts (Flickr connector, Instagram/Flickr/Pinterest/Dribbble layouts, feed shortcodes/blocks) [Pro]
audit.verdict_reason: The Flickr connector and the four feed layouts are substantially built and mostly correct, but there are two customer-facing breakages of exactly the bug class this cycle is fighting. (1) BLOCKER privacy leak: InstagramLayout::render_feed() runs its own raw SQL with no privacy filter — private/members-only media is exposed to anonymous visitors on every Instagram feed surface, while the other three layouts gate correctly. (2) The d8a0447 Load More fix healed Load More on shortcode/block feed pages but missed the sibling interactivity on those same surfaces: the lightbox (mvs/shared-ui store + dialog frame) is never enqueued/rendered on non-MVS pages, so clicking any feed tile in a shortcode/block is a dead end. Plus two dead REST routes (export, sync) with no consumer. So: layouts are RIGHT-SIZED in ambition but HALF-COOKED on completeness (privacy + lightbox), and the connector API is slightly OVERCOOKED (9 routes, 2 unused).

api.notes: 9 connector routes under mvs-pro/v1/connectors. Permission model is sound: check_logged_in for list/connect, check_connected (logged-in + has stored token for that connector) for the rest. Input validation/sanitization is present and correct (absint, sanitize_text_field, rest_sanitize_boolean, array map sanitizers; per_page clamped to 30). OAuth callback in ConnectorManager::handle_oauth_callback intentionally skips nonce (external redirect) and that is acceptable, but it relies only on a per-user transient token match in the connector — reasonable. DEAD API: POST /connectors/{id}/export and POST /connectors/{id}/sync have NO frontend or admin consumer — JS only calls connect/disconnect/status/photos/albums/import. Export only ever runs via maybe_auto_export() calling export_item() directly (not the route); sync (delta) has no UI at all and the last_delta timestamp it writes is never surfaced. Response shapes for import/export are consistent and actionable. list_photos honors Pagination helper. No broken wiring found (every JS-called route exists). Minor: delta_sync reads media across the user's whole library via find_ids_by_meta with author_id filter — correct scoping.

dataflow.notes: Flickr import/export path is clean: dedup by external_id (find_by_meta), sideload through Free upload service, dual-write tags (taxonomy + repo meta JSON), external_source/external_id/external_url/external_synced_at persisted via set_many, mvs_media_imported/mvs_media_exported fired for extensibility. disconnect() clears all user meta + the mvs_flickr_valid_ transient (good — added 1.4.0). GAP: no cleanup of external_* meta or reverse-dedup on media DELETION — if an imported media row is deleted and re-imported the dedup still works (meta gone with row), so acceptable; but there is no hook to notify the remote or clear last_delta linkage. SECURITY (medium): OAuthHelper::encrypt/decrypt call wp_encrypt_cookie/wp_decrypt_cookie which are NOT WP core functions, so in practice every site uses the XOR-with-wp_salt fallback — reversible obfuscation, not encryption, for stored OAuth tokens (the docblock admits this). PRIVACY: Flickr/Pinterest/Dribbble feed-body all gate reads correctly (anon->public, logged-in non-mod->visible+own, mod->any) and route through MediaRepository::query build_privacy_where. Instagram does NOT (see findings). Caching follows cardinality rule (per-user transients are token-validation flags, guarded TTLs).

ux.notes: Surfaces: 4 feed shortcodes ([mvs_pro_{instagram,flickr,pinterest,dribbble}_feed]), 4 feed blocks (mvs/pro-*-feed render.php), the site-wide layout override (mvs_pro_feed_layout option via LayoutManager on Explore/profile/archive), profile templates, and the connector dashboard/settings JS surfaces. Load More: FIXED on shortcode/block pages by d8a0447 (layouts now enqueue the globally-registered mvs-load-more JS+CSS). BUT the same fix did NOT carry the lightbox: feed templates emit data-wp-on--click="actions.openLightbox" against Free's mvs/shared-ui store, which is only enqueued inside the is_mvs_page branch of Plugin.php (line ~1009) and is NOT registered globally; the lightbox dialog itself lives only in templates/partials/shared-ui-frame.php which render_shared_ui_frame() returns-early on for non-MVS pages / logged-out viewers (line ~1845). So tile click on a shortcode or block feed placed on an ordinary page does nothing — dead end, identical bug class to the one just fixed. Empty states present on all 4 layouts. Filters/search bar (explore-filters partial) enqueues mvs-explore-search (globally registered) + @mvs/explore-view module inline, so tag cloud + search work on shortcode pages. Mobile/390px: layouts are flex/masonry CSS with per-layout media queries; no obvious structural overflow risk flagged.

findings.title: Instagram feed layout has NO privacy filter — leaks private/members media to anonymous visitors
findings.customer_impact: Any private or members-only photo a user uploaded appears in the Instagram-style feed to logged-out strangers. The shortcode [mvs_pro_instagram_feed], the mvs/pro-instagram-feed block, and the site-wide 'instagram' layout on Explore all build a raw SQL query of WHERE status='publish' AND moderation_status='approved' with zero privacy clause, while the Flickr/Pinterest/Dribbble layouts correctly gate anon->public only. This is the exact members-level leak class the team fixed on BP tabs/activity — still live here. Must add the same viewer-based privacy gating (or route through MediaRepository::query with privacy/viewer_id) before release.

findings.title: Lightbox is dead on feed shortcode/block pages — same surface-miss as the Load More bug
findings.customer_impact: On an ordinary page hosting [mvs_pro_flickr_feed] (or the block), clicking any tile does nothing: the feed emits data-wp-on--click="actions.openLightbox" but Free's mvs/shared-ui store is only enqueued on MVS-native pages and is never registered globally, and the lightbox <dialog> shell (shared-ui-frame.php) is not printed on non-MVS pages for logged-out viewers. The d8a0447 fix made Load More work on these pages but left the lightbox broken — customers see a gallery whose images can't be opened. Fix mirrors the Load More fix: register @mvs/shared-ui globally + render the lightbox frame (or have FlickrLayout::enqueue_assets enqueue it and the feed print its own dialog) on shortcode/block surfaces.

findings.title: REST routes /connectors/{id}/export and /connectors/{id}/sync have no consumer (dead API)
findings.customer_impact: Two of the nine connector endpoints can never be invoked by a customer. Export to Flickr only happens silently via auto-export-on-upload; there is no button to push existing media, and the /export route is unreachable. Delta sync (/sync) has no UI anywhere — a customer who connects Flickr can never pull updated titles/tags/privacy back from Flickr, and the last_delta timestamp the route writes is never shown. Per Pro Coding Rule 6 (three entry points), sync is a HALF-COOKED feature: API exists, frontend + admin entry points missing. Either wire a 'Sync now' / 'Export selected' control or drop the unused routes.

findings.title: OAuth tokens stored with reversible XOR obfuscation, not encryption
findings.customer_impact: encrypt()/decrypt() branch on wp_encrypt_cookie/wp_decrypt_cookie, which are not WordPress core functions — so on every real site the fallback path runs: base64 of XOR-with-wp_salt('auth'). Anyone with DB read access plus the (well-known-location) wp salts can recover a user's Flickr access token. The docblock admits it is 'NOT cryptographically strong.' For a feature sold as a dependable connector, stored third-party credentials should use a real authenticated-encryption primitive (e.g. sodium_crypto_secretbox) keyed off a wp-config secret.

findings.title: Instagram feed export/import dedup discrepancy and global side-effect in loop
findings.customer_impact: The Instagram feed-card loop sets $GLOBALS['mvs_current_media'] per item and unsets it after — harmless for rendering, but it means the shared-ui frame's own is_mvs_tpl detection (which keys off that global) can never benefit from it because the global is gone by wp_footer. Minor; only matters once the lightbox-frame gap above is addressed. Worth tidying when the lightbox fix lands.

findings.title: Import 'skipped' detection does an extra repository round-trip with fragile logic
findings.customer_impact: import_photos() re-queries external_source and find_by_meta('external_id') after each import to decide imported-vs-skipped. import_item() already returns the existing media ID on dedup, so this second lookup is redundant and the (int)!== comparison can misclassify a freshly-imported item as imported when it was actually a dedup hit. Cosmetic (counts in the summary can be off by a few) but adds N extra DB calls per import batch. Simplify by having import_item() signal dedup directly.

overcooked_items: Two dead REST routes (/connectors/{id}/export, /connectors/{id}/sync) with no UI — either wire them or remove them; right now they are API surface a customer pays for but cannot reach.

Redundant post-import dedup re-query in import_photos() (lines 609-622) — import_item() already returns the existing ID on dedup; the extra external_source/find_by_meta lookups and brittle int comparison can be deleted.

The ConnectorInterface/ConnectorManager framework advertises 5 capability flags (import/export/albums/video/delta_sync) and a third-party mvs_connectors filter, but only Flickr ships and only import/albums/photos are actually wired to UI — the generic multi-connector abstraction buys the customer nothing today beyond the single Flickr integration.
missing_for_complete_solution: Privacy gating on the Instagram layout (blocker) — must match the other three layouts before this can ship.

Working lightbox on feed shortcode and block surfaces placed on ordinary pages (register @mvs/shared-ui globally + render the lightbox dialog frame there), so tiles are clickable everywhere the feed can be embedded.
A user-facing 'Sync from Flickr' control and a visible 'last synced' timestamp — otherwise delta sync is invisible and customers will ask why their Flickr edits don't reflect locally.
A manual 'Export selected media to Flickr' action (the /export route exists but is unreachable; today export is only silent auto-export-on-upload, which is surprising and undiscoverable).
Real encryption for stored OAuth tokens instead of XOR-with-salt obfuscation.
Connector coverage beyond Flickr — the UI/labels imply 'platform connectors' (plural) but only Flickr exists; customers will ask where Google Photos / Instagram import is.

feature.name: Cloud storage drivers (S3, BunnyCDN, R2, DO Spaces) + Storage Management UI
feature.entry: Integrations/AmazonS3 + BunnyCDN + CloudflareR2 + DigitalOceanSpaces StorageDrivers, Admin/CloudOpsManager.php, Core/ConnectionTester.php

audit.feature: Cloud storage drivers (S3, BunnyCDN, R2, DO Spaces) + Storage Management UI (Pro)
audit.verdict_reason: The four drivers, the Test-Connection flow, and the migrate/cleanup/"Migrate all" UI are wired end-to-end and well-factored (R2/DO correctly subclass S3, virtual- vs path-style addressing handled, privacy gate enforced at both query and service level, no dead routes). This is largely RIGHT-SIZED. The MIXED downgrade is driven by one HIGH count-correctness bug that makes the "still on this server" tile and migrate banner perpetually non-zero for any site with private media, plus a real cross-cloud download gap in the documented CLI migrate flow when buckets aren't public-read, plus an orphaned-bytes cost leak when the active driver is switched. None leak private media, but all three are things a paying customer will open a ticket about ("it says 12 files still local but Migrate all says done").

api.notes: No REST routes for this feature (deliberate). Surface is admin-ajax: 4 Test-Connection actions (mvs_pro_test_s3/bunny/r2/dospaces) + 1 chunked migrate (mvs_pro_cloud_migrate_chunk) + 2 admin-post handlers (migrate/cleanup). Every handler pairs a nonce check with a capability check: Test-Connection uses check_ajax_referer('mvs_pro_test_connection') + current_user_can('manage_mvs_settings'); migrate-chunk uses check_ajax_referer + current_user_can('manage_options'); admin-post handlers use check_admin_referer + current_user_can('manage_options'). All admin-ajax actions are wp_ajax_ only (no nopriv) so logged-out is correctly blocked. Documented Rule-A allowlist (admin-only, no headless consumers) is a legitimate reason not to migrate to REST. Every JS caller has a matching handler and vice-versa: admin.js binds .mvs-test-connection[data-action] to all 4 testers; admin-storage-mgmt.js binds [data-mvs-migrate-all] to the chunk action. No dead handler, no broken wiring. Minor: error responses from S3/Bunny store() collapse ret/HTTP detail to generic 'Failed to upload test file' — actionable enough but the underlying error_log line the customer can't see has the real cause.

dataflow.notes: Entry->service->repo path is clean and single-sourced: admin UI and CLI both call CloudOps::migrate_one / cleanup_local_one, candidate rows come from MediaRepository::query_public_cloud_candidates (privacy='public' enforced). Privacy gate is defense-in-depth: query-level WHERE privacy='public' AND a service-level guard in migrate_one that refuses non-public->cloud unless the mvs_cloudops_allow_non_public_to_cloud filter is set. file_url is rewritten on the index row after verified upload; cleanup verifies driver->exists() before deleting local bytes (fail-closed). Delete cleanup exists via StorageService::delete_everywhere (local + active driver). THREE gaps: (1) CloudOps::count_candidates()::needs_migration counts file_url LIKE 'http%/wp-content/uploads/%' with NO privacy filter, while the migrate set is public-only — private media is always local, so 'still_local' permanently over-counts; (2) delete_everywhere only deletes from local + the CURRENTLY-active driver, so bytes migrated to cloud A then driver switched to cloud B are never reclaimed (cost leak, orphaned objects); (3) no extensibility hook fires on the migrate/cleanup transition (only the resolve-driver and allow-non-public filters exist), so other integrations can't react to a media changing storage tier. Caching: status is a single global option (correct by cardinality rule — it's a job singleton, not per-entity). counts_by_service runs uncached COUNT/SUM per page load but is admin-only and bounded by service list.

ux.notes: Single surface: the Storage Management section inside Settings -> Storage tab (registered as a proper add_settings_section card alongside the 4 driver config cards, not a floating panel). This is the right and only place it belongs — no missing-surface problem here because cloud storage is an admin-only config feature, not a block/shortcode/BP-tab feature. Wired end-to-end: per-service overview table, 3 stat tiles, switch-service guard banner, Migrate-all (chunked AJAX + progress bar + stall guard), Move-next-N, Delete-next-N (mvsConfirm destructive modal, native-confirm fallback removed per rulebook). Empty/local state present (intro tells the customer to pick a driver). Test Connection present on each active driver's card. PROBLEM: because of the count bug, on any site with private media the 'still on this server' tile and the amber 'N files still on their previous location' banner show a number that 'Migrate all' can never drive to zero — the loop terminates (rows empty) and shows 'All media migrated' while the tile/banner still read e.g. 12. That contradiction is exactly the kind of thing that generates a support ticket. Mobile/390px: __stats and __action collapse to single column at 640px, but the __overview table is a fixed grid 1fr 120px 120px with no mobile override — at 390px it's tight (~280px of fixed columns + gaps) though not overflowing; flag as low structural risk.

findings.title: needs_migration / 'still on this server' count omits the privacy filter the migrate flow enforces
findings.customer_impact: On any site that has even one private/members/friends media item, the Storage Management 'still on this server' stat tile and the amber 'N files still on their previous location' banner show a count that never reaches zero. The migrate flow only moves public media (query_public_cloud_candidates filters privacy='public'), but count_candidates() counts every local-URL row regardless of privacy. After 'Migrate all' finishes the customer still sees 'still on this server: 12' and a warning banner — looks broken, generates a 'migration didn't work' ticket. on_cloud (total - needs_migration) is correspondingly understated.
findings.detail: Line 282 query: ...AND file_url LIKE 'http%/wp-content/uploads/%' with no AND privacy='public'. Compare query_public_cloud_candidates (MediaRepository.php:950) which DOES filter privacy='public'. The two should use the same predicate so the tile matches what the buttons process. Fix: add AND privacy='public' to the still_local count (and optionally show non_public separately, which the UI already does via the third tile).

findings.title: Cross-cloud / CLI download relies on bucket being public-read; fails for R2 raw host and private buckets
findings.customer_impact: The documented CLI flow `wp mvs migrate-storage` (cloud A -> cloud B) and `cloud-thumbs-backfill` pull the source object with an UNAUTHENTICATED GET of the public URL. For Cloudflare R2 with no public domain configured (the raw *.r2.cloudflarestorage.com host is never publicly readable) or any non-public-read bucket, the download silently returns false and migration reports 'download failed' for every file. The admin-UI migrate path is unaffected (source is always local), but a customer following the CLI docs to move between cloud providers hits a wall with no actionable cause beyond 'download failed'.
findings.detail: download() builds $this->url($path) (the public/CDN URL) and wp_safe_remote_get's it; the doc comment even concedes 'a signed-GET path is the 1.3.0 enhancement' but it never shipped. exists() uses a signed HEAD/Range so verification works, but the actual byte transfer does not. R2 driver inherits this download() unchanged, so R2-as-source is the most exposed (its API host is explicitly not public). Either implement a signed GET in download() or detect+error with a clear 'source bucket must be public-readable, or configure a public domain' message.

findings.title: delete_everywhere strands bytes on a previously-active cloud driver after a driver switch
findings.customer_impact: If a customer migrates media to cloud A, later switches the active driver to cloud B (or back to local), then deletes media, the bytes on cloud A are never removed — they accumulate as orphaned objects the customer keeps paying storage for and can't easily find. No UI surface lists or reclaims them.
findings.detail: delete_everywhere deletes from local + the single currently-active driver only. There is no record of which driver a given media's bytes actually live on (file_url host is the only hint, and it's overwritten on migrate). For a feature that explicitly supports 4 interchangeable backends and a 'switch service' flow, delete cleanup should either iterate all configured drivers or resolve the driver from the stored file_url host. Cost leak, not a data leak.

findings.title: Drivers log failures to error_log instead of the plugin LoggerService
findings.customer_impact: When an upload to S3/BunnyCDN fails after 3 retries, the only trace is in PHP's error_log, which the site owner usually can't see. The plugin ships a Log Viewer admin page (mvs_error_log table) but storage failures don't land there, so a customer whose migrations silently fail has no in-product way to discover why.
findings.detail: S3 StorageDriver.php:100 and BunnyCDN StorageDriver.php:113 call error_log() directly, violating Free Coding Rule 8 (use WP_Error or LoggerService, no silent failures). store() returns bool false to CloudOps, which records last_error only for the migrate verb's generic 'upload failed' — the per-attempt HTTP code / cURL error is lost to the customer. Route these through LoggerService so they appear in Log Viewer.

findings.title: No extensibility hook fires when a media changes storage tier
findings.customer_impact: Integrators (CDN cache purgers, custom backup tooling, audit logs) have no hook to react when a file is migrated to cloud or its local copy is cleaned up. Every other key transition in the plugin fires an mvs_* action; this one doesn't.
findings.detail: migrate_one returns status='migrated' and cleanup_local_one returns status='cleaned' but neither fires a do_action (e.g. mvs_media_migrated / mvs_media_local_cleaned with media_id + from/to driver). Only mvs_cloudops_allow_non_public_to_cloud (a gate filter) and mvs_storage_driver (resolution filter) exist. Additive, low effort.

findings.title: Per-service overview table has no mobile breakpoint
findings.customer_impact: On a phone (390px) the storage overview table keeps its fixed 1fr/120px/120px columns while the stat tiles and action rows correctly stack. It fits without horizontal overflow but the columns are cramped; on very long service labels plus a translated 'Active' pill it can get tight.
findings.detail: The 640px media block (admin.css:564) collapses __stats and __action but not __overview-head/__overview-row. Add a narrow-screen rule (e.g. stack to label + right-aligned count/size, or reduce the fixed columns) for parity with the rest of the panel.

findings.title: Migrate-all stall guard reports generic 'failed' that hides the real cause
findings.customer_impact: If the migrate loop makes no forward progress on a chunk (e.g. a persistent upload credential problem), the bar stops and shows 'Migration stopped on an error. See the last-run status above.' The last-run status only carries CloudOps' generic per-verb error ('upload failed' / 'verify failed'), so the customer still doesn't know it was, say, a bad secret key.
findings.detail: The lastError returned by ajax_migrate_chunk is the result['error'] string from migrate_one, which is intentionally coarse. Combined with the error_log-only driver logging (finding above), a failed migrate is hard to self-diagnose. Surface the driver's HTTP/cURL detail through the status last_error.

overcooked_items: Nothing meaningfully over-built. The R2/DO drivers correctly subclass S3 with minimal overrides (host + URI + public-URL) rather than duplicating the SigV4 machinery — this is the right amount of abstraction, not over-engineering. The ConnectionTester::round_trip() helper was extracted to share the upload-then-delete probe across providers (S3/Bunny still inline their own copy and could also use it, but that's de-duplication debt, not over-abstraction).

Minor: ConnectionTester still has bespoke test_s3/test_bunny methods that duplicate the round_trip() body instead of calling it (R2/DO already use the shared helper). Consolidating the two older testers onto round_trip() would remove ~30 duplicated lines — a simplify, not a complexity removal.
missing_for_complete_solution: Make the 'still on this server' / needs_migration count match the migrate flow's privacy='public' predicate so the tile and banner reach zero after a full migration (the #1 ticket-generator).
Signed-GET download for cross-cloud CLI migration, or a clear pre-flight error when the source bucket/host is not publicly readable (especially R2 without a public domain).
Reclaim bytes on a previously-active driver: either driver-iterating delete cleanup or a 'find orphaned cloud objects' tool, so switching services doesn't silently accumulate paid-for orphans.
Route driver upload/download failures through LoggerService so they appear in the Log Viewer admin page, and surface the underlying HTTP/cURL cause in the migrate-all 'failed' status.
An extensibility action on storage-tier transitions (mvs_media_migrated / mvs_media_local_cleaned) for CDN purge / backup / audit integrations.

Documented behaviour for non-public media on cloud: the UI says private media is 'kept here' and the code enforces it, but there's no in-product explanation of WHEN private media will ever move to cloud (the code comments reference a cloud-aware /serve that the changelog shows shipped in 1.4.0 via location-based serving) — the kept-here messaging may now be stale and should be reconciled with the 1.4.0 location-based serve.

feature.name: Migration importers (rtMedia, MediaPress, BuddyBoss) + migration admin
feature.entry: Integrations/RtMedia + MediaPress + BuddyBoss (Importer + MigrationAdmin), Integrations/AbstractBatchImporter.php, Admin/MigrationPage.php

audit.feature: Migration importers (rtMedia, MediaPress, BuddyBoss) + migration admin (Pro)
audit.verdict_reason: The feature is well-architected (clean abstract base classes, one MigrationAdmin per platform, AJAX-batched UI that survives pause/resume/refresh, idempotent media-row dedup via mvs_media_meta) and right-sized in its use of admin-ajax over REST.
