But two real, customer-visible defects undercut the "dependable" promise: (1) the BuddyBoss admin migration stops after the first non-empty source table, so documents and videos silently never import via the UI; (2) album de-duplication is broken in BOTH the CLI importers and the admin path because the existence check reads WP postmeta while the marker is written to mvs_media_meta — re-running creates duplicate albums every time. Media-item dedup, counts, and the activity-rewrite thumbnail wiring are correct. So: API axis right-sized, data-flow axis half-cooked (album dedup + multi-table stop), UX axis mostly complete with gaps.

api.notes: No REST routes — the feature deliberately uses two admin-ajax actions (mvs_migration_batch, mvs_migration_reset) registered in MigrationPage.php:65-66, plus three WP-CLI subcommands (import-rtmedia/import-mediapress/import-buddyboss). The CLAUDE.md and an inline comment (MigrationPage.php:61-64) justify NOT using REST: an admin-only utility with no headless/third-party consumer. That is the correct call — REST here would be overcooked. Both AJAX handlers are correctly gated: check_ajax_referer('mvs_migration') + current_user_can('manage_mvs_settings') on BOTH ajax_run_batch (MigrationPage.php:327-331) and ajax_reset_state (MigrationPage.php:374-378). Inputs sanitized: sanitize_key on source/bb_source, absint on offset/batch_size, explicit isset() check against the registered-platforms allowlist before dispatch (MigrationPage.php:340, 381) — an unknown source returns a clean 'Invalid source' error. Response shape is consistent (batch_imported/batch_skipped/batch_errors/next_offset/done + cumulative totals). No dead AJAX (both consumed by migration-page.js) and no orphan JS calls. One minor: error responses use bare English strings ('Permission denied.','Invalid source.') not i18n'd, and wp_send_json_error does not exit explicitly after the permission failure — execution continues, though the subsequent isset() guard happens to also send-and-exit, so it is not exploitable. batch_size from the client is absint'd but not clamped to an upper bound, so a crafted request could pass a very large batch_size; admin-only cap limits the blast radius.

dataflow.notes: Entry (admin card / CLI) -> MigrationAdmin.run_batch or Importer.run_source -> MediaRepository.insert + set_many (mvs_media_index + mvs_media_meta) -> ensure_stats_row + generate_thumbnails_for_import -> optional add_to_album (mvs_album_items). Media-item dedup is correct and idempotent: find_by_meta/count_by_meta read the same mvs_media_meta key the importer writes (rtmedia_id/mpp_id/bb_*_id). Media deletion cleanup is correct — MediaRepository delete and MediaListPage both purge mvs_album_items by media_id. The activity-rewrite thumbnail keys also align (resolve_imported_thumbnail strips _mvs_ prefix so _mvs_mpp_id->mpp_id, _mvs_bb_media_id->bb_media_id match what the importer wrote). BUT two structural defects: (A) ALBUM DEDUP IS BROKEN across all three platforms and both entry points — create_album_from_* checks existence via get_posts(meta_key=>'_mvs_rtmedia_album_id'/'_mvs_bb_album_id'/'_mvs_mpp_gallery_id') which reads WP POSTMETA, but writes the marker via $repo->set($album_id,'rtmedia_album_id'/...) which writes mvs_media_meta. The two stores never intersect, so the existence query always returns empty and every re-run creates a fresh duplicate album. (B) Imported mvs_album posts have no cleanup on Reset (Reset only clears progress state by design) and no cleanup on media deletion — orphan albums accumulate. (C) Caching follows the cardinality rule (per-platform state in one option key keyed by slug, ~3 keys total — acceptable). (D) Privacy: the importer maps source privacy onto mvs privacy correctly, but rewrite_rtmedia_activity bakes media into bp_activity.content; at render the shared enhance_activity_media_content path re-signs via broadcast-TTL URLs, which is the same members-level activity-leak class the team is already tracking — not migration-specific but inherited. (E) Extensibility: no do_action hooks fire on import of an item or completion of a migration, so third parties cannot react to imported media (e.g. re-index, notify).

ux.notes: Surfaces: exactly one admin page (WPMediaVerse -> Import Migration, MigrationPage::PAGE_SLUG) plus three WP-CLI subcommands. There is NO block/shortcode/BP-tab/dashboard surface — correct, migration is an admin-only one-time tool, so no cross-surface duplication risk here. The admin page is wired end-to-end: start/resume/pause/reset buttons -> migration-page.js -> mvs_migration_batch AJAX -> run_batch -> live progress bar + speed + ETA + status badge, persisted to an option so the page survives refresh/close. Empty/not-detected state is handled (inactive card + not_found_message per platform). Dry-run and skip-albums toggles are honored end-to-end. Reset routes through mvsConfirm and fails closed if absent (no native confirm). GAPS: (1) The BuddyBoss multi-table picker offers 'All', but with 'All' the admin import STOPS after the first non-empty table (done = count(items) < batch_size triggers at the first table's boundary) — documents and videos are silently never imported via the UI, while the CLI loops per-table correctly. A customer using 'All' gets a falsely-'Completed' badge with two-thirds of their media missing. (2) Album-dedup breakage (data-flow A) is user-visible: re-running or resuming produces duplicate albums. (3) The 'Imported' count uses count_by_meta which can exceed live 'Available' after source rows are deleted; Remaining is max(0,...)-guarded so it shows 0, but the card can read 'Available 100 / Imported 130' confusingly. Mobile/390px: migration.css drives multi-column .mvs-migration-stats and a button row in the card footer; with 3 stat columns + 3-4 action buttons + 2 checkbox labels + last-run text in one footer, 390px is a structural wrap risk worth verifying. No logged-out concern (admin page).

findings.title: BuddyBoss admin 'All' import stops after the first source table — documents and videos never import
findings.customer_impact: A customer migrating from BuddyBoss via the admin UI with the default 'All (photos + documents + videos)' option will see the import finish with a green 'Completed' badge but only their photos (first non-empty table) are actually imported. Documents and videos are silently dropped. The run_batch computes done = (count(items) < batch_size); when the active table's last partial batch returns fewer than batch_size rows it reports done=true and the JS stops, never advancing the global offset into bp_document/bp_video. The CLI importer does NOT have this bug (it loops run_source per table). Workaround exists (run each source separately from the dropdown, or use WP-CLI) but the default path quietly loses data.

findings.title: Album de-duplication is broken — existence check reads WP postmeta, marker written to mvs_media_meta (all 3 platforms, both CLI and admin)
findings.customer_impact: Re-running or resuming any migration creates duplicate MVS albums every time. create_album_from_rtmedia/_bb/_mpp_gallery check 'have I already made this album?' via get_posts(meta_key=>'_mvs_rtmedia_album_id') which queries WP postmeta, but the only place the album marker is written is $repo->set($album_id,'rtmedia_album_id',...) which writes the custom mvs_media_meta table — the two never meet, so the guard always misses. Same defect in MediaPress/MigrationAdmin.php:225-260, BuddyBoss/MigrationAdmin.php:384-438, and identically in RtMedia/MediaPress/BuddyBoss Importer.php. Customers who pause/resume (the explicitly-advertised safe workflow) or re-run after adding more source media end up with 2x, 3x duplicate albums. Fix: write the marker to postmeta too (update_post_meta with the same '_mvs_*' key) OR change the existence query to read mvs_media_meta via $repo->find_by_meta on a dedicated album key.

findings.title: Imported albums are never cleaned up on Reset or on media deletion (orphan accumulation)
findings.customer_impact: clear_state() (Reset) only deletes the progress option; it leaves every mvs_album post + mvs_album_items rows created by the run. Combined with the broken album dedup above, a customer who Resets and re-runs to 'start clean' accumulates orphaned/duplicate albums with no way to bulk-remove them from this screen. There is also no on-delete cleanup of the imported mvs_album posts themselves (only their item links are purged). A paying customer doing trial migrations will ask support how to undo a migration.

findings.title: No extensibility hooks fire on item import or migration completion
findings.customer_impact: After a media item is imported (run_batch / run_source) and after a platform migration completes, no do_action is fired. Sites that need to re-index search, recount user stats, send a notification, or trigger a CDN sync after a large migration have no hook to attach to — they must poll. For a 'complete, dependable' migration tool this is a discoverability/integration gap support will field ('how do I run X after import?'). Low code cost to add mvs_migration_item_imported / mvs_migration_completed.

findings.title: BuddyBoss 'Available vs Imported' counts can disagree and confuse
findings.customer_impact: count_total counts live source rows while count_imported counts mvs_media_meta dedup keys; after source rows are deleted (or after duplicate imports from the dedup bug) the card can show 'Imported' larger than 'Available'. Remaining is max(0)-guarded so it reads 0, but the side-by-side numbers look wrong to a customer and invite a support ticket. Cosmetic, but it erodes trust in a tool whose whole job is an accurate count.

findings.title: Migration card footer has structural mobile-wrap risk at 390px
findings.customer_impact: The available-platform card footer packs 3 stat columns, up to 4 action buttons (Start/Resume + Pause + Reset), 2 checkbox option labels, and a 'Last run' string into one row group. On a 390px admin viewport this is a real overflow/cramping risk. Per the project's mobile-at-390px definition-of-done this surface should be verified; flagging structurally since I did not browser-test.

findings.title: AJAX permission-denied response does not exit; error strings not i18n'd
findings.customer_impact: After the current_user_can() failure, wp_send_json_error() is called but execution is not explicitly halted (no wp_die/return on that branch); the subsequent isset() guard happens to send-and-exit so it is not currently exploitable, but it is fragile. Separately, 'Permission denied.' / 'Invalid source.' are raw English, unlike the rest of the page which is fully translatable. Minor robustness + i18n polish.

overcooked_items: Nothing materially overcooked. The abstract base classes (AbstractBatchImporter, AbstractMigrationAdmin) are justified at n=3 platforms by the project's own de-duplication rule and carry real shared logic (flag parsing, batch loop, state persistence, add_to_album) — keep them.

The AbstractBatchImporter.track_extras() generic int-accumulator + extras[] map is a small amount of speculative generality (only rtMedia uses extras) but it is cheap and harmless — not worth removing.
missing_for_complete_solution: Fix BuddyBoss admin 'All' so it advances through bp_document and bp_video instead of stopping at the first table (walk to the next table when the active table is exhausted, only report done after the LAST table).
Fix album de-duplication so the existence check and the marker write hit the same store (both CLI importers and all three MigrationAdmin classes) — otherwise re-run/resume produces duplicate albums.
An 'undo migration' / cleanup path (or at minimum: clean up imported mvs_album posts on Reset) so trial migrations are reversible without manual DB surgery.
Clamp the client-supplied batch_size to a sane maximum in ajax_run_batch.
Fire do_action hooks on item import and on migration completion for re-index/notify/CDN-sync integrations.
i18n the two AJAX error strings and verify the migration card at 390px.

feature.name: Licensing & updates (EDD), Pro settings shell
feature.entry: License/License.php, Core/LicenseManager.php, Admin/ProSettings.php

audit.feature: Licensing & updates (EDD), Pro settings shell
audit.verdict_reason: The Pro settings shell is RIGHT-SIZED and well-wired, but licensing is HALF-COOKED: License::is_valid()/get_tier() are read ONLY to choose which form the License tab shows - NO Pro feature is gated by license validity, so a customer with no/expired/refunded license keeps every Pro feature forever; and there are TWO competing activation surfaces (custom in-page License tab AND the EDD SDK Plugins-list overlay) that can show divergent state.

api.notes: Licensing uses no mvs/v1 REST routes; it calls wbcomdesigns.com via wp_remote_post with edd_action=activate_license/deactivate_license (LicenseManager.php L93-148), the correct EDD pattern. The only AJAX, wp_ajax_mvs_save_connector_prefs (ProSettings.php L63, L1706), checks nonce and is_user_logged_in and whitelists default_privacy/auto_export. The EDD SDK registers its own activate/deactivate/delete/update_tracking AJAX handlers (Handler.php L188-192) with their own nonces - a SECOND activation path. No dead routes, no broken wiring. Activation sends item_id 1660828 plus url and environment, never item_name; item_name_mismatch still mapped.

dataflow.notes: State lives in two SDK-owned options: wpmediaverse-pro_license_key and wpmediaverse-pro_license. LicenseManager writes both on activate (L117-118), deletes both on deactivate (L150-151); SDK reads the same names, so custom tab and SDK share storage. THREE gaps: (1) License::is_valid() (License.php L32) is computed but NEVER consumed to gate a feature - Plugin::init() (Plugin.php L84+) boots all Pro features with zero license check. (2) Activation force-writes the _allow_tracking consent flag (L120-126); deactivation deletes only key+status, leaving telemetry consent behind. (3) get_tier() maps price_id 1-4 to tiers (L69-77), surfaced as Plan but never gates anything. Expiry check strtotime($expires) < time() (L48) compares server-TZ string vs UTC. Shell secret-preservation filter (ProSettings.php L37-58) and constant-backed credential rendering (L1759-1776) are correct.

ux.notes: Shell coverage strong: Pro sections merge INTO existing Free sidebar items and add Video + Connected Accounts + License via mvs_settings_sections (ProSettings.php L72-133, LicenseManager.php L58-72). Free SettingsPage renderer (SettingsPage.php L460-498) dispatches do_action mvs_settings_render_license and does NOT wrap renderer sections in its own form, so the tab's self-contained forms work without double-form conflict. THREE rough edges: (1) DUPLICATE surfaces - EDD SDK adds a Manage License button on the Plugins row (Handlers/Plugin.php L80-87); only the in-page tab shows Plan/Expires. (2) FAILED activation: key input (LicenseManager.php L220) has no value attribute, wiping the typed key. (3) No renewal/expiry nag - a lapsed license flips is_valid() false silently. Account link uses store.wbcomdesigns.com (L227) while registry uses wbcomdesigns.com. No 390px risk.

findings.title: License validity gates NOTHING - Pro features run fully with no/expired/refunded license
findings.customer_impact: License::is_valid() is computed but never checked before booting any Pro feature. A site with no key, expired key, or refunded key keeps every Pro capability (quota, cloud storage, layouts, captions, transcoding, competitions, connectors) indefinitely. The plugin gives away exactly what it sells.

findings.title: Two competing license-activation surfaces that can show different state
findings.customer_impact: Customers can activate from the in-page License tab OR the EDD SDK Manage License overlay on the Plugins screen. Both write the same options, but only the in-page tab shows Plan and Expires, so the surfaces diverge and generate support tickets. Pick one canonical surface.

findings.title: Deactivation leaves telemetry-consent option set
findings.customer_impact: Activating force-writes the _allow_tracking consent flag; deactivating deletes only key+status, so consent persists. A customer who deactivates expects tracking to stop. Clear or set allowed:false on deactivate.

findings.title: Failed activation wipes the typed license key
findings.customer_impact: The key input has no value attribute, so after any failed activation the field comes back empty and the customer must paste the full 32-char key again. Re-populate with the submitted key on error.

findings.title: No renewal / expiry notice anywhere
findings.customer_impact: When a license expires, is_valid() flips false but nothing surfaces it - no banner, no warning, no visible change. The customer has no signal to renew until updates silently stop. Add a dismissible notice off get_data()['expires'].

findings.title: Account link host differs from the EDD store host used elsewhere
findings.customer_impact: The account link points at store.wbcomdesigns.com/your-account/ while activation and the registry use wbcomdesigns.com. The customer may land on the wrong account page. Make the host consistent.

findings.title: Expiry comparison mixes server-timezone string with UTC timestamp
findings.customer_impact: strtotime($expires) parses the date in server TZ and compares to time() (UTC), flipping is_valid() hours early/late on the expiry day. Harmless today but a real edge case once enforcement exists. Parse as GMT.

findings.title: Masked key returns the full key for short keys
findings.customer_impact: get_masked_key() returns the raw key unchanged when strlen < 8. Real EDD keys are 32 chars so this never triggers; the always-mask contract is not honored for a short/test key. Defensive only.

overcooked_items: License::get_tier() maps price_id 1-4 to starter/growth/agency/lifetime (License.php:69-77) and renders Plan: X, but no tier ever changes what the customer can do - cosmetic. Either gate on tier or just show the EDD item_name.

Two full activation/deactivation code paths (custom LicenseManager wp_remote_post flow + the EDD SDK AJAX handlers) maintain the same two options. The custom tab re-implements what the SDK overlay already does.
missing_for_complete_solution: Actual license enforcement: a single gate (is_valid() checked in Plugin::init() or around feature registration) so Pro degrades gracefully when missing/expired - today licensing is display-only.
A renewal/expiry admin notice so a lapsing/lapsed customer is told to renew before updates silently stop.
A single canonical license-management surface - decide between the in-page tab and the SDK overlay and suppress the other.
Telemetry consent revocation on deactivation (clear wpmediaverse-pro_license_key_allow_tracking).
Field repopulation + clearer recovery on failed activation.

verified.title: License validity gates NOTHING - Pro features run fully with no/expired/refunded license
verified.customer_impact: License::is_valid() is computed but never checked before booting any Pro feature. A site with no key, expired key, or refunded key keeps every Pro capability (quota, cloud storage, layouts, captions, transcoding, competitions, connectors) indefinitely. The plugin gives away exactly what it sells.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code. License::is_valid() (wpmediaverse-pro/includes/License/License.php:32) computes validity but its ONLY consumer is LicenseManager::render_license_section() (includes/Core/LicenseManager.php:160), where it merely toggles the Settings page between an "Active" status table and the activation form. The Pro boot path proves no feature gate exists: wpmediaverse-pro.php:224 hooks mvs_loaded → calls mvs_pro_check_requirements() (which checks ONLY Free-plugin presence + version, never license) → calls Plugin::init() (includes/Core/Plugin.php:84). Plugin::init() unconditionally instantiates every Pro feature — quota, cloud storage drivers, layouts, captions, transcoding, competitions, connectors, analytics, privacy, collections. Individual features are gated only by get_option('mvs_*_enabled'), never by license. I grepped all of includes/, templates/, build/, assets/ (PHP+JS) and the Free plugin: zero license checks anywhere outside the settings-UI render, no apply_filters license gate, no REST permission_callback license check. The Free plugin contains no references to Pro license validity either. Not documented as intentional — the License.php docblock says its purpose is 'so the rest of the Pro plugin can check license validity', i.e. the gate was meant to exist but was never wired; the audit FEATURE_AUDIT.md describes the class only as 'EDD license key UI'. MVS_PRO_LICENSE_BYPASS is a dev-only escape hatch, not the default mode. Customer impact materializes exactly as claimed: a site with no/expired/refunded key retains every Pro capability indefinitely. Severity 'high' is correct (not blocker): this is a revenue/licensing-enforcement gap, not a security/data-loss/crash defect.

verified.title: Two competing license-activation surfaces that can show different state
verified.customer_impact: Customers can activate from the in-page License tab OR the EDD SDK Manage License overlay on the Plugins screen. Both write the same options, but only the in-page tab shows Plan and Expires, so the surfaces diverge and generate support tickets. Pick one canonical surface.

verdict.reason:
The structural premise is real: there ARE two active license-activation surfaces sharing one backing store. (1) The in-page License tab — `LicenseManager::handle_license_form()` (wpmediaverse-pro/includes/Core/LicenseManager.php:78-154) writes `wpmediaverse-pro_license_key` + `wpmediaverse-pro_license`, rendered via the `mvs_settings_render_license` hook into Free's SettingsPage. (2) The bundled EDD SL SDK overlay — registered unconditionally at wpmediaverse-pro.php:46-60 (no `keyless` arg), whose `Handlers/Plugin::plugin_links()` (vendor/.../src/Handlers/Plugin.php:76-91) injects a "Manage License" button + modal on the Plugins screen, and whose `Licensing/License::ajax_activate()` (vendor/.../src/Licensing/License.php:152-153) writes the SAME two options via `get_key_option_name()`/`get_status_option_name()` (slug = `wpmediaverse-pro`, no custom `option_name`). So both surfaces are genuinely exposed at once.

BUT the finding's justification for HIGH severity is factually wrong on two counts:

1. "they can show DIFFERENT state / surfaces diverge" — false. Both read/write the identical `wpmediaverse-pro_license` stdClass (with `expires`, `price_id`, `item_name`). Activate on the overlay and the in-page tab (`License::is_valid()`/`get_data()`, includes/License/License.php:32-101) reads it correctly, and vice-versa. There is no divergent state — the data is shared and consistent. The SDK even saves the full license object via `save()` (vendor/.../License.php:323-324), the same shape the in-page tab stores.

2. "only the in-page tab shows Plan and Expires" — false on Expires. The SDK overlay surfaces expiry through `Licensing/Messages.php` + `Messenger.php` ("Your license key expires on %s", "expired on %s", "License key never expires."). The only genuine cosmetic delta is the in-page tab adds a discrete "Plan/tier" row (derived from `price_id`); the overlay does not show a tier label.

So what actually exists is benign UI redundancy (two front-ends for one shared, consistent option store), not "competing surfaces that show different state." The claimed customer impact — divergent state generating support tickets — does not materialize because the surfaces are fully interoperable and both display status + expiry. "Pick one canonical surface" is reasonable polish advice, but this is a low-severity UX cleanup note, not a high-severity state-divergence bug. Downgraded to low.
